Hyundai Motor's long-term partnership with Tate continues to support artistic innovation and expand public access to contemporary art, fostering meaningful dialogue and collaboration
– Hyundai Motor Company and Tate Modern announce the opening of

, a major new multisensory installation by artist and composer Tarek Atoui. Combining sculpture, performance, music, technology and social research, Atoui creates environments where sound is experienced not only through the ears, but through the whole body. For his Hyundai Commission, he has transformed Tate Modern’s Turbine Hall into an immersive sonic landscape comprising custom-built wind instruments, percussion, electronics and sculptural objects, woven together to make an orchestra which connects the earth and sky. Through participation and performance, this living environment will constantly evolve throughout the run of the commission.

marks the 11th annual Hyundai Commission and inaugurates the next decade of the Hyundai Motor and Tate partnership extending through 2036. Established in 2014, the partnership represents the longest initial commitment from a corporate partner in Tate's history, encompassing the Hyundai Commission and, since 2019, the Hyundai Tate Research Centre: Transnational.

Atoui's Hyundai Commission is the culmination of over two decades of experimentation, including collaborations with musicians, instrument-makers, engineers and researchers across Asia and Europe. Drawing on these projects, he reimagines shengs, Korean drums, Uzbek horns and custom-built electronic systems.

Hanging above the Turbine Hall ramp, a metal karnai (a ceremonial brass trumpet from Uzbekistan) is joined by two 3D-printed horns that echo and amplify the instrument’s elongated form. At the far end of the hall, drum skins, gongs, horns, stones and 20m long textiles are suspended among a network of bamboo and shengs (mouth organs from China and Southeast Asia), through which wind is channeled by a computer-controlled motor. In making the work, Atoui has responded to the extraordinary height, airflows and acoustic character of the Turbine Hall. Lithophone-like stones and warm lights invite visitors to sit, lie, gaze up, and attune themselves to the relationship between sound, materials, architecture and bodies. Drawing on the artist’s memories of gathering places, from vine-covered canopies to sheltered courtyards,
situates the Turbine Hall as a site for encounter and exchange.

Microphones embedded within the installation sample the sounds produced by the instruments and the bustling backdrop of the Turbine Hall, with custom software reworking and playing them back as layers of the composition. Foregrounding the importance of improvisation in Atoui's practice, these elements contribute to an ever-changing soundscape.

Throughout the six-month duration of the Hyundai Commission, the Turbine Hall will regularly become a site for live sound-based performances, where a network of musicians will 'plug into' Atoui's installation as a sound system. The program will platform both local and international musicians – from instrumentalists to electronic artists, collectives and labels – highlighting the work of Atoui's longstanding collaborators and fostering new connections.

Hyundai Commission: Tarek Atoui: Hold creates new forms of connection through sound, bringing together diverse cultures and communities. Through his multisensory and collaborative practice, Atoui invites meaningful exchange and collective reflection on our contemporary world.

The annual Hyundai Commission has attracted over 21.6 million visitors and established a platform for some of the most bold and memorable artworks of the past decade – from Kara Walker's spectacular fountain to Anicka Yi's floating artificial lifeforms. By extending the partnership until 2036, Hyundai Motor and Tate reaffirm their shared, long-term commitment to artistic innovation and public access to contemporary art.

Which Newly Commissioned Works Does Ho Tzu Nyen Present in the Exhibition?
Hyundai Translocal Series: Ho Tzu Nyen
presents newly commissioned, site-specific works by Singapore-based artist Ho Tzu Nyen, whose work across film, video, performance, and multimedia installation investigates the
plurality of cultural identities across Southeast Asia

. Drawing on numerous Eastern and Western cultural references, Ho’s works blend mythical narratives and historical facts to mobilize different understandings of history, its writing, and its transmission.

(2026) is installed on screens in the museum’s OMA-designed, glass-front elevators looking onto the Bowery. When an elevator button is activated, a life-size child protagonist appears on screen and delivers a short text in the form of a mantra, question, riddle, or note reflecting on the nature of power.

Each time a visitor presses a floor button, an AI system generates a new image sequence in real time. Here, AI functions not simply as a tool for producing images, but as a generative structure through which narratives and identities remain open to change.

Presented in parallel with Ho’s commission for the Ulsan Art Museum, the exhibition connects New York and Ulsan through a shared conceptual framework while responding to the distinct architectural and cultural contexts of each site.
P for Power: Double Life of P
(2026) will open at the Ulsan Art Museum on October 22. Configured as an immersive installation using 24 projectors and a multichannel sound system,
P for Power: Double Life of P

(2026) incorporates data drawn from Ulsan’s industries, technologies, materials, and soundscapes. Together, the mutable nature of the two works connects to Ho’s longstanding engagement with histories and identities that resist singular or fixed definition. Across New York and Ulsan, the exhibition explores the multiple meanings of power, from political and technological systems to more fluid notions of endurance, transformation, and agency.

Ho Tzu Nyen (b. 1976, Singapore) is a Singapore-based artist and filmmaker. Working across film, video, performance, and multimedia installation, he investigates the plurality of cultural identities across Southeast Asia. Ho has held solo exhibitions at LUMA Arles (2025); Mudam, Luxembourg (2025); Hessel Museum, Annandale-on-Hudson (2024); Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (2024); Singapore Art Museum (2023); and Hammer Museum, Los Angeles (2022). His works are held in the collections of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York; Tate Modern, London; Guggenheim, New York and Abu Dhabi; M+ Museum, Hong Kong; MMCA, Seoul; Mori Art Museum, Tokyo; and Singapore Art Museum, among others. He is the Artistic Director of the 16th Gwangju Biennale (2026).

The New Museum is the only museum in New York City exclusively devoted to contemporary art. Founded in 1977, the New Museum is a center for exhibitions, information, and documentation about living artists from around the world. From its beginnings as a one-room office on Hudson Street, to the inauguration of its SANAA-designed flagship building in 2007, to the OMA-designed expansion of its home on the Bowery in 2026, the New Museum continues to be a place of experimentation and a hub of new art and new ideas.

Opened in January 2022, Ulsan Art Museum is the city's first public art museum, established in response to the long-standing cultural aspirations of its residents. Envisioned as a future-oriented museum grounded in digital technology, it serves as an open platform for experimental and innovative artistic discourse. Since its opening, the museum has presented exhibitions that cross the boundaries of traditional media—including painting, sculpture, new media, and installation—while engaging with key contemporary themes such as artificial intelligence, ecology, technology, and migration. Beyond its galleries, the museum offers a diverse artistic environment through facilities such as the XR Lab, a dedicated immersive space for media art; a research library providing specialized art publications and visual resources; and a multipurpose hall that hosts academic programs and interdisciplinary projects.

For over a decade, Hyundai Motor Company has deepened its partnerships with museums and cultural organizations worldwide, including Tate, the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the Korean Pavilion at the Venice Biennale. Hyundai Translocal Series is a new partnership initiative that roots itself in fostering dialogues and collaborations among art institutions in Korea and across the globe. Hyundai Motor’s own art initiatives include open call programs such as the VH AWARD, the Hyundai Blue Prize+, and Artlab Editorial, a digital platform dedicated to art writing by transnational voices. These ongoing collaborations embrace the complexities of the cultural landscape by exploring new ideas and perspectives within and beyond the art ecosystem.

The BMW iX4 M60 xDrive has M Sport seats with ten-way electric adjustment as standard. The M Sport seats can also be ordered as an option for the other model variants, as can the multifunction seats.

The elegantly sporty seats fitted as standard in the new BMW iX4 offer excellent comfort and secure lateral support. They come with electric adjustment, a memory function and the Travel & Comfort System. The rear seat backrest of the BMW iX4 splits 40:20:40. Seat heating can be specified for the rear seats as an option.

The new BMW iX4 is fitted as standard with a hi-fi system with seven speakers and a system output of 205 watts. The BMW iX4 M60 xDrive has the Harman Kardon hi-fi system with 13 speakers and 430 watts as standard. It enables use of Dolby Atmos and can be ordered as an option for all other models.
New BMW iX4 launches with two drive system variants.
The fundamentally new sixth-generation (Gen6) BMW eDrive technology is a standout innovation of the Neue Klasse and a defining component of the new BMW iX4.

Playing an essential role in this technological leap forward are all-new high-voltage batteries with cylindrical cells, 800V technology and further developed, highly efficient electric motors. Gen6 brings the BMW iX4 even more dynamic performance, up to 400 kW DC charging, significantly higher range figures than models with Gen5 and bidirectional charging functionality.

Two drive system variants will initially be available for the new BMW iX4 from the start of orders. The BMW iX4 50 xDrive has one electric motor at the front axle and one at the rear axle, which work together to generate maximum output of 345 kW/469 hp and peak torque of 645 Nm (475 lb-ft). The sporty SUV coupé accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h (62 mph) in 4.9 seconds and reaches a top speed of 210 km/h (130 mph). Its high-voltage battery has a usable energy content of 108.7 kWh.
It offers an outstanding range of up to 828 kilometres (514 miles)
. The maximum charging rate of the new BMW iX4 50 xDrive is 400 kW, which means enough energy can be added in ten minutes of charging for another 387 kilometres (240 miles) of range

The BMW iX4 40 xDrive also has one electric motor on each axle. Together, they produce maximum output of 275 kW/374 hp and peak torque of 520 Nm (383 lb-ft). The BMW iX4 40 xDrive needs 5.6 seconds for the sprint from rest to 100 km/h (62 mph). Its maximum range is 638 kilometres (396 miles)
Setting new standards: the BMW iX4 M60 xDrive.

Shortly after the order books open for its two sister models, the range-topping BMW iX4 M60 xDrive will join the line-up: it can be ordered from January 2027. The M Performance model has an M-specific all-wheel-drive application and serves up smile-inducing performance. Developing 450 kW/612 hp
, this is the most powerful version of the new BMW iX4 and sprints from 0 to 100 km/h (62 mph) in 3.9 seconds
. The electronically limited top speed of the BMW iX4 M60 xDrive is 240 km/h (149 mph)
. The M Performance model has a maximum range of up to 777 kilometres (483 miles)
Heart of Joy brings a new dimension in driving pleasure.

The new BMW iX4 utilises previously untapped potential of electric mobility. Like all Neue Klasse models, this software-defined car has a newly developed electronics and software architecture. The Heart of Joy high-performance computer links up with the BMW Dynamic Performance Control Driving Stack to provide hugely effective drive system and driving dynamics control. The Heart of Joy works ten times faster than previous systems and reduces the number of control inputs required. This technological leap forward ensures extremely effortless, precise and composed driving characteristics.
Adaptive M suspension: turning up the dial for sportiness and comfort.

The new, flat high-voltage battery is the key to the extremely low centre of gravity of the new BMW iX4. Together with the almost perfectly balanced weight distribution and upgraded chassis technology, this paves the way for precise and agile handling. In addition, the long wheelbase provides outstanding directional stability.

Leading the way dynamically in the BMW iX4 line-up is the BMW iX4 M60 xDrive, which comes as standard with adaptive M suspension. This brings electronically controlled shock absorbers and sport steering with variable rack-and-pinion ratio – and enhances both sportiness and comfort. Adaptive M suspension is available as an option for all BMW iX4 models. The BMW iX4 M60 xDrive comes exclusively with an electronically controlled M locking differential at the rear axle. It also offers two M-exclusive My Modes – M Sport and M Sport Plus – that provide a particularly engaging and sporty driving experience.
Innovative assistance systems and active safety functions.

The new BMW iX4 is offered with an extensive array of standard and optional assistance systems. The application of advanced technology and increased use of artificial intelligence provide even greater safety and genuinely reduce the strain on the driver during partially automated driving and parking . BMW Symbiotic Drive ensures intuitive interaction between human behaviour and driver assistance. The Motorway Assistant enables hands-free driving up to 130 km/h (81 mph)

Munich. “The BMW F 450 R has everything that defines a true BMW naked bike: performance, precision, and pure riding pleasure. It is light, agile, and full of character. We have developed a motorcycle that inspires confidence from the outset while also generating a lot of excitement. With the F 450 R, we are bringing our decades-long naked bike tradition into a compact and especially accessible format.”
The new BMW F 450 R: A dynamic naked bike for the 48-hp class—developed for maximum riding pleasure and featuring iconic BMW design language.

The new BMW F 450 R for the 48-hp class was developed as a standalone naked bike within the BMW F 450 model family. The focus was on signature BMW riding pleasure, enabled by a carefully engineered chassis and geometry layout, rigorous weight optimization, and a powerful parallel-twin engine. Its design clearly follows the current design language of the high-performance S 1000 R naked bike and visually underscores its sporty ambitions.
Smooth and characterful parallel-twin engine with a 135-degree crankpin offset for dynamic riding pleasure.

At the heart of the new BMW F 450 R is the newly developed fuel-injected parallel-twin engine first used in the F 450 GS, together with a stainless-steel underfloor muffler. For use in the F 450 R, it has been specifically tuned for road riding and gives the motorcycle a particularly distinctive sound. With an output of 35 kW (48 hp) at 8,750 rpm and maximum torque of 43 Nm at 6,750 rpm, the new F 450 R delivers powerful acceleration and confident roll-on performance. As much as 80 percent of the available torque is already on tap at 3,000 rpm, providing strong propulsion from low engine speeds. High-tech materials and optimized internal friction make these performance figures possible from exactly 420 cc. This makes the engine one of the most compact and powerful units in the A2 parallel-twin segment. It not only meets the stringent Euro 5+ requirements, but is also particularly efficient, with fuel consumption of just 3.8 liters per 100 km. With its 14-liter fuel tank, the F 450 R achieves a range of more than 350 km. The service interval is the BMW Motorrad-standard 10,000 km.
Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) for a significant increase in operating and riding comfort.

The optional Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) engages the clutch according to engine speed, increasing comfort and control—especially in urban traffic, while maneuvering, and on winding country roads. In combination with Shift Assistant Pro, it enables riding and shifting without manual clutch operation; the clutch lever remains available for deliberate rider input.
Six-speed transmission and left-side secondary drive. Shift Assistant Pro for fast upshifts and downshifts without operating the clutch.

The six-speed transmission transfers torque to the left-side secondary drive via an X-ring chain. For rapid upshifts and downshifts without operating the clutch, the new F 450 R is equipped with Shift Assistant Pro in every equipment variant except the base model. It can be retrofitted to the base model.
ABS Pro, DBC, DTC, and MSR, plus the “Rain,” “Road,” and “Dynamic” riding modes as standard—delivering a high level of riding pleasure and safety.

The standard “Rain,” “Road,” and “Dynamic” riding modes allow riders to tailor the new BMW F 450 R to their individual preferences. ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control (DBC), Dynamic Traction Control (DTC), and engine drag torque control (MSR) are also standard.
Chassis with a tubular steel space frame for high rigidity, robustness, and riding precision. Naked bike-specific tuning and a short wheelbase for agile, playful turn-in behavior.

The new BMW F 450 R also uses the newly developed BMW F 450 GS chassis concept as its technical foundation, with a setup tailored specifically to road use. The tuning focused on easy handling, excellent accessibility, and direct feedback. The tubular frame is made of welded steel tubes and forged components, with the parallel-twin engine integrated as a load-bearing element.
Front wheel control via KYB upside-down telescopic fork and rear wheel control via an aluminum hollow-cast double-sided swingarm with a KYB central spring strut.
At the front, a torsionally rigid 43 mm KYB upside-down telescopic fork controls the wheel. On the so-called “Sport Suspension,” the fork offers adjustable rebound and compression damping.

At the rear, the wheel is guided by a closed, highly torsion-resistant yet lightweight hollow-cast aluminum double-sided swingarm. It is paired with a directly mounted KYB central spring strut with adjustable spring preload and rebound damping.
Wheels and tires designed for dynamic riding pleasure.
The new BMW F 450 R rides on lightweight yet robust cast-aluminum wheels. The
naked bike is fitted with tubeless tires measuring 110/70-17 at the front and 150/60-17 at the rear.
Powerful braking system combined with BMW Motorrad ABS Pro for safe braking, even when leaned over. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) and the dynamic brake light provide additional safety features.

At the front wheel of the new BMW F 450 R, a floating single-disc brake with a Brembo four-piston monobloc fixed caliper and a 310 mm brake disc provides confident and efficient deceleration. At the rear, a single-disc brake with a floating ByBre single-piston caliper and a 240 mm disc is used.

BMW Motorrad ABS Pro is standard on the new BMW F 450 R. The system enables ABS-assisted braking when leaned over, increasing safety in corners. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) enhances safety during braking in challenging situations by preventing unintended throttle application. The dynamic brake light effectively alerts following vehicles that the motorcycle ahead is slowing down.
Optimal ergonomics and equipment for comfortable, playfully agile riding enjoyment on the road.

A carefully engineered ergonomic triangle and a tapered aluminum handlebar positioned high and close to the rider provide an ideal riding position in all conditions. The bodywork and the 14-liter fuel tank beneath it are shaped for secure support and effective knee grip.

The new BMW F 450 R comes standard with a two-piece seat at a height of 790 mm, offering most riders an ideal balance of comfort and performance. Ergonomics can be customized with Original BMW Motorrad Accessories: the high Sport rider’s seat raises the seating position by 20 mm, while the low rider’s seat lowers it by 15 mm. The gearshift lever, footbrake lever, and side stand are made of forged aluminum. The passenger footpeg brackets are bolted to the rear frame—an exceptional feature in this vehicle class.
Reversible shift pattern for an extra dose of sportiness and a true racing feel.
For an extra dose of sportiness, the shift pattern can be reversed quickly and with minimal effort—ideal for occasional track outings.

Powerful LED headlight and LED lighting as standard. Connectivity with comprehensive information and functionality through a large, perfectly legible 6.5-inch TFT display. Practical USB-C port in the cockpit area.
The new BMW F 450 R comes standard with an LED headlight featuring bracket-shaped daytime running light LEDs. The turn indicators and taillight of the new F 450 R also use LED technology.

The standard 6.5-inch TFT display on the new BMW F 450 R offers a wide range of information, brilliant display quality, and intuitive operation at a premium level. The TFT display features the Pure Ride Screen. M Sport variants with Riding Modes Pro also offer three additional Sport screens with detailed information on DTC, braking force, and lean angle, as well as a lap timer function. Riders can also make phone calls, listen to music, and navigate conveniently while riding.

Frequently Asked Questions about the BMW F 450 R
What is the BMW F 450 R?
The BMW F 450 R is a new lightweight naked bike for the A2 licence class, with an output of 35 kW (48 hp) and a road-ready weight of 175 kg.
How much power does the BMW F 450 R deliver?
The two-cylinder in-line engine delivers 35 kW (48 hp) and develops a maximum torque of 43 Nm.
With fuel consumption of 3.8 l/100 km and a 14-litre fuel tank, the BMW F 450 R has a range of more than 350 km.
What is the Easy Ride Clutch?

In combination with BMW Shift Assistant Pro, the rider no longer needs to operate the clutch lever when moving off, stopping or changing gear. This is particularly practical in urban traffic with frequent stops. The clutch lever remains in place and can still be used when required.
What rider heights is the BMW F 450 R suitable for?

With three available seat heights of 775 mm (low seat), 790 mm (standard) and 810 mm (high seat), the BMW F 450 R can be adapted to suit riders of different heights. The slim contour below the seat also enables most riders to reach the ground very easily.
Which licence class was the BMW F 450 R developed for?
With an output of 35 kW (48 hp), the BMW F 450 R meets the requirements of the European A2 licence class.

The new BMW X5 adds another chapter to its story of success. The fifth generation of the BMW X5 impresses with technical innovations, a stunning new design and the integration of future-oriented technologies from the Neue Klasse. This underlines its exceptional status and reinforces its leading position in a segment that it originally established.
First model from the brand with

As the first Sports Activity Vehicle (SAV) from the brand and founding father of the eminently successful BMW X family, the trendsetting BMW X5 has been shaping the future in innovative style since its introduction in 1999. Embodying that very same aspiration, the new BMW X5 is the first model from the brand to come to market with a choice of five different drive system types.

In addition to variants with petrol or diesel combustion engines, including 48V mild hybrid technology, and plug-in hybrid models, the fifth generation of the successful model does not just encompass the first all-electric BMW iX5. The BMW iX5 Hydrogen is also set to celebrate its market launch – at a later stage – as the first hydrogen-powered BMW production vehicle. The powertrain encompasses the fuel cell system, in-car hydrogen storage with the new BMW Hydrogen Flat Storage technology and an innovative high-voltage battery. The third generation of the fuel cell system enables a particularly compact design within a high-performance, efficient drive system with a range of up to 750 kilometres (466 miles)

The new BMW iX5 – the first battery-electric BMW X5 – is launching with the sixth generation of BMW’s eDrive technology. This means longer ranges of up to 845 kilometres (525 miles) in the BMW iX5 60 xDrive, fast charging, 800V technology and practical bidirectional charging. This is thanks to new cylindrical cells with a height of 120 millimetres, installed in the high-voltage battery and in use for the first time in the new BMW iX5.

“With its imposing presence and flawless symbiosis of comfort and driving pleasure, the BMW X5 became a global bestseller,” says Dr. Joachim Post, Member of the Board of Management of BMW AG responsible for Development. “And now the latest generation also benefits from the technologies in the Neue Klasse and the widest possible range of drive systems. As a result, I’m sure the new BMW X5 will set the benchmark in its class once again and write the next chapter in its success story.”
New design: unmistakeable presence from every perspective.

The new BMW X5 also takes a major leap forward in terms of design. Viewed from any perspective, the clear, monolithic and powerful appearance of the car embodies the confident presence that underlines its leading position in the segment, becoming one of the key faces of the brand. This is in large part down to the effortless melding of classic SAV proportions with the forward-looking BMW design language of the Neue Klasse to produce a harmonious, distinct end result.

The next generation of the distinctive X exterior is characterised by the upright design of the front end, the vertically aligned BMW kidney Iconic Glow and the new “double-X” light icons, making their first appearance in a BMW. The clearly structured side view of the BMW X5 is particularly impressive, thanks in large part to the innovative door handles, the BMW Winglets. These combine progressive design with functional convenience: recessed handles requires the lightest of touches to open the electrically powered doors.

Naturally, all models offer broad scope for tailoring the design, including eleven exterior paint colours and a precisely curated wheel range that now boasts 23-inch rims. The new BMW X5 M60e xDrive creates visual highlights emphasising its role as the sporting flagship, while the M Sport package and the M Sport package Pro provide a range of distinctive features.

In addition, high-quality M Performance Parts are available for the BMW X5. Highlights of the range include striking exterior items such as the M Performance front splitter carbon fibre, M Performance roof spoiler black high-gloss, M Performance rear diffuser aramid and M Performance exterior mirror caps aramid. Also available are M Performance summer and winter complete wheels in 21- and 23-inch formats. The cabin can likewise be given an even sportier look with items such as the M Performance floor mats.
Spacious, natural and innovative: redesigned interior combines feel good atmosphere with digital user experience.

One glance at the redesigned interior immediately reveals the extremely high quality of the new BMW X5. The interior impresses with clear structures and uncluttered surfaces, producing a harmonious sense of space and calmly providing subtle support for classic BMW driver orientation.

The outstanding visual and haptic quality of the interior is also underlined by the new decorative surfaces constructed from materials such as slate and glass that generate an atmosphere of elemental sophistication. BMW is the first carmaker worldwide to offer slate as an optional decorative surface.

The BMW X5 incorporates core technologies from the Neue Klasse in the form of the new BMW Panoramic iDrive display and operating system, underpinned by BMW Operating System X. These include the Central Display in free-cut design, the BMW 3D Head-Up Display, the BMW Passenger Screen available as an optional extra in the BMW X5 for the first time, the BMW Panoramic Vision with a projection surface extending across the full width of the windscreen and the new multifunction steering wheel. This results in an all-encompassing digital user experience centred around both the driver and their passengers.

The BMW X5 combines fascinating new technologies with a genuinely feel-good interior atmosphere. This is expressed in the lighting animations provided by the ambient light strip, a central element that creates an inviting wrap-around effect from door to door to generate a harmonious atmosphere.
BMW X5 combines a high level of comfort with BMW typical driving dynamics and intelligent driver assistance systems.

As the sportiest SUV in its segment, the BMW X5 has long set standards in terms of driving dynamics – and the latest generation of the BMW X5 is equally impressive in its this respect. This is due in no small part to the adaptive suspension fitted as standard and axle load distribution close to 50:50. Optional extras include Adaptive Chassis Control, as well as the Adaptive Chassis Control Professional with roll stabilisation initially available for every all‑electric and plug‑in hybrid model. This system leads the way when it comes to blending BMW’s characteristic driving dynamics with maximum ride comfort.

BMW Symbiotic Drive provides intelligent support tailored to individual driving behaviour. The advanced Level 2 driver assistance systems and active safety functions are designed down to the smallest detail for seamless interaction between assistance and human driving. In the BMW iX5 models, and in the upcoming BMW iX5 Hydrogen, the Heart of Joy also enables a very special experience: BMW Soft-Stop, which executes the smoothest stopping action every provided by BMW.

The market launch of the first variants of the new BMW X5 is scheduled for late November 2026, with the all-electric and plug‑in hybrid versions to follow in early 2027. Production of the new models will ramp up some months ahead of this, with BMW Group Plant Spartanburg (USA) initiating series production of the fifth-generation BMW X5 in August 2026.

Plant Spartanburg has been producing the X5 ever since it was launched – founding a new market segment – in 1999. And now the facility is celebrating a new premiere: the new BMW iX5 will be the first all-electric vehicle to be manufactured there. The new factory for sixth-generation high-voltage batteries built for this model variant adjacent to BMW Group Plant Spartanburg requires no fossil fuels for normal operations. Airbus forecasts growing services market to double by 2045

– Airbus anticipates that total demand for aviation services will double from 2026 reaching an estimated value of more than US$420 billion by 2045. These services, which sustain the aviation sector’s robustness, will grow at a 3.8% compound annual growth rate (CAGR), supporting an increasing world aircraft fleet of 45,550 by 2045. Over the same 20 year period, passenger numbers will double to 10 billion.
This will lead to a cumulative need for 730,000 maintenance technicians, 660,000 pilots and 1,050,000 cabin crew, totalling more than 2.44 million additional skilled people.

Digital solutions and connectivity underpin all sectors of the services market supporting airlines to improve operational efficiency, reduce disruptions such as delays and cancellations, maintenance agility and real-time connectivity to meet passenger expectations for a seamless journey.
Airbus’ GSF outlines six key services segments:

(2045: US$217 billion, +3.7% CAGR) – Doubling in value driven by an increasing number of shop visits due to aging and growing global fleet. Material supply is significant reflecting demand for parts support and repair.

(2045: US$104 billion, +4.3% CAGR) – The addition of this new cluster includes inventory provision on time and on quality and engineering support to ensure continued airworthiness and aircraft reliability.
(2045: US$36 billion, +2.8% CAGR) – Covering light inspections to heavy checks and growing in line with the overall growing global fleet.
(2045: US$27 billion, +5.3% CAGR) – The fastest-growing market, this is expected to triple over the next two decades.
(2045: US$21 billion, +2.6% CAGR) – Upgrades of older aircraft through cabin retrofits and modern technology integration.
(2045: US$17 billion, +3.1% CAGR) – Addressing a massive new workforce requirement, the industry must intensify efforts to attract and train new talent.

As the global fleet doubles to more than 45,550 aircraft by 2045, we need to get ready. Airbus is expanding its role as an integral services partner to support our customers across the entire aircraft lifecycle. By integrating predictive operations, fleet modernisation, and advanced digital solutions, we are helping airlines ensure fleet availability, reliability, safety and long-term operational excellence,” highlights Cristina Aguilar Grieder, SVP Customer Services Commercial Aircraft at Airbus.

In the next 20 years, Europe & CIS, North America and China will remain the largest services markets in terms of total demand, while Asia (Asia-Pacific, China and South Asia) is projected to be the fastest growing. The Airbus GSF is aircraft agnostic, focusing on passenger jets with a capacity exceeding 100 seats and freighters with a payload capability above 10 tonnes.

With this deployment, Galp and Siemens are shaping the future of digitally optimized renewable hydrogen production on an industrial scale.

Central to the collaboration is Siemens' Hydrogen Performance Suite (HPS) – an advanced digital cockpit designed to continuously enhance renewable hydrogen plant operations. At its core lies a predictive Digital Process Twin: a high-fidelity model built on physics-based modeling that delivers operational insights via real-time optimization for faster and data-driven decision-making. To power the digital twin, Siemens deploys an integrated software stack for process modelling, data analytics and real-time visualization – translating complex plant data into clear, actionable insights for operators.

By seamlessly integrating the digital twin with live plant data and external sources, such as grid operators and energy markets, the HPS gives Galp’s operators end-to-end visibility of their facility. The result is smarter production scheduling, and optimized energy procurement. Siemens estimates that the HPS can deliver energy savings of up to 15 percent – a significant lever for both cost competitiveness and sustainability.

"GalpH2Park is a lighthouse for Europe's energy transition”, said Axel Lorenz, Executive Vice President Automation Process Industries at Siemens. “We are convinced that digital innovation is the key to making renewable hydrogen economically viable and accelerating the decarbonization of industry. Siemens is turning this ambition into industrial reality – at scale."

Powered by renewable electricity sourced through long-term supply agreements and Galp's own renewable generation capacity, the GalpH2Park plant is set to produce up to 15,000 tons of renewable hydrogen per year. This is expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 110,000 tons of CO₂ equivalent per year (Scope 1) – a meaningful contribution to Portugal's and Europe's decarbonization targets.

Siemens offers a comprehensive portfolio of digital and automation solutions for the hydrogen industry – spanning monitoring and control systems, industrial automation, digital twin, power protection and distribution, and drives. With a holistic approach that integrates electrification, advanced instrumentation, and state-of-the-art digital services, Siemens is actively accelerating industrial decarbonization and the global energy transition.

Lower Saxony Transport Authority (LNVG) and Greater Braunschweig Regional Association (RGB) award contract for 113 three-car Mireo Plus B battery trains, maintenance, and depots valued at over two billion euros
83 vehicles for Lower Saxony Transport Authority and an additional 30 trains for Greater Braunschweig Regional Association
Two new maintenance facilities in Lower Saxony, including long-term digital maintenance over 30 years and up to 100 future-proof jobs
Option for the procurement of an additional 132 trains

Siemens Mobility has received a major order from the Landesnahverkehrsgesellschaft Niedersachsen (LNVG) and the Regionalverband Großraum Braunschweig (RGB) for battery-powered regional trains. The order includes 113 three-car Mireo Plus B trains, an extensive 30-year service package, and the construction of two Rail Service Centers in Lower Saxony. The contract also includes options for up to 132 additional rail vehicles. The trains will enter passenger service starting at the end of 2031.

Michael Peter, President, Siemens Mobility: “With the world’s largest order for battery-powered trains, we are working alongside our partners in Lower Saxony to drive forward the decarbonisation of rail transport and demonstrate that sustainable mobility is already economically viable and scalable today. Our Mireo Plus B battery-powered trains offer emission-free operation, high availability and first-class passenger comfort. In combination with our digital service and maintenance concept, Railigent X, we are laying the foundations for efficient and reliable fleet operation throughout the vehicles’ 30-year life cycle. At the same time, we are investing in service and maintenance capacity as well as skilled local jobs. In this way, we are creating long-term added value for passengers, transport authorities and the region.”

With the proven Mireo Plus B, Siemens Mobility offers a tried-and-tested battery-electric platform for sustainable and economical regional transport on routes that are only partially electrified. The high-performance, three-car vehicles, valued at around 1.1 billion euros, enable emission-free operation without continuous overhead lines, reach speeds of up to 160 km/h, and make a significant contribution to the decarbonization of rail transport. The batteries are charged while traveling under overhead lines and subsequently enable emission-free operation on route sections without catenary wires.

The 113 three-car, battery-electric Mireo Plus B trains offer an exceptionally high level of accessibility and passenger comfort. Due to doors with different levels of entry height, level boarding and a comfortable entry at different platform heights is mostly possible. Two wheelchair spaces, spacious multi-purpose areas, as well as modern passenger information systems and Wi-Fi ensure a pleasant journey for all passengers. Furthermore, the trains features more than 170 seats, including at least six seats in 1st class. For bicycle transport, there are at least six storage spaces per train, which can be expanded to up to 18 spaces if required.
30-Year service contract and two new rail service centers

In addition to vehicle delivery, the contract includes comprehensive customer service provisions. For long-term and reliable operation of the fleet, the contract relies on Siemens Mobility's comprehensive operations and maintenance concept, Railigent X. The core of the project is a 30-year full-service contract for the 113 battery-electric Mireo Plus B trains. Siemens Mobility will assume full maintenance of the vehicles and support a near-hundred-percent operational availability. The service package includes modern digital services for condition-based maintenance and fleet performance optimization, comprehensive asset management, supply of spare parts, and maintenance services throughout the entire lifecycle of the trains. Additionally, training programs for operations and maintenance personnel ensure that reliable expertise is built up and that efficient and resource-saving operation is guaranteed.

For the Lower Saxony BEMU project, a modern maintenance infrastructure for the battery-electric vehicles is planned. This involves a workshop concept that encompasses both operational running maintenance of the vehicles and the centralization of overhauls and heavy maintenance work in a center of competence. This is complemented by additional local facilities for regional vehicle care. Up to 100 future-proof jobs will be created. The concept combines high fleet availability with economical operational processes, therefore establishing the foundation for long-term reliable and sustainable rail transport in Lower Saxony.

Microsoft to expand Azure Maia system to multi-gigawatt deployments
Scott Guthrie - Executive Vice President, Cloud + AI
Azure Maia 200 now in production; Azure Maia 300 coming in 2027

As we move into the era of Super Intelligence, Microsoft is entering a new phase of infrastructure. We will scale our Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia the primary inference system for Microsoft products and services.
The multigenerational Azure Maia program has become a foundational element of Microsoft’s AI infrastructure strategy. Maia 200 is now serving Microsoft production workloads, including

Maia 300 is a complete intelligent system designed for the new types of AI workloads emerging today: Long-context reasoning, latency-sensitive conversational experiences and sustained, multi-step agentic tasks. By improving efficiency across the system, we expect Maia 300 to deliver

Maia 200: Driving the workloads that Microsoft runs at scale

The Azure Maia system is designed around the real-world workloads Microsoft runs at scale and the models we expect to build in the years ahead. Because silicon development takes years, our software and hardware teams collaborate early to anticipate architectures, scale and capabilities, translating those requirements into greater memory capacity, higher bandwidth and more accelerators operating as a single system.
That co-engineering is already delivering measurable efficiency gains. Maia 200 is deploying across the United States, Europe and Australia and delivering up to
for built-in AI capabilities in Microsoft Teams, Copilot and Cowork experiences compared with leading GPU infrastructure.

Experience running our AI models and services on Maia 200 directly informed the design of Maia 300. Together, the two generations are designed to support a broad set of additional Microsoft’s AI services: multi-step agentic work that will help GitHub deliver coding experiences more efficiently; cloud-scale model serving that will help Microsoft Foundry support diverse architectures and deployment environments; inference and data generation for the MAI team; and latency-sensitive interactions that will help Dragon Copilot scale workflows and reduce clinicians’ administrative burden.
Maia 300: Scaling more useful AI within every megawatt

AI is becoming a foundational layer of every application, workflow and business process. As enterprises move beyond chat experiences to systems of agents that can reason, act and collaborate, AI infrastructure must deliver intelligence securely and efficiently at scale while continuously adapting as models and workloads evolve.

As the third generation of our Azure Maia program, Maia 300 is designed with an inference-first architecture optimized for long-context, memory-intensive and decode-heavy AI workloads. This involves balancing compute, memory bandwidth, networking and power efficiency at cloud scale.
Key capabilities of the Maia 300 system include:
Less data movement, more useful compute:

Moving data efficiently, rather than raw compute power, is increasingly the bottleneck in large inference systems. Maia 300’s software-defined dataflow architecture and AI-assisted kernel optimization work together to maximize locality, reduce data movement and improve utilization across compute, memory and networking resources. By treating dataflow as a first-class design principle, Maia 300 delivers a significant performance-per-watt advantage over traditional GPU architectures.
Higher memory bandwidth within every watt:

As AI workloads become increasingly context and memory-bound, Maia 300 delivers industry-leading HBM bandwidth per watt. Eight HBM4 stacks provide 18.0 TB/s of peak memory bandwidth within a 950-watt TDP, enabling efficient execution of large models and long-context workloads. Specialized kernel support uses on-die SRAM as a software-managed scratchpad, reducing pressure on HBM.

A new multi-chiplet architecture separates compute, memory-controller and I/O functions, improving efficiency, scalability and cost structure. Compute chiplets are built on TSMC’s N2P process node to maximize performance-per-watt.

By designing for advanced low-precision formats, including enhanced MXFP4, Maia 300 reduces memory and bandwidth requirements for both computation and KV-cache storage. The result is larger context windows, higher throughput and improved model efficiency within the same power envelope.

Maia 300 treats networking as a seamless extension of the software-defined dataflow architecture. Rather than moving data through separate communication layers, dataflow operations span compute, memory and network resources as a single system. High-bandwidth interconnects between Maia accelerators are optimized for tensor parallelism, while a custom AI transport delivers performant and reliable scale-up communication across accelerators and racks. The AI-optimized transport leverages Ethernet-based networking infrastructure to enable a unified topology that scales efficiently from a single rack to datacenter-scale deployments.
Higher AI throughput from every rack:

Maia 300 rack systems bring together 96 accelerators within a 167-kilowatt power envelope, delivering 27.6 TB of HBM capacity and 1.7 PB/s of aggregate HBM bandwidth across a high-speed scale-up domain. That density allows Microsoft to serve more simultaneous AI interactions and larger workloads from each rack, improving datacenter capacity and the economics of expanding AI services.

Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO, and Ryan Roslansky,
Executive Vice President of LinkedIn and Microsoft 365
, shared the below communications with Microsoft and LinkedIn employees this morning.
After nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft, Ryan Roslansky has decided to leave Microsoft and embark on his next chapter.

As Ryan and I have been discussing our roadmap and work ahead, we felt this was the right moment for this change. Ryan will stay through the end of the calendar year as an advisor to me and will support on the transition.

Ryan leaves the organization in a strong position. With Copilot, we are executing rapidly against our vision to build a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task, with Office fully embedded in Copilot and vice versa! Over the past year, Ryan’s team has done critical work bringing together the product, engineering, and design foundations that have made this next phase possible. Last week’s launch was an important milestone in that journey, and the strong response from customers, partners, and the broader ecosystem reinforced both how far we’ve come and how much opportunity remains ahead.

At LinkedIn, we remain focused on our core vision of creating economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce, helping our 1.3 billion members access the knowledge, insights, and opportunities they need to navigate rapidly changing professional and labor markets.
Effective today we will make the following changes:
Sumit Chauhan and Lan Ye will report to Charles Lamanna.
Jon Friedman will report to Jacob Andreou.
Dan Shapero will continue as CEO of LinkedIn and Mohak Shroff will continue in his role, both reporting to me.

Over his nearly two decades at Microsoft, Ryan has helped shape how people around the world find opportunity, build their careers, and get their work done. I’ve always appreciated his clarity of thinking and I’m deeply grateful for everything Ryan has built, for the leaders and teams he has developed, and for his friendship and counsel.
Please join me in thanking Ryan for his extraordinary contributions to LinkedIn and Microsoft, and in wishing him the very best in what comes next.

In 1996, as a college freshman, I taught myself to code so a few friends and I could help other students find a place to live around campus. I didn’t know much. I did know the internet was about to change how people found things, and I wanted to be as close to that as possible.

In 2009, Jeff Weiner made me his first hire at LinkedIn. I’ve spent the nearly 18 years since working on a much bigger version of that same idea: helping people find opportunity, and then helping them do great work once they have it.
This has (obviously) been the best professional experience of my life.

As a product manager, I got to build dozens of features that are still around today (some good, some not so good!). When I became CEO in 2020, the world was months into a pandemic that changed what work even meant. Nobody hands you a playbook for that. This team wrote one anyway. Since then, LinkedIn has passed a billion members and nearly tripled its business, and every bit of that belongs to the people who built it.

Last year, Satya asked me to help build the future of M365. Once again, the old rules didn’t apply. AI was rapidly changing how professionals work, and the world’s largest productivity suite needed to lead the way. That meant figuring out what Copilot, and the future of work, should look like as one ecosystem.

We still have a ways to go, but the progress over the past year has been inspiring to watch. A lot of talented people set aside their own roadmaps to make that happen. Thank you. I know it wasn’t easy.

Satya, thank you. When LinkedIn joined Microsoft, you gave us room to build, and then trusted many of us with a lot more. I’ve learned more from you than I can fit in an email, and I’m grateful for the friendship that came with it.

All of which made this a hard decision. I know what it would take for me to lead the next phase of this work well: being in Redmond full time, every day. But my life and my family’s life are here in the Bay Area. My wife Leigh gives her time to more local organizations than I can keep track of. Our youngest daughter just started high school, and our dog Buddy remains deeply committed to the trails on the Peninsula!
I thought about this for a long time. It’s the right call. The work now goes to leaders who are set up to take it further. I can’t wait to see what they do with it.

Over the years, people have asked me what’s kept me so energized and motivated in this work. I think the answer is that I got to spend my career working where doing good and doing well are the same thing. In technology, that’s the best place to operate.

Most companies start by focusing on doing well, so doing good becomes a compromise. It’s the last slide of the PowerPoint, or a separate .org. But when doing good is built into the product itself, it becomes a real competitive advantage. When we build valuable products, people find jobs, they hire, they learn skills, they start companies, they run companies. That creates value for members, customers and the world. And for our business too.
Not many companies get to work this way, and not many people get the chance to build something like it. We do.

That matters more now than it ever has. Technology will continue to touch every job on the planet, and the people building it will decide what kind of world it helps create. I can’t think of a better group to figure that out than the people reading this note.
Thank you for the best 18 years I could have asked for.
New Microsoft data innovations unlock what only your business knows
Jessica Hawk - CVP, Azure Product Marketing

Every organization has knowledge that is uniquely its own: the way its business operates, the data it has built over time, the expertise of its people and the context behind thousands of everyday decisions.

As powerful AI models become more widely available, that unique business intelligence matters more than ever. The difference will come from how effectively organizations combine those models with the data, expertise and business context that make them unique.

Turning that intelligence into lasting advantage requires three elements to work together: human ambition to set the direction, intelligence grounded in the organization’s unique knowledge and trust to provide the foundation for operating at scale. Microsoft’s approach is designed to bring those elements together so organizations can build on what they know and create greater value over time.

That value can compound through a continuous learning loop, where AI draws on an organization’s data and expertise, improves the systems and experiences it creates and generates better outcomes over time without making the organization dependent on any single model provider.
European Microsoft Fabric + SQL Community Conference
in Barcelona, we are introducing advances across Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databases that help organizations put their data estate at the heart of a successful AI strategy.
Fabric IQ: Bring your unique business context into Microsoft Copilot

As Microsoft Copilot evolves across Home, Code and Autopilot, access to trusted business context becomes essential. Fabric IQ brings governed business context into Copilot, grounding experiences in the Power BI semantic models, metrics, relationships and business definitions organizations already trust.

With Fabric IQ in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Cowork now generally available, users can ask business questions and receive answers grounded in governed Power BI data, while Cowork can use those insights as part of broader multistep work. Integration with the new Code experience is coming through the Frontier program.

That means when someone asks Copilot for the latest sales forecast or another critical business metric, the answer can be grounded in the same semantic model that powers the organization’s reports, helping avoid confusion about which number is correct. For Power BI customers, this extends the semantic foundation they already have into Microsoft Copilot while preserving existing access controls and governance.

I experienced this myself recently as I was preparing for a sales review and asked Copilot, “What’s our latest sales forecast?” With Fabric IQ, that answer was grounded in the same governed Power BI semantic model that powers the team’s sales reporting, using the same business definitions and metrics my team already trusts. So, instead of spending the meeting uncovering and debating whose number was right, the team was able to get straight to what the numbers mean and focus on what we do next. That’s exactly the kind of experience we want to create.

For Fabric and Power BI customers, this capability is on by default in Copilot Chat and Cowork and extends the semantic foundation they already have into Microsoft Copilot while preserving existing access controls and governance.
IQ Sharing in Microsoft Fabric: Share unique business context without giving up control

Business knowledge does not stop at the boundary of a team or business unit. Organizations increasingly need to collaborate across customers, partners and broader ecosystems while maintaining control over the information they share.

IQ Sharing in Fabric, now in preview as part of Fabric IQ, breaks down company boundaries by enabling organizations to securely share data and the business context that gives it meaning, while maintaining governance over the underlying assets. Starting with key Fabric IQ artifacts and context, IQ Share is designed to evolve beyond preview to help customers discover, share and activate trusted context wherever it’s needed.
Together with OneLake mirroring and shortcuts, these investments create a more open foundation for sharing governed data and context across organizations, platforms and ecosystems.
Observability in Microsoft Fabric: Maintain visibility and control as AI scales
As organizations put more workloads on their unified data platform, they need to understand system health and address issues before they affect business and AI outcomes.

Observability in Fabric helps teams move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive operations. Cross-workspace monitoring and an enhanced Monitor Hub provide a unified view across jobs, capacities, workspaces and workloads, while Operations Agents and Activator help teams investigate issues, identify root causes with AI and automate responses.
Together, these capabilities help organizations maintain oversight as they scale data and AI.
Build applications directly on governed business data

AI is transforming how applications are created, but enterprises still need a secure, governed path from idea to production. Fabric Apps brings application development directly to governed data in Microsoft Fabric, helping organizations build and scale AI-powered business applications faster.

The Les Benjamins designer brought together Turkish heritage, 1970s rock ’n’ roll influences, and futurism for a landmark fashion show in Cappadocia shot on iPhone 18 Pro Max
“From Earth to Sky” celebrates 15 years of the Istanbul-based lifestyle brand Les Benjamins, bringing together Anatolian heritage, avant-garde design, and the magic of iPad Pro with Apple Pencil Pro.

Long before the sun rises in Cappadocia, Türkiye’s Rose Valley is already awake. Crews are on the move, models refresh their makeup, and three giant hot-air balloons — neon green, yellow, and pink — float above a landscape that looks like it belongs on Mars.

The scene is set for Les Benjamins designer Bünyamin Aydın’s most ambitious project yet. “From Earth to Sky” celebrates 15 years of the Istanbul-based lifestyle brand and brings together Anatolian heritage, avant-garde design, and the magic of iPad Pro with Apple Pencil Pro. Shot on iPhone 18 Pro Max by French filmmaker Neels Castillon, this fashion show is like no other.

The project began to take shape during a research trip to Cappadocia in early 2026. Aydın used iPad Pro and Apple Pencil Pro, alongside iPhone 17 Pro Max to record the extraordinary terrain, shooting photographs and 4K video at 60 fps.
Native flowers Bünyamin Aydın encountered in Cappadocia, Türkiye’s Rose Valley became the heart of his latest collection, inspiring 10 striking looks and three custom-built hot-air balloons.
Native flowers Bünyamin Aydın encountered in Cappadocia, Türkiye’s Rose Valley became the heart of his latest collection, inspiring 10 striking looks and three custom-built hot-air balloons.

Aydın’s creative process seldom takes place behind a desk, so he appreciates the flexibility iPad Pro offers with its thin, light form factor and battery life that can last him up to two days. “It’s the ultimate workstation on the go,” Aydın says. “That gives me freedom.”

Three native flowers he encountered in the region — spiky green Echinops, flutelike pink trumpets, and wild yellow tulips — became the heart of this latest collection, inspiring 10 striking looks and three custom-built hot-air balloons.

For Aydın, Les Benjamins represents the intersection of people and their cultures, and “From Earth to Sky” is no different. Born in Germany, the designer was raised with what he describes as “German discipline and Turkish heart” — a duality that runs through his work. “The canvas is the West; the paint is the East,” he says of a collection that combines contemporary silhouettes with Turkish fabrics and Silk Road influences.

iPad Pro with the powerful M5 chip became the creative nexus for the entire project. After research trips, Aydın would assemble photographs, fabric references, and early designs in the Freeform app, where evolving mood boards could be easily shared or exported to keep work ticking along. “Freeform allowed me to bring my team into my creative journey instead of simply giving them finished ideas,” he says.

The multitasking features on iPad Pro became integral as the workflows multiplied. Aydın could use its intuitive windowing system to work on an active sketch in Procreate, refer to photos from his travels, and research local flora in Safari, all while Background Tasks exported files for his collaborators.
iPad Pro with M5 became the project’s creative nexus, allowing Aydın (left) to assemble photographs, fabric references, and early designs in the Freeform app and share mood boards with his team.

And then there were the hot-air balloons. Working in Procreate, Aydın and his team designed a single structure as a starting point, then rapidly duplicated, altered, and redrew it until three final forms emerged from dozens of variations.

To bring the designs to life, Aydın collaborated with Pasha Balloons, one of Cappadocia’s hot-air balloon pioneers. “I would send my sketches to them, and they would use their engineering know-how to make sure they could actually fly,” he says with a smile. These technical drawings would then go straight back into Procreate for review and refinement.

Finding the right colors was vital. In addition to the electric hues of the balloons, Aydın also worked with cream, blue, and natural tones. “These are the colors of the earth and the sky,” he explains. The Ultra Retina XDR display on iPad Pro — which uses tandem OLED technology — became a key tool, while True Tone helped Aydın achieve the saturation he wanted, regardless of ambient lighting.

We were working on high‑resolution images, creating multiple layers and playing with textures. That’s usually when things start to slow down. But that never happened on iPad Pro. It felt just like working on a desktop.
Using iPad Pro and Apple Pencil Pro, Aydın designed the show’s colorful hot-air balloons in Procreate.

Apple Pencil Pro helped draw the line from idea to iterative design. “Working with regular pen and paper feels very natural, but the hover feature on Apple Pencil Pro lets me preview every stroke before I even make it, so I can see any mistakes beforehand,” he says. “It’s like a supernatural tool.”

An avid gamer, Aydın compares his relationship with Apple Pencil Pro to the muscle memory he developed while playing his favorite titles. Squeezing, double-tapping, and switching to the eraser now feel like reflexive actions, which enabled him to move quickly through variations without the tool interrupting the idea. And the low latency made the creative experience feel more immersive and responsive than ever.

“We were working on high-resolution images, creating multiple layers and playing with textures. That’s usually when things start to slow down,” he says. “But that never happened on iPad Pro. It felt just like working on a desktop.”
To bring the hot-air balloons to life, Aydın and his team collaborated with Pasha Balloons, one of Cappadocia’s ballooning pioneers.
“The canvas is the West; the paint is the East,” Aydın (right) says of a collection that combines contemporary silhouettes with Turkish fabrics and influences gathered along the Silk Road.
Back in Rose Valley, months of planning and work are finally coming to life.

Even before the sun touches the horizon, Castillon’s iPhone 18 Pro Max is already rolling. Three runways, gigantic hot-air balloons, and natural light that continues to change with every passing minute mean there is little room for error.

The new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture allows Castillon to begin filming in low light before narrowing the aperture as the sun comes up. Camera operators use Pro controls like histogram and white balance to keep the look consistent across multiple cameras as the sky changes from pink to blue.

Working with iPhone 18 Pro Max brings the immediacy Castillon loves as a director. “When I see something beautiful, I want to film it right away,” he says. The A20 Pro chip and improved thermal management also give the production the sustained performance and reliability it needs to capture heavy 4K video throughout the event.

Just as Aydın’s show travels from past to future, movement drives Castillon’s visual treatment. Custom-built drones each carry two iPhone 18 Pro Max models, with their 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide cameras focused on enhancing the sense of vertiginous speed while fitting the massive balloons into frame.

Footage captured at 4K 120 fps allows Castillon to highlight elements like rippling fabric in cinematic slow motion, while a slower shutter speed turns quick drone passes into a painterly impressionistic motion blur.
Aydın also worked with French filmmaker Neels Castillon, who captured footage of the new collection using iPhone 18 Pro Max.

Castillon’s treatment also creates a dreamlike, psychedelic look. He uses ProRes RAW to preserve flexibility for color grading in post-production, as Cappadocia’s pale hues meet saturated pinks, yellows, and greens. “I’m a huge nerd for color, and the tones are really accurate on iPad Pro,” he says.

While his team records video, Castillon shoots stills with the 48MP Fusion Main camera, using the new texture and grain controls in Photographic Styles 3 to bring some of the tactile character he loves in analog photography into the images.

As feeds from the whirling drones come into Castillon’s production control center, synchronizing them begins right there on location. He reviews footage and makes selections on MacBook Pro with M4 Max; its nano-texture display helps reduce glare from the sun overhead.

With the performance in full swing, Castillon’s focus switches from crane to drone to capture the opening look: a Turkish caftan and a tree branch representing Anatolia, an homage to Turkish rock icon Barış Manço. The show’s scale is huge, but Aydın believes its potential is larger still.

For him, “From Earth to Sky” is a chance to bring Turkish culture to a global audience without losing sight of its roots. “I see my role as that of a translator and a bridge between East and West,” Aydın says. “I hope this project makes Turkish people proud.”

Apple HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI and built with privacy and security at its core
Powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, Apple HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place.

, designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it. With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core.

HomeView recognizes users by their faces, adapting so they can access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My. HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses.

Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13.

“Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”

Through Sony Innovation Fund, Sony invests in startups and promotes business development and incubation with the aim of creating new businesses. At the CEATEC 2026, Sony will introduce its innovation support initiatives across the Sony Group, as well as companies that became independent from Sony Group with support from Sony Innovation Fund. Visitors will also be able to explore products and services from companies in which the Sony Innovation Fund has invested since its establishment in 2016. The exhibit highlights how ideas grow through co-creation and evolve into new businesses and sources of value.

It will also present examples of business development support through internal incubation and business co-creation, together with the background to the initiative's establishment and its activities to date.

Visa Direct Launches Stablecoin-Powered Money Movement as Pilots Move to Production

Inyo Global becomes the first enabler to bring Visa Direct's stablecoin-enabled prefunding into production, making stablecoin-powered money movement available for businesses that run cross-border payments through Visa Direct.

SAN FRANCISCO — Today, Visa (NYSE: V) announced the next phase of its stablecoin strategy as Visa Direct stablecoin capabilities advance from pilot stage to commercial deployment. The milestone marks an important step in bringing stablecoin-enabled money movement into real-world commercial operations. In the initial rollout, Inyo Global, a Visa Direct processor, is the first enabler of this new offering, powering it for eligible Visa Direct clients and partners.¹

Over the past year, Visa Direct has worked with clients and partners to explore how stablecoins can help improve the way businesses fund and move money across borders. As interest in faster, more flexible just-in-time funding solutions continues to grow, Visa is now seeing those efforts move beyond experimentation and into day-to-day business operations.

As part of this next phase, Visa is working with Inyo Global, a payments infrastructure provider serving money transmitters, fintechs, banks and payment businesses, to bring Visa Direct's stablecoin-enabled prefunding to market. Inyo has integrated the capability into its platform, giving the businesses it serves the option to prefund cross-border payouts through Visa Direct with USDC in near real time, rather than relying solely on traditional funding windows.²

Through a single connection, Inyo's platform lets businesses onboard users, manage fraud and compliance, accept payments and send domestic and international payouts across more than 180 countries, powered by Visa Direct.

"The next chapter for stablecoins is adoption," said Vira Platonova, Global Head of Visa Direct. "Over the last several years, we've worked with several partners and clients to explore how these technologies can improve money movement. We're now seeing those efforts translate into live implementations, helping businesses access more flexible and efficient ways to fund and move money globally through Visa Direct, starting with Inyo Global as our first enabler."
Visa Direct Head Vira Platonova will discuss how stablecoins are reshaping global money movement during several Money20/20 USA sessions next week.
The pilots demonstrated how stablecoins could support cross-border funding, liquidity management and global money movement for eligible clients.
Today, those capabilities are moving from pilot programs and into real-world commercial operations.
Inyo Global is the first enabler to bring Visa Direct's stablecoin prefunding capability into commercial production.

"Innovation in money movement is ultimately about creating a better experience for customers, and that's exactly our focus at Inyo," said Robson Dantas, Chief Product and Technology Officer and co-founder at Inyo Global. "By integrating Visa Direct's stablecoin-enabled prefunding into the Inyo platform, we're giving the money transmitters, fintechs and payment companies we serve a new way to fund their payouts, one that is available around the clock and runs through the same Inyo APIs they already use."

The implementation builds on Visa's broader efforts to connect traditional payment infrastructure with blockchain-enabled technologies. By offering stablecoin funding and moving money, Visa is helping clients explore new ways to improve efficiency while maintaining the reliability, security and scale of Visa's global network.

Visa’s work with Inyo Global reflects growing demand for stablecoin-powered solutions that can help businesses manage liquidity, fund payment activity and move money internationally with greater speed and flexibility. As adoption continues to accelerate, Visa is working with clients and partners to bring stablecoin-enabled capabilities to additional money movement use cases around the world.

Visa Expands Fan-First Strategy with New and Renewed Team Partnerships Across Pro Football
Visa’s portfolio of 13 team relationships brings fans closer to pro football culture in some of the sport’s most passionate markets

SAN FRANCISCO — Visa (NYSE: V), a global leader in digital payments, is building a fan-first pro football platform designed to connect more directly with fans, teams, communities, and culture. The company is announcing new partnerships with the Los Angeles Rams, Los Angeles Chargers, Kansas City Chiefs, Washington Commanders, Dallas Cowboys, Houston Texans, and Philadelphia Eagles, and long-term renewals with the San Francisco 49ers, New England Patriots, Buffalo Bills, and Pittsburgh Steelers, alongside current partnerships with the Chicago Bears and Baltimore Ravens.

By building a portfolio of team relationships, Visa is able to create deeper engagement where fandom is most personal: in local markets, communities, and shared experiences. Through these partnerships, Visa will engage fans through game-day experiences, community programs, athletes and creators, client activations, and innovative commerce experiences that bring fans closer to the teams they love.

As pro football drives commerce moments across travel, ticketing, dining, merchandise, and entertainment, Visa will help clients and merchants connect with fans and participate in those moments throughout the season through these team relationships. At every touchpoint, Visa’s trusted global network helps make those experiences more seamless, secure, and reliable — whether fans are buying game-day gear, grabbing food with friends, or traveling to cheer on their team.

“We are building partnerships that help Visa bring fans closer to the people and communities driving culture across music, gaming, entertainment, and, of course, sports. From pro football to the Olympic and Paralympic Games, to the FIFA World Cup™ to Red Bull Racing, these partnerships give us opportunities to engage with fans around the moments and experiences they care about most,” said Frank Cooper III, Chief Marketing Officer, Visa. “Our focus is on creating meaningful participation, not just visibility. These team relationships give us new ways to connect with fans through experiences, commerce, community, and the moments that make football one of the most influential cultural forces in America.”

Pro football is more than what happens on the field. It lives in neighborhoods, local businesses, rivalries, traditions, and communities across the country. Visa Data Shows Stablecoins Gaining Traction in Business Payments

New Visa data shows nearly 17%¹ of stablecoin-linked card volume is occurring across business and commercial card programs, underscoring growing adoption of stablecoins for settlement, treasury management and cross-border commerce.

SAN FRANCISCO AND MIAMI — Today, Visa (NYSE: V) shared new data showing the growing adoption of stablecoins across business payments and commercial card programs, underscoring how stablecoins are increasingly being used as financial infrastructure.
The findings come as businesses, financial institutions and payment providers increasingly explore stablecoins for settlement, treasury management, payouts and cross-border commerce.
Approximately 17% of stablecoin-linked card volume in FY26 year-to-date occurred across business and commercial card programs.
Visa today supports more than 160 stablecoin-linked card programs spanning consumer, business and commercial card activity. Payments volume across these programs has grown nearly 200% year over year.
Businesses are increasingly exploring stablecoins for settlement, treasury management, payouts and cross-border commerce.

"Businesses aren't looking for new payment technologies for the sake of innovation. They’re looking for trusted, reliable ways to move money," said Mark Nelsen, Global Head of Product, Commercial and Money Movement Solutions, Visa. "What's changing is that stablecoins are increasingly becoming part of the conversation around real business applications, from supplier payments and treasury operations to cross-border commerce."
The Shift from Trading to Payments
For years, stablecoins have been associated with trading activity within digital asset markets, helping users move between cryptocurrencies and transact on crypto exchanges.
Today, businesses are increasingly putting stablecoins to work for payments, treasury operations and liquidity management.

found that payments are now the fastest-growing stablecoin use case, with annual payments volume estimated between $401 billion and $527 billion. The largest business payment categories include service fees ($56 billion), payroll ($43 billion) and supplier payments ($28 billion).² Among the payment flows analyzed, B2B payments had the highest cross-border share, with 43% of volume occurring across borders.²

Visa is seeing that trend reflected across its own ecosystem. In FY26 year-to-date, approximately 17% of stablecoin-linked card volume occurred across business and commercial card programs, reflecting growing interest in stablecoins for settlement, treasury management and cross-border commerce.
Supporting the Next Generation of Money Movement

Visa continues to expand its stablecoin capabilities across settlement, money movement and payment acceptance. Through initiatives spanning stablecoin settlement, Visa Direct pre-funding and payouts, Visa is helping connect stablecoin innovation into real-world payment flows.
