Overseas sales to begin for the LY 680, first announced in 2024, with the yacht to be exhibited at the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show (October 28-November 1, 2026, Florida, U.S.A.)

Under the theme of "DISCOVER ESCAPISM," Lexus offers a new proposition that expands the possibilities of mobility, creating experiences that allow people to return to their true selves in a private sanctuary on the open sea.

The LY 680 went on sale in Japan in 2024, with the actual yacht making its world debut in March 2026. Now, approximately six months later, in September 2026, Lexus is expanding sales of the LY 680 to global markets.

The LY 680 is an evolution of the LY 650, Lexus' first luxury yacht, featuring a flybridge approximately 1,400 mm longer and a swimming platform extended by 700 mm, bringing its overall length to approximately 68 feet.

Mobility is not limited to land. People cross oceans and take to the skies, experiencing something at every stage of the journey. Across each of these experiences, Lexus seeks to create moments and spaces where those who appreciate true authenticity can simply be themselves.

At the Japan Mobility Show 2025 last October, Chief Branding Officer Simon Humphries spoke of a future in which Lexus is "not just about creating cars," extending its vision beyond land to "sea and air. In other words, 360 degrees of mobility."
Going back eight years to January 2017, as Toyota was advancing its transformation from a "car company" into a "mobility company," Toyota Marine and Lexus unveiled the Lexus Sport Yacht Concept.
The Lexus Sport Yacht Concept, unveiled in 2017
Approximately two years after the unveiling of the Lexus Sport Yacht Concept, the LY 650 was announced in 2019, expanding its vision of mobility to the sea.
Building on the Lexus Sport Yacht Concept, the LY 650 embodied Lexus' design philosophy in a new form―a 65-foot luxury yacht.

Akio Toyoda, Chairman of Toyota Motor Corporation (President at the time), commented, "The LY 650 symbolizes Lexus' efforts to go beyond automobiles as it strives to become a luxury lifestyle brand. I am truly looking forward to seeing the advanced, high-quality LY 650 grace the waters around the world with its beautiful presence. As a mobility company, we will continue to explore new possibilities on the water as well."

As a pioneer in delivering new mobility experiences, the LY 680 embodies Lexus itself as the brand continues to evolve with greater freedom at the heart of luxury, under the theme "Discover Escapism."

Out on the water, free from traffic lights, congestion, and the eyes of others, the LY 680 creates the ultimate private sanctuary―a secluded retreat from the demands of everyday life, where those who appreciate authenticity can simply be themselves.
Go Hayashi, Deputy General Manager of the Marine Business Division, explains the significance of the LY 680's global expansion:

"The LY 680 brings the values Lexus has cultivated to the sea, embodying a new future of mobility that seamlessly connects land, sea, and air. With the vast ocean as its stage, it creates an exceptional private space where family and friends can share precious time together, offering experiences that leave a lasting impression. Through these experiences, we aim to enrich our customers' lives and broaden the possibilities of the Lexus brand around the world."
The LY 680 features an exterior that embodies L-finesse, the Lexus design philosophy, complemented by comfortable onboard spaces crafted with careful attention to every detail.
In terms of performance, the LY 680 delivers the refined yet deeply engaging cruising experience Lexus strives for, combining stable handling with exceptional ride comfort and quietness.
A Dream Team Collaboration with Horizon Group
Lexus is not taking on this challenge alone. Rather than developing marine mobility entirely in-house, Lexus sought to bring its vision to life by collaborating with world-class partners.
The LY 680 is produced by Horizon Group, one of Asia's leading brands in the luxury yacht market, renowned for its custom-built yachts, advanced technical expertise, and production capabilities.

Lexus is responsible for the design and creation of the overall experience, while Horizon Group contributes the craftsmanship and production expertise it has developed through years of building large yachts.
The LY 680 was born from the combination of these capabilities, together with yacht production methods adapted from the Toyota Production System (TPS), drawing on the strengths of both brands.
John Lu, CEO of Horizon Group, shares his thoughts on the LY 680's global expansion:

"We are deeply honored to have been chosen as a partner of Lexus. If asked what Horizon's core value is, I would say it is not our facilities or assets, but our people. The opportunity to bring our products to customers around the world is a source of pride not only for Horizon, but also for Taiwan, and we are very excited about what lies ahead."

The Impressionist Artist Monet and Ukiyo-e: The Beauty of Japan That Captivated Monet

One of the key sources of inspiration that broadened the world of Monet's art was ukiyo-e prints from Japan. The unique compositions, views of nature, and aesthetics created by Hokusai, Hiroshige, Utamaro, and others offered Monet new perspectives in his ongoing exploration of changes in light and nature, enriching the breadth of expression in Impressionism. This exhibition allows visitors to experience art unbound, presenting the dialogue between Monet's works and Japanese art. It takes Impressionist paintings outside their frames to fill the entire space in a fusion of imagery, music, architecture, and sound. Rather than merely looking at the art, visitors can experience a new viewpoint born from the encounter between Japanese and European art as they wander through this world.
Monet's dining room: the ukiyo-e space that entranced Monet

Monet lived in his house at Giverny from 1883 until the end of his life. The dining room, a space that grew to symbolize that house, was decorated with prints by Hokusai, Hiroshige, and Utamaro that Monet treasured. The venue showcases a space inspired by that room.

Toyota Announces New Exhibition at the Toyota Kaikan Museum
"TOYOTA's Creative Carmaking" presents Toyota's pursuit of ever-better cars guided by the founding principle of "for the benefit of others"
Toyota City, Japan―June 1, 2026―Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC) has added a new exhibition space to the Toyota Kaikan Museum,

a corporate exhibition hall located in Toyota City. Titled "TOYOTA's Creative Carmaking," the new section will open to the public on Friday, June 5. The immersive exhibits feature real vehicles and visual displays that guide visitors through each stage of Toyota's long-established carmaking process, from vehicle planning and development to procurement, production, and customer delivery.

The Toyota Kaikan Museum was established in 1977 to commemorate TMC's 40th anniversary. The museum showcases Toyota's corporate philosophy and latest automotive technologies. It has received over 17 million visitors, including those who visited Toyota Hall, its predecessor, which opened in 1960.
The Japanese automotive industry is widely known for its creative manufacturing processes, including

activities that drive continuous improvement on the production line. To pass this manufacturing philosophy and these processes on to future generations, TMC introduced the Toyota Virtual Plant Tour on its website in 2023 as a comprehensive guide to the car manufacturing process. The new exhibition space builds on this initiative. After introducing the origin of Toyota's passion for manufacturing, the exhibition takes a close look at the entire carmaking process―from vehicle planning and development to production and logistics. The exhibition is divided into three zones, each presenting a multifaceted perspective through real vehicles and dynamic visuals.
Zone 1: The Inspiration for TOYOTA's Creative Carmaking

Toyota's approach to creative carmaking was inspired by Sakichi Toyoda, the founder of the Toyota Group and the father of Kiichiro Toyoda, who founded TMC. As a young boy, Sakichi wanted to ease his mother's work burden. His commitment to "for the benefit of others" continues to inspire TMC employees today, as does the slogan "Let's Make Ever-Better Cars," introduced in 2009 by Akio Toyoda, the current TMC chairman. United by these enduring visions, TMC employees pursue creative carmaking every day.

Kiichiro Toyoda aimed to establish the automobile industry as the foundation of Japan's economic development. "With Japanese ideas and skills, we must create an automobile industry for Japan," he declared before successfully completing the Toyoda Model AA, Toyota's first passenger car. Zone 1 features a concept video on the origins of Toyota's carmaking philosophy, together with a one-eighth scale model of the Toyoda Model AA.

One of Toyota's distinctive approaches to carmaking is its organizational style, which grants chief engineers extensive responsibility over their respective models, covering planning, development, production, and sales. This exhibit zone uses graphics, videos, and figures, and special lighting effects to show how teams unite under the chief engineer's leadership. The exhibition uses the fifth-generation Prius released in 2023 as a case study. Through real vehicles and life-size video presentations, the exhibition presents behind-the-scenes development episodes and demonstrates how engineering, production, and sales personnel worked closely together throughout the development process.
Zone 3: Experience the Wonder and Craftsmanship of Toyota's Manufacturing Plants

This exhibit zone uses graphics to illustrate the basic production flow, including stamping, welding, painting, assembly, inspection, and logistics. Real disassembled parts and welding robots complement the displays. In addition, visitors can experience dynamic plant operations in an immersive theater, together with large-screen production line footage from the workers' perspective.

Through this exhibition, we hope to convey the appeal of automobiles and the spirit of carmaking and monozukuri that underpin them to people of all ages, and to contribute to promoting automobiles as part of Japanese culture.

Broadcom Introduces VMware HyperArmor, Expanding Hypervisor Security and Protections for VMware Cloud Foundation
VMware HyperArmor offers unique, proactive zero day protection to VMware Cloud Foundation environments with no downtime, software upgrades, or in-guest agents

PALO ALTO, Calif., Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO), a global technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, today introduced VMware HyperArmor, a new software solution to help further protect the VMware ESX hypervisor component of VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) against the exponential increase in cyber attack sophistication by closing exposure windows without disrupting the workloads that depend on the host.

"Frontier AI has changed the three V's of cybersecurity threats - the volume, velocity, and variety. When attacks come at machine speed, reactive detection and patching are no longer enough," said Paul Turner, chief product officer, VMware Cloud Foundation Division, Broadcom. "VMware HyperArmor takes a different approach by allowing only what is 'known good' to run on the host. With VMware vDefend already delivering virtual patching capabilities for the network layer of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware HyperArmor now expands that protection around the hypervisor component itself."

As AI-accelerated threats grow in scale and sophistication, the threat surface now extends across every layer of the infrastructure stack including the hypervisor. Two problems account for most hypervisor attacks: stolen root credentials and unpatched vulnerabilities. VMware HyperArmor addresses both problems, with support for VMware ESX 8.x and later releases, as follows:
Virtual patching for VCF’s ESX Component Host Environment.

HyperArmor delivers host-layer virtual patching to shield ESX by detecting and blocking attempted malicious actions within the host nodes before any vulnerabilities can be exploited. These host-level virtual patching capabilities complement the network-layer virtual patching available for VCF via VMware vDefend. Because virtual patching of ESX does not require host reboots or software upgrades to mitigate vulnerabilities, security teams will benefit from dramatically reduced risk windows and IT teams gain more operational flexibility to test and apply official patches on the schedule they prefer.

HyperArmor protects the host at the infrastructure layer, with no agents inside guest virtual machines (VMs). An ESX host runs a small, fixed set of processes. HyperArmor establishes a positive security baseline and automatically blocks any unauthorized executable or script. HyperArmor takes an inventory of scripts already on the host and allows them automatically, and administrators can approve new ones. The result is continuous monitoring and compliance enforcement with minimal performance overhead.

HyperArmor integrates MFA functionality directly into the ESX SSH login path. Logging in requires two steps: standard SSH credentials, followed by a secondary time-based one-time password challenge tied to a separately defined identity. Even if an attacker obtains the root password through phishing or credential leaks, they cannot reach the command line without that second factor.

“Attackers are using automation and AI to exploit infrastructure weaknesses faster than most organizations can patch, which means layered defense must extend all the way to the hypervisor as the foundation of the private cloud,” said Stephen Elliot, Group Vice President, Software Development and IT Operations, IDC. “Technology leaders should prioritize preventive controls that help shrink exposure windows without disrupting production, and approaches that harden the virtualization layer natively rather than relying on external agents or post-incident detection.”
Defense in Depth Across VMware Cloud Foundation

VMware HyperArmor works alongside the broader security capabilities in VMware Cloud Foundation to deliver an integrated and multi-layered approach. VMware Cloud Foundation is hardened out of the box with key capabilities that include centralized identity management, data-at-rest and data-in-transit encryption, and VMware vSphere live patching, which applies critical updates to the hypervisor without taking workloads down or placing hosts into full maintenance mode. VMware HyperArmor adds a proactive layer of protection for the hypervisor by blocking process execution exploits and credential theft. VMware vDefend delivers strong lateral security with micro-segmentation and advanced threat detection and prevention for VCF workloads, which uses deep traffic inspection to block emerging exploits and to deliver network-level virtual patching. VMware Avi Load Balancer provides web application and API protection (WAAP) for securing web and API traffic. Together, these layers give customers defense in depth across the infrastructure, network, and hypervisor.

AST Completes Singapore's First High-End FC-BGA Substrate Facility to Meet Growing AI Chip Demand
First Flip Chip Ball Grid Array (FC-BGA) substrate production facility in Singapore
Addresses one of the most critical supply chain capacity constraints of the semiconductor industry
Diversifies Singapore’s semiconductor ecosystem beyond current wafer fab, IC design and assembly operations.

Advanced Substrate Technologies (AST) today announced the official opening of its new manufacturing facility in Singapore, the first in the country capable of producing high-end Flip Chip Ball Grid Array (FC-BGA) substrates, and the TOPPAN Group’s first such facility outside Japan. The milestone comes as demand for advanced substrate capacity, a persistent bottleneck for AI, networking, and next-generation computing chips, continues to outpace global supply. AST is a joint venture between TOPPAN Holdings Inc. and Broadcom Inc.

A delegation of AST executives, including key partners from the TOPPAN Group and Broadcom welcomed Mr Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade), alongside other partners and guests to the opening ceremony.

“AST’s ability to deliver large-body, high-layer-count substrates at TOPPAN's exacting standard is helping meet a real bottleneck in AI and networking chip production,” said Yoshiyuki Iida, CEO, AST. “We are grateful for the longstanding support and partnership of the Singapore government in this venture. This investment reflects both TOPPAN and Broadcom’s long-term commitment to Singapore as a critical hub in our global manufacturing network and strengthens the resilience of the semiconductor supply chain.”

The approximately 95,000-square-metre facility is designed to meet the growing demand for generative AI and data centres in the region featuring sustainability elements such as solar panels and advanced water recycling technologies. The Singapore production base also complements TOPPAN’s main production hub in Niigata, Japan, and will manufacture large-body, high-layer-count substrates for advanced semiconductor products, including AI compute and networking devices.

Since breaking ground in March 2024, AST has already hired more than 200 high-tech engineers and skilled technicians, in addition to operational personnel in Singapore. The facility also houses R&D capabilities to meet future performance demands, alongside close collaborations with technology institutions in Singapore.

“Singapore continues to be an attractive destination and gateway to the global semiconductor industry for us, especially with a strong ecosystem of innovation, capabilities and resources,” said Satoshi Oya, President & COO, TOPPAN Holdings. “TOPPAN looks forward to continuing to drive advanced semiconductor packaging forward as artificial intelligence accelerates across the board.”
The project is supported by Singapore's Economic Development Board (EDB) and JTC Corporation, which have played a key role in enabling the facility's establishment.

“AST’s facility will boost Singapore’s capabilities in advanced substrates, which is a critical enabler for advanced packaging, and strengthen our position in the global semiconductor value chain,” said Png Cheong Boon, Chairman, Singapore Economic Development Board. “Singapore has served as an important base for Broadcom and TOPPAN. We are glad that both companies are growing their manufacturing and R&D presence here through AST. EDB will continue to work with both companies and AST to build new capabilities to support global demand for semiconductors, and create new jobs and opportunities here.”

JTC Ms Jacqueline Poh, Chief Executive of JTC Corporation, said: “Advanced substrates are increasingly critical to the semiconductor value chain as AI and high-performance computing drive demand. JTC is pleased to support Broadcom and TOPPAN in establishing this new facility in Jurong and will continue to work with industry partners to provide the infrastructure needed for next generation semiconductor manufacturing in Singapore.”

As TOPPAN's largest customer for FC-BGA substrates, Broadcom has closely supported the facility's development, reflecting the strategic importance of additional large-body, high-layer-count substrate capacity to its next-generation AI compute and networking product roadmap.

“AST's FC-BGA substrate capacity in Singapore gives us meaningful flexibility and differentiation as demand for AI and networking silicon continues to climb. This facility, brought online three months early, strengthens our supply chain resilience by delivering vital relief while the industry is constrained by substrate shortages,” said Charlie Kawwas, Ph.D., president, Semiconductor Solutions Group, Broadcom. “Thanks to the exceptional execution by TOPPAN and AST, alongside the continued partnership of the Singapore EDB, this facility will deliver the next generation of large-body, high-layer-count substrates that Broadcom requires to further scale global AI infrastructure.”

Located in the Jurong Lake District, AST’s facility is targeting the start of high-value manufacturing by late-2026, with ongoing recruitment across engineering and technical roles. The company will work closely with TOPPAN and Broadcom to scale the output as demand for advanced substrates grows across AI, networking, and next-generation computing applications.

Purpose-Built to Accelerate Innovation and Commercialization

, campus, the EPIC Center represents one of the most complex R&D construction projects in the world. The 600,000-square-foot structure houses nearly four acres of advanced cleanroom space and required more than six million construction hours to complete. Its foundation holds enough concrete to fill 34 Olympic-sized swimming pools, and its steel-reinforced structure holds enough steel to build two
. Thirty-four roof trusses cover the cleanrooms, each spanning nearly 300 feet in length and weighing as much as 12 school buses.

EPIC is designed to reinvent the R&D model the industry has relied on for decades. In the traditional model, foundational materials research happens in one environment, equipment and process development in another, and process integration and pilot production in a third, with a careful handoff at every phase. The EPIC Center is designed to remove these handoffs, putting the people who invent the materials, build the equipment, and make the chips together in a state-of-the-art facility purpose-built for commercialization.

EPIC is founded on a simple conviction: the technologies the AI era demands are too complex and too consequential for any one company to invent alone. The EPIC Center opens with a founding roster that spans the AI technology stack. . Each partner brings its own roadmap challenges and engineers into the facility, working in tight, secure learning cycles alongside Applied teams. Over time, additional companies and organizations are expected to join the EPIC ecosystem.

New governed agentic execution runtime enables Oracle Fusion Agentic Applications to complete highly complex work more autonomously at scale
25 Claw-powered Fusion Agentic Applications are now available to help organizations drive business outcomes with built-in, enterprise-grade governance and security controls

Oracle today announced Oracle Fusion Claw, a governed agentic execution runtime for Oracle Fusion Agentic Applications that combines AI reasoning with deterministic enterprise computation to enable highly complex work to be economically completed at scale. Oracle Fusion Applications customers can take advantage of Fusion Claw through 25 new Claw-powered agentic applications that can reason, compute, adapt, and execute specialist-grade work including deep research, computation, simulation, modeling, and continuous re-planning. The new Claw-powered Agentic Applications are the latest additions to the growing portfolio of 75 Agentic Applications that can coordinate and execute end-to-end business processes.

“Every organization is looking at AI and asking the same question: how can we use it to create measurable value for our business?” said Mike Sicilia, CEO, Oracle. “Fusion Claw helps answer that question by moving from AI assistance to execution, enabling customers to automate increasingly complex work across their most important business processes, with enterprise-grade governance. By letting AI take on more of the work, while people set the objectives and guardrails, organizations can unlock tremendous capacity for their teams to focus more on driving growth, innovation, and serving customers.”

Agentic Applications represent a new class of outcome-based applications that provide Fusion Applications customers with a system of outcomes, where people define the objectives, authority, and accountability and the Agentic Applications coordinate the process to get to an outcome. Fusion Claw enables Agentic Applications to take on more complex, specialist-grade work by providing a new execution runtime that supports larger scale and longer-running work, continuous replanning, deterministic execution, and increased governed autonomy. Each Claw Outcome begins with a frontier model that reasons, plans, learns, and adapts. Fusion Claw then uses deterministic enterprise computation to execute precisely and at scale. This separation provides Fusion Applications customers with a potential economic advantage by applying AI reasoning only where intelligence is needed and using efficient deterministic computation for high-volume execution.

To govern autonomous enterprise execution, Fusion Claw applies an Enterprise Operating Envelope, which includes an organization’s objectives, standard operating procedures, policies, constraints, permissions, risk thresholds, decision rights, approval requirements, and escalation boundaries. The operating envelope is enforced across all outcomes through an Outcome Trust Harness that applies specific governing authority and controls to each outcome run, including identity, capabilities, data, and actions. When the outcome is complete, an Outcome Receipt provides an auditable record of exactly what happened, including the authority applied, evidence used, decisions made, actions and transactions executed, and the result. In addition, Fusion Applications customers can decide what level of automation they want a process to have, ranging from quick assistance to governed full auto execution within explicitly delegated authority.

Running on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and powered by industry-leading frontier models including Gemini and OpenAI, with support for additional frontier models planned over time, new Claw-powered Agentic Applications extend the broader Agentic Applications portfolio. There are 25 new Claw-powered, full auto-capable Agentic Applications available today, including:

Through various improvements, such as expansion of the high-efficiency operating range of the engine and improvement of the efficiency and downsizing of the drive unit, Honda is striving to further improve the fuel economy of next-generation hybrid models.

Moreover, the next-generation hybrid models equipped with Honda Hybrid systems will be built on the newly-developed platform that achieves both optimized rigidity and weight reduction through the adoption of a new approach to body rigidity management which brings about vehicle behavior as if the body is flexing during cornering and improving roadholding performance. In addition, new features such as a Motion Management System, original Honda integrated control technology, and a newly-developed electric all-wheel-drive system (e-AWD), will enable those models to deliver a high-quality and exhilarating driving experience at the will of the driver, appealing to all senses of the driver, while providing peace of mind.

First introduced in the first-generation Insight in 1999, IMA was a lightweight and compact parallel hybrid system in which the engine served as the primary source of power, with the motor assisting the engine during startup and acceleration. As the original Honda hybrid system, IMA achieved both excellent environmental performance and the fun of driving.
SPORT HYBRID i-DCD (Intelligent Dual Clutch Drive) – Introduced in 2012

i-DCD was a one-motor hybrid system featuring a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission (DCT) with a high-output motor integrated into the transmission. In addition to excellent fuel economy, the system delivered powerful acceleration and a rhythmic, leaner acceleration feel.
SPORT HYBRID i-MMD (Intelligent Multi-Mode Drive) – introduced in 2012

i-MMD was a hybrid system equipped with two motors: generator motor and traction motor. With the adoption of high-efficiency, high-output motors, the system delivers excellent fuel economy together with the smooth, powerful driving performance unique only to EVs. With two motors, the system uses efficient motor drive for most daily driving situations. This high-efficiency hybrid system automatically and seamlessly switches among three driving modes according to driving conditions, achieving EV-like smooth and powerful acceleration, a high level of quietness, and excellent environmental performance. From 2020 onward, Honda adopted “e:HEV” as the communication name for this hybrid technology.
SPORT HYBRID SH-AWD (Super Handling All-Wheel Drive) – introduced in 2012

SH-AWD was a three-motor hybrid system that combined an engine and three motors. Original Honda torque-control technology, using right and left independent electric motors for torque vectoring, enabled the system to optimally distribute driving force to all four wheels, achieving both outstanding fuel economy and driving performance.

Honda Hybrid is a next-generation hybrid system developed by further advancing key components of e:HEV, such as the engine and drive unit, as well as the control technologies. The system name, Honda Hybrid, will also serve as a communication name.

TOKYO, Japan, September 7, 2026 - Honda HRC PETRONAS rider Jeffrey Herlings (31, Netherlands) claimed the series championship in MXGP, the premier class, at Round 17 of the 2026 FIM* Motocross World Championship (MXGP), the Türkiye GP, held from September 5–6.

Herlings joined Honda HRC PETRONAS for the 2026 season and made a strong start with victory at the season-opening Argentina GP. By the end of Round 16, the Netherlands GP, he had recorded 10 victories, including five consecutive wins, and held a commanding 143-point lead over the second-ranked rider, putting him within reach of the championship.

With his resulting points advantage over the second-ranked rider, he secured the MXGP championship with two rounds remaining. He went on to win Race 2 as well, completing an overall victory at the Türkiye GP to celebrate his championship success.

“Wow. What a ride it’s been to win this sixth world title. Even since my last one in 2021 to finally get number six is just an incredible feeling. Just so glad to have made it happen and a big thank you to the team and to my friends and family who have supported me through some tough times.”
Marcus Pereira de Freitas, Honda HRC PETRONAS Team Manager

“It has been an amazing effort from Jeffrey and the whole team. This year has been one of the hardest years, but I think it proves that hard work pays off because when you look at the performances that Jeffrey has been putting in this year, especially these last few weeks, this championship is exactly what he deserves. A big thank you to Jeffrey, to the whole team at the races, and also everyone back at Japan for helping make this happen, I am proud of everyone.”
Koji Watanabe, President of Honda Racing Corporation

“I would like to express my sincere respect and gratitude to Jeffrey Herlings for winning the MXGP World Championship in his first year with Honda HRC PETRONAS. In a new environment with a new machine and a new team, he won from the opening round and demonstrated throughout the season the speed and strength of a rider competing at the highest level in the world. In particular, during the second half of the season, he continued to take victories in a variety of track conditions and made powerful progress toward securing the title, inspiring all of us along the way. This title is the result not only of Herlings’ tireless efforts, but also of the entire team—including Team Manager Marcus and all of the staff and riders—coming together under the new structure and continuing to take on the challenge as one. Once again, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to all of the sponsors and everyone involved who have supported Honda HRC PETRONAS, as well as motocross fans around the world for their passionate support.”

The C-130J-30 Super Hercules will be modified into the E-130J Phoenix II, the Navy's next‑generation TACAMO mission platform, fulfilling an added mission for the Super Hercules. TACAMO is the U.S. Navy's airborne nuclear command‑and‑control support mission.

It is built to deliver the capabilities our joint force demands and built to last through any operational challenge."

The delivery re-establishes the link between the TACAMO mission and the Hercules family. For three decades, the EC-130Q variant served as the Navy's TACAMO platform, flying the mission successfully from 1963 until 1993. The new Super Hercules builds on that legacy while adding advanced avionics, communications and survivability enhancements.

"The C-130J platform has a storied history supporting our strategic communications mission, and accepting this first C-130J-30 marks an exciting new chapter," said U.S. Navy Capt. Spain has proven renewables can scale, now it must ensure the system can operate reliably as complexity increases
Net zero is achievable, but not all pathways are equal, system design choices will determine cost, resilience, and long-term performance
Electricity demand is expected to grow ~60% by 2050, increasing pressure on flexibility, grid infrastructure, and system coordination
New analysis from GE Vernova outlines the trade-offs and system choices required to deliver a reliable net zero power system

(15 October 2026) – Spain has emerged as one of Europe’s leading renewable energy markets, with renewables supplying nearly 57% of electricity in 2025 and more than 80% renewable electricity expected by 2030. But as renewable penetration accelerates and electricity demand is projected to grow by around 60% by 2050, the country’s next challenge is no longer scaling renewable energy, it is ensuring the power system can operate reliably under increasing complexity.

As renewable penetration rises and system dynamics shift, challenges around stability, flexibility, and grid coordination are becoming more pronounced. Events such as the April 2025 Iberian blackout have brought renewed attention to system strength, reserve margins, and the need for coordinated grid operation in a high-renewables environment.
New analysis from GE Vernova examines how Spain can meet its net zero goals while maintaining reliability, affordability, and system resilience.

The analysis finds that Spain can achieve a net zero electricity system by 2050 through multiple pathways. However, these pathways differ significantly in terms of system cost, infrastructure requirements, operational resilience, and execution complexity.

"Spain has earned its place as one of Europe's leaders in the energy transition,” said Jaime Elguero, Country Manager, Spain, GE Vernova. “The challenge now is not whether the country can achieve its ambitions, but how to build a power system that keeps pace with them, one that is as reliable and resilient as it is sustainable.”

With electricity demand projected to rise by around 60% by 2050, driven by electrification and economic growth, the analysis outlines four distinct pathways for Spain’s power system: Business-as-Usual, Progressive, Pioneering, and Lower-Carbon Pathway, illustrating how different system choices shape long-term outcomes.

Across these pathways, wind and solar capacity could expand to between 150 GW and 250 GW by 2050. At the same time, the analysis shows that a renewable-dominated system is not a renewable-only system. Even in the most renewable-heavy scenarios, 15-20% of system capacity must remain firm and dispatchable to maintain reliability during periods of low wind and solar output.

This shifts the focus from how much capacity is built to how the system is balanced, operated, and reinforced over time. Technologies such as storage, hydrogen, nuclear extensions, and carbon capture play structural roles in supporting system flexibility and stability.

Transmission and flexibility emerge as critical enablers of the transition. As renewable generation becomes more geographically concentrated, long-distance power flows increase, placing greater pressure on grid infrastructure. Without coordinated investment in transmission, storage, and system services, system inefficiencies such as renewable curtailment are likely to increase.

The analysis also underscores the role of policy and market design in enabling this transition. Streamlined permitting, incentives for geographically optimized renewable deployment, support for storage, and market mechanisms that value flexibility will be essential to align investment with system needs.
“We are proud to partner with Spain's utilities, policymakers and industry leaders as they shape the next chapter of the country's energy future,” added Elguero.

As Spain advances toward its 2030 and 2050 targets, the defining challenge is no longer ambition, but execution. The analysis provides a framework for policymakers, system operators, and investors to navigate trade-offs and build a power system that is not only net zero, but reliable, resilient, and economically sustainable.

Merck Inaugurates State-of-the-Art ADVANCE Bioanalytical Facility on West Point, Pennsylvania, Campus
Gov. Josh Shapiro joins Merck leadership for official ribbon-cutting ceremony
Merck’s $550 million regional investment reinforces ongoing commitment to U.S. R&D while strengthening its long-standing footprint in Pennsylvania

RAHWAY N.J., Oct. 14, 2026 – Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, today inaugurated its state-of-the-art ADVANCE research facility on its West Point, Pennsylvania, campus, signaling a new chapter in global scientific discovery. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro joined Merck executive leadership, federal and state government officials and local community partners for a ribbon-cutting ceremony to celebrate the pivotal expansion of the company’s premier research and development capabilities.

By integrating highly automated robotic systems and advanced digital AI capabilities, ADVANCE is designed to streamline the analysis of biological samples from Merck’s ongoing clinical development programs while supporting one of the broadest and most diverse pipelines in the company’s recent history.

“My Administration has made life sciences a key part of our economic development strategy here in Pennsylvania — and Merck’s major investment in Montgomery County is another major win for the Commonwealth,” said Gov. Josh Shapiro. “We are proud to partner with Merck as they expand their operations in Montgomery County, advance cutting-edge research and manufacturing, and create new opportunities for thousands of Pennsylvanians. The life sciences industry is booming in Pennsylvania and I am committed to winning more investments like this and making sure our Commonwealth remains a national leader in innovation, medicine and manufacturing.”

The ribbon-cutting marks another significant milestone for the 400-acre West Point campus, Merck’s largest integrated research and human health manufacturing site. Since 1953, West Point site has been home to a series of important biopharmaceutical breakthroughs. The addition of the ADVANCE research facility ensures Pennsylvania remains a key driver of global scientific innovation.

“The ADVANCE facility represents the future of clinical development at Merck and underscores our continued commitment to addressing the needs of the patients we serve,” said Rob Davis, chairman and chief executive officer, Merck. “This builds on our longstanding presence in Pennsylvania where we’re proud to invest in the people, communities and scientific capabilities that will help drive the next generation of medicines.”
A legacy of scientific progress in Pennsylvania

Merck originally acquired the West Point site as part of the landmark 1953 merger of Merck and Sharp & Dohme. Since then, Merck’s operations in Pennsylvania have grown substantially, transforming the West Point campus into a cornerstone of the company’s research efforts and global manufacturing supply chain. Today, the site is the largest employer in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, and the seventh largest private employer in the state.

Merck has made significant capital investments to the West Point site totaling more than $15 billion over the past 35 years. As part of the company’s previously announced $70 billion commitment to domestic manufacturing and R&D, Merck is investing approximately $550 million in R&D facilities at ADVANCE and the nearby Spring House Innovation Park (SHIP).

The capital investments at West Point have continuously sustained an on-site workforce of approximately 800 contracting, engineering, and construction jobs during this time. Many of these capital projects have been designed in Pennsylvania and represent more than $1 billion in services provided by locally based architects.

Intismeran autogene (intismeran; V940 or mRNA-4157) is a novel, potential first-in-class investigational messenger RNA (mRNA)-based individualized neoantigen therapy (INT) jointly developed by Merck and Moderna. Intismeran is designed and produced using a patient's tumor sample to identify the unique mutational signature, or "fingerprint," of their cancer and generate an anti-tumor immune response. Each therapy consists of a synthetic mRNA coding for up to 34 neoantigens and is tailored to the unique biology of an individual patient's tumor. Upon administration, the RNA-encoded neoantigen sequences are translated in the body and presented to the immune system, a key step in generating specific T-cell responses against cancer cells. KEYTRUDA is an anti-programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) therapy that works by increasing the ability of the body’s immune system to help detect and fight tumor cells. KEYTRUDA is a humanized monoclonal antibody that blocks the interaction between PD-1 and its ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, thereby activating T lymphocytes which may affect both tumor cells and healthy cells.

Merck has the industry’s largest immuno-oncology clinical research program. There are currently more than 2,800 trials studying KEYTRUDA across a wide variety of cancers and treatment settings. The KEYTRUDA clinical program seeks to understand the role of KEYTRUDA across cancers and the factors that may predict a patient's likelihood of benefitting from treatment with KEYTRUDA, including exploring several different biomarkers.
