• Eaton announces $1 million commitment to support global freshwater conservation through The Nature Conservancy

CLEVELAND, OH – Intelligent power management company Eaton today announced a $1 million investment over four years to support The Nature Conservancy's (TNC) Global Freshwater Program and Forever Freshwater Geographies, helping protect and restore freshwater resources around the world.

The investment will support freshwater conservation efforts across priority geographies, including the Western Balkans, Selva Maya, the Colorado River Basin, the Great Lakes and Appalachia. Through this collaboration, Eaton and TNC will work to advance freshwater resilience, support healthy ecosystems and strengthen communities in some of the world's most important freshwater landscapes. While Eaton has a long history of investing in communities, this commitment is one of the largest philanthropic contributions in the company’s 115-year history.

"Strong businesses don’t succeed in isolation. They succeed when the communities around them are healthy and resilient," said Lucy Clark Dougherty, executive vice president and chief legal officer, Eaton. "For generations, Eaton and our people have contributed their time, talent and resources to support the places we call home. As we continue to grow, so does our opportunity and responsibility to make a positive impact. Through our support of The Nature Conservancy, we're investing in the long-term resilience of both communities and freshwater systems, creating lasting impact for generations to come.”

Through TNC's Global Freshwater Program and Forever Freshwater Geographies initiative, conservation efforts focus on improving river and watershed health, restoring critical habitats, supporting biodiversity and strengthening freshwater resilience in regions facing growing environmental pressures.

“This collaboration with Eaton will help advance healthy freshwater systems across North America, Europe, and Latin America,” said Nicole Silk, The Nature Conservancy’s global director of freshwater. "Directing investment to these programs will help safeguard and restore rivers, lakes and wetlands that directly benefit communities around the world.”

Eaton is an intelligent power management company dedicated to protecting the environment and improving the quality of life for people everywhere. We make products for the data center, utility, industrial, commercial, machine building, residential, aerospace and mobility markets. • Eaton Mobility segment to highlight Advantor series of automated manual transmissions at IAA Transportation

SOUTHFIELD, Mich.— Intelligent power management company Eaton today announced that its Mobility segment is introducing a full family of Advantor™ automated manual transmissions (AMTs), purpose-built for fleets to deliver greater efficiency, superior drivability and lower total cost of ownership in the next generation of commercial trucks and buses. The Advantor portfolio will be showcased at IAA Transportation, September 15–20, 2026, in Hannover, Germany.

Designed with OEMs and end users' challenges in mind, the Advantor lineup offers 6-, 8- and 10-speed models tailored for light-, medium-, and medium-heavy duty applications. By blending advanced automation with smart, adaptive controls and application-specific tuning, these transmissions help manufacturers create vehicles that feel more responsive and intuitive while delivering real-world performance gains across diverse operating conditions.

Advantor represents a new chapter in intelligent drivetrains. It gives OEMs a powerful way to boost fuel efficiency — up to 10% better than manual transmissions and up to 20% versus traditional automatics — while improving vehicle uptime, extending component life and simplifying integration into today’s platforms. Fleets win with lower operating costs and drivers enjoy a smoother, more confident experience behind the wheel.

At the heart of Advantor is Eaton’s proven automation technology, combining an electronically controlled X-Y shifter, pneumatic clutch actuation, inertia brake and an intelligent transmission control unit powered by advanced software. Built on a common software architecture, the system continuously analyzes road conditions, vehicle load and driver input to optimize shift timing and clutch engagement in real time. Features such as Load-Based Shifting, Smart Gear Selection, Hill Start Aid and Engine Overspeed Protection work together to enhance drivability, improve efficiency and help protect drivetrain components. The result is smoother operation, reduced wear and consistent, predictable performance that OEMs and fleets can confidently spec into their vehicles.

One of the transmission family’s biggest strengths is its high degree of component commonality across models. This shared architecture not only streamlines manufacturing and assembly for vehicle builders but also simplifies service and maintenance through common components and service procedures. The result is improved parts commonality, reduced maintenance complexity and greater vehicle uptime.

Advantor is also engineered for strong long-term value, with extended oil drain intervals of up to 700,000 kilometers in certain configurations and efficiency improvements that support lower emissions. Its flexible design allows for easy integration across a wide variety of vehicle platforms, giving manufacturers the freedom to enhance performance without adding unnecessary complexity.

The 6-speed model is optimized for lighter-duty trucks and buses with torque ratings up to 700 Nm and 14-ton GVW, while the 8-speed targets medium-duty bus and truck applications up to 1,300 Nm. The 10-speed variant, also up to 1,300 Nm torque capacity, brings robust capability to medium-heavy duty trucks, excelling in both linehaul and vocational roles, such as construction, agricultural and refuse trucks applications.

By making driving easier and more efficient in demanding real-world conditions, Advantor helps elevate the entire ownership experience—from the production line to the open road. This launch underscores Eaton’s ongoing commitment to advancing intelligent drivetrain solutions that combine cutting-edge controls, reliable engineering and scalable design in one cohesive family.

OEM partners and fleet operators will find Advantor an ideal choice for meeting evolving demands around efficiency, sustainability and driver satisfaction. It’s more than a transmission—it’s a smarter foundation for the commercial vehicles of tomorrow.

• Agile Robots announces Agile ONE SN, a humanoid reference platform built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and NVIDIA Jetson Thor with planned integration of the NVIDIA Halos safety stack, giving developers and researchers a complete platform for frontier humanoid development and validation.

• NVIDIA Isaac platform adds new Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0 for robot learning and open source reference workflows that combine ChatGPT Astra with NVIDIA Isaac and Cosmos on NVIDIA DGX Station to accelerate robot data generation, training and evaluation.

• Europe’s robotics ecosystem, including leaders like ABB Robotics, Flexion, Hexagon Robotics, Humanoid, KUKA, NEURA Robotics, Sereact and Universal Robots, is building on NVIDIA’s open robotics platform to advance autonomous robotic systems.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced a major expansion of the NVIDIA Isaac™ open robotics development platform, adding a reference humanoid, datasets and runtime, along with updates to its robot learning framework.
Together, these technologies give developers an integrated path from data to deployment to bring general-purpose robots to the real-world faster.

“General-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed — the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA Isaac, our full-stack open robotics platform, we are giving developers the models, data, simulation tools and computing systems to bring physical AI to the world’s largest industries.”

Agile ONE SN — A Frontier Humanoid Reference Platform for Research Agile Robots announced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack reference humanoid preconfigured with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and powered by the NVIDIA Jetson Thor™ edge AI platform.

Robotics researchers and developers often struggle to integrate the separate simulation, training and deployment tools needed to take robot skills from development to the physical world. Agile ONE SN unifies these tools and workflows on a single platform, cutting setup time from weeks to days.
• Agile ONE S humanoid body, standing 1.40 meters (4.59 feet tall) and weighing 40 kilograms (88 pounds), with 31 degrees of freedom and a 3-kilogram payload per arm.
• Dual WUJI Hand 2 five-finger hands, each offering 20 degrees of freedom, 1kHz force control and tactile sensing for dexterous manipulation
• NVIDIA Jetson Thor onboard compute, delivering 2,070 FP4 teraflops of compute and 128GB of unified memory for onboard reasoning and real-time control.
• Multimodal sensing, including head and wrist cameras, lidar sensors and inertial measurement units to help the robot perceive and interact with its surroundings.
• NVIDIA Isaac GR00T platform, which comprises the GR00T foundation model, a full workflow from data capture to deployment and whole-body control for coordinated movement.
• Safety capabilities, with planned integration of on-robot safety protocols with the NVIDIA Halos full-stack safety system for robotics.

“The breakthrough for humanoids is usefulness at scale: one adaptable machine that learns many skills and works across environments built for people,” said Zhaopeng Chen, founder and CEO of Agile Robots. “Today, Agile Robots introduced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack, open reference humanoid built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, powered by Jetson Thor, giving developers a ready system to create, train and validate the capabilities needed to put humanoids to work.”

Scheduled to be available in early 2027, Agile ONE SN is designed to advance frontier humanoid research and development, with interest from leading institutions such as Stanford University and ETH Zurich.

New NVIDIA Technology Accelerate Robot Learning — From Data to Deployment New NVIDIA technologies help developers generate training data, scale robot learning, build simulation environments and deploy robot applications, reducing time to solution.

• SimReady Central Library offers more than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, while the Human 1M Dataset includes diverse human activities, synchronized three-view video and 3D hand tracking. Both are available on Hugging Face, with the full Human 1M Dataset accessible to Cosmos Coalition partners.

• NVIDIA Isaac Lab 3.0 is now generally available, providing an open source, agent-ready learning framework training and refining robot policies from desktop to data center using multi-GPU workflows and physics engines including Newton and NVIDIA PhysX™.

• NVIDIA Isaac OS, an open source runtime framework built on NVIDIA Holoscan, connects AI, sensors, controls and robot hardware for deterministic, real-time performance from simulation to physical robots.

• NVIDIA is releasing three open source reference workflows for NVIDIA DGX Station™ that help developers refine GR00T 1.7 models with reinforcement learning, train dexterous manipulation skills in NVIDIA Isaac Lab and post-train NVIDIA Cosmos™ world models for synthetic data generation using ChatGPT Astra.
• NVIDIA Halos provides a full-stack safety platform built on NVIDIA IGX Thor™ to help move autonomous vehicles and robots from development to safer real-world deployment at scale.
SimReady Central Library on Hugging Face includes simulation-ready assets from Comau, FANUC, ForgeCAD, Franka Robotics, LG Electronics, Palatial, Robotiq, Standard Bots, Universal Robots and Vertiv.

NVIDIA’s open source robot learning reference workflows running on DGX Station will be supported by solutions from 1X, Agile Robots, Humanoid, Maven Robotics, Mentee, MicroAGI, Rhoda, Sereact and Skild AI.

Robotics partners are integrating NVIDIA Halos within their safety architectures, including Agile Robots, Agility, Dexory, FORT Robotics and KION for warehouse robot safety. SICK is evaluating Halos to advance dynamic safety for industrial robots, helping them respond to changing conditions beyond fixed zones.

Advantech and NexCOBOT are developing NVIDIA IGX-based industrial computing platforms, while Reynolds & Moore, Accenture and TÜV SÜD are accelerating the certification process for the safe deployment of industrial physical AI.

European Robotics Leaders Build on NVIDIA Open Technologies ABB Robotics is integrating NVIDIA Omniverse™ libraries with RobotStudio HyperReality to simulate and virtually commission robotic systems before installation across a wide range of industries. KUKA Group is using Omniverse libraries in its Visual Components FactoryLens to add real-time rendering for factory simulation workflows. Sereact is using Isaac GR00T with Cosmos Transfer to train and post-train its Cortex platform for goods handling, running on Universal Robots industrial robot arms.

Using Jetson Thor, Holoscan Sensor Bridge, Halos and NVIDIA Isaac OS, Humanoid is developing and validating robot behaviors before industrial pilots, Hexagon Robotics is building AEON perception capabilities including teleoperation video, localization, mapping and object pose detection, and Bear Robotics is accelerating KR1 perception and model execution while post-training Isaac GR00T through Kino-2 for warehouse, returns and industrial workflows.

Toyota Material Handling Europe and SoftServe use Omniverse and the NVIDIA Isaac Sim™ framework to develop autonomous material-handling solutions, reducing deployment time by up to 50%. Idealworks is using NVIDIA open models and Jetson to develop memory capabilities for autonomous mobile robots in factories. Analog Devices Inc. (ADI) is using NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin™ and the cuVSLAM library to build autonomous mobile robots.

Hugging Face and Pollen Robotics are using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Isaac Sim and Newton to build Microduck, a small, open source robot designed to help developers and students train, modify and share new physical behaviors. Franka Robotics is using NVIDIA NIM™ microservices and Isaac Sim to turn natural-language requests into actions on its Franka FR3 Duo robot system. Bellboy is using Jetson and GR00T to power Billie, its first robot teammate built on Bellboy’s physical AI infrastructure, already deployed at hotels operated by Marriott, Hilton, IHG and OYO.

• Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets, with Volvo Cars adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for safe automated driving.

• NVIDIA introduces Halos SAFE, a new framework within the NVIDIA Halos safety system, which combines simulation and physical testing to help developers generate measurable, traceable AV safety evidence.

• NVIDIA announces Alpamayo 2 Edge, Alpamayo Agentic Factory and new Cosmos 3 Nano model variants to help developers build, customize and evaluate autonomous-driving for diverse vehicles, operating conditions and regions.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced that leading automakers in Europe and mobility providers, including Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride, are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets.

In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale.

Autonomous transportation represents a multitrillion-dollar opportunity, with robotaxis leading the move to commercial level 4 deployment. NVIDIA Hyperion and the NVIDIA Halos full-stack safety system give automakers and mobility providers the computing performance, safety foundation and long-term support to bring AVs and robotaxi fleets to market at scale.

“Robotaxis are the first mass-market application of robotics and physical AI, reinventing how people and goods move,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “NVIDIA Hyperion, together with our Halos safety operating system, gives our partners a full-stack robotaxi platform designed to achieve full autonomy and the highest levels of safety, bringing us closer to a future where everything that moves is autonomous.”

Mobility Leaders in Europe Build on NVIDIA Hyperion Automakers and mobility providers in Europe are pursuing various paths to autonomy, from passenger vehicles and robotaxi fleets to autonomous freight trucks. NVIDIA Hyperion’s modular architecture supports all of these programs, compatible with NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack autonomous driving software as well as partners’ own driving software.

Bolt has selected NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for its European robotaxi program, beginning with future Lucid vehicles built on Hyperion. Bolt and NVIDIA will adapt the software for European roads and integrate it into vehicles from multiple manufacturers, combining NVIDIA’s driving and safety technologies with Bolt’s fleet-management systems, operations and local market expertise.

Bolt plans to begin gathering real-world driving data to support the development and validation of the autonomous driving technology — subject to regulatory approval — in Madrid in 2027, with Germany being a priority for future deployment as part of a planned European rollout of at least 25,000 level 4-capable future Lucid vehicles built on NVIDIA Hyperion.

At GTC Berlin, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles is presenting its autonomous ID. Buzz AD vehicle platform with Hyperion to support multiple autonomous-driving systems. Hyperion provides a common computing and sensor architecture designed to simplify integration and validation, helping developers and mobility operators bring robotaxi and commercial transport services to market.

Volvo Cars is combining its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with Hyperion, Halos OS and Alpamayo Stack to enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door.

Mercedes-Benz is extending its partnership with NVIDIA on Hyperion and Alpamayo Stack to support the development of the automaker’s L3 and L4 capabilities. The company also announced that MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO, developed in partnership with NVIDIA, will soon get approval for urban point-to-point urban driver assistance in Germany, helping drivers navigate journeys through complex city traffic.

Beyond passenger vehicles and robotaxis, Einride is building its next-generation Einride Driver on Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using Halos, Alpamayo and NVIDIA Cosmos™ open world models to develop and validate its driving system, while TIER IV and the Technical University of Munich plan to integrate Hyperion to develop and validate systems for autonomous public transportation in Germany.

NVIDIA technology and manufacturing partners are also helping expand the AV ecosystem, with Aptiv, Valeo and Schaeffler building Hyperion-based computing platforms that can be integrated by vehicle manufacturers for L4 AVs and robotaxis.

Scaling Safe Autonomy With NVIDIA Halos Halos provides the safety foundation for NVIDIA’s AV platform, bringing together AI computing, safety software and validation from development through deployment.

To give developers repeatable ways to evaluate driving behavior and simulation accuracy, NVIDIA today introduced Halos SAFE — the Safety Assurance Framework for Evaluation — with dSPACE, IVEX and TÜV Rheinland collaborating on evaluation workflows. Halos SAFE connects simulation, software- and hardware-in-the-loop evaluation, on-road testing and fleet monitoring through defined scenarios, tests and measurable performance criteria to generate traceable safety evidence that supports deployment.
The Halos SAFE ecosystem also includes JLR, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo Cars, 51Sim, aiMotive, AVL, Deepen AI, Foretellix and Synopsys.

Accelerating AV Development Developing AVs means teaching AI to handle the diversity of real-world driving, then bringing that intelligence into the vehicle. NVIDIA’s latest models, tools and blueprints help developers prepare driving data, improve models and evaluate performance:

• Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2-billion-parameter reasoning model built on NVIDIA Cosmos, is optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor™ platform and designed to run at 10Hz for in-vehicle scene understanding and motion planning.
• AlpaJudge, a human-calibrated evaluation and reward model, scores driving explanations to assess reasoning quality, filter weak annotations and reduce manual review of training data.
• Foundation4D labels multicamera video without lidar input, supporting perception-model training and NVIDIA Omniverse™ NuRec scene reconstruction.

• New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants expand synthetic data generation and closed-loop simulation for autonomous driving through synchronized multiview, multi-camera and lidar generation across diverse driving scenarios.
• Cosmos Data Factory’s AV dataset-generation blueprint turns driving video and vehicle signals into curated, searchable, labeled data, using synthetic data to expand scenario coverage.

• Alpamayo Agentic Factory, an open blueprint expected to become available in early 2027, uses AI agents to connect data preparation, model post-training and simulation evaluation, reducing integration work.
• NVIDIA NIM™ microservices for Alpamayo 1.5 and NuRec Harmonizer deliver both models as optimized inference containers, giving AV reasoning and scene harmonization a simplified deployment path.

Uber and NVIDIA are developing a data factory powered by Cosmos to curate and process data for AV development. The effort is part of a broader partnership spanning AI development infrastructure, Hyperion-based vehicles and Uber’s global ride-hailing network.

Porsche is leading the development of a data flywheel workflow across Volkswagen Group brands through Voxel51, using NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory and Omniverse NuRec on Microsoft Azure to turn fleet data into datasets and simulations for evaluating autonomous-driving models. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle duration by up to 85%.

Micron Appoints Deirdre Hanford to Lead Micron Research Labs

BOISE, Idaho, Sept. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Micron Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: MU) today announced the appointment of Deirdre Hanford as corporate vice president and president of Micron Research Labs, the company’s flagship long-horizon research institution. She will establish its research infrastructure, operating model and partnerships while defining a research agenda that extends across Micron, academia, government, startups and the broader industry ecosystem.

Micron Research Labs, announced in August 2026, is a global research institution headquartered in Boise, Idaho, and backed by Micron’s planned $10 billion investment over the next decade. As the first dedicated memory research hub of its kind in the U.S., it is connected to Micron’s research and technology footprint across the U.S., Europe, Japan, India, Singapore and Taiwan, with work spanning critical memory process technologies, future memory and compute architectures, advanced packaging and next-generation semiconductor manufacturing. Micron Research Labs builds on Micron’s previously announced U.S. investment plan of more than $250 billion in both manufacturing and R&D, expected to create 90,000 American jobs.

“Micron Research Labs was created to pursue the breakthroughs that will define the future of memory, compute and AI, and Deirdre is uniquely qualified to lead that mission,” said Scott DeBoer, president and chief technology and products officer of Micron Technology. “She combines deep semiconductor industry expertise with a proven ability to build partnerships, inspire collaboration and turn ambitious ideas into lasting impact.”

Hanford brings extensive semiconductor industry experience, ecosystem relationships and public-private collaboration expertise central to Micron Research Labs’ mission. Her appointment, following a comprehensive search, marks the transition of Micron Research Labs from launch toward execution, building on the company’s research momentum and reinforcing Micron’s position at the forefront of long-horizon memory and AI innovation.

“Micron Research Labs has both scale and long-term commitment,” said Deirdre Hanford, corporate vice president and president of Micron Research Labs. “We look forward to fostering innovation by enabling experienced and next-generation researchers whose ideas will shape future technologies and markets.”

Hanford most recently advised leading organizations across semiconductors, electronic design automation, national defense and AI. She previously led a national effort to strengthen U.S. semiconductor research and workforce development. Her career spans semiconductor innovation, secure microelectronics, public-private research strategy and industry partnerships. She spent 37 years at Synopsys, where she helped scale the company into a global leader in electronic design automation and semiconductor design intellectual property. Her roles there included chief security officer, co-general manager of the Design Group and executive vice president of customer engagement.

She previously served on the board of directors of Cirrus Logic and currently serves on the UC Berkeley College of Engineering Advisory Board, the MIT School of Engineering Dean’s Advisory Council and the SEMI Board of Industry Leaders. She received the 2025 IEEE Frederik Philips Award for visionary leadership in electronic design automation for secure and energy-efficient microelectronics.

Hanford will advance Micron Research Labs’ research charter, pursuing foundational technologies and scientific questions that extend well beyond today’s product roadmaps. As a member of DeBoer’s Innovation, Technology and Products leadership team, she will connect that research to priorities across Micron while deepening collaborations with universities, research institutions and technology partners worldwide.

Micron Technology, Inc. is a global leader in semiconductor memory and storage, powering AI and compute-intensive applications from cloud to edge. With a relentless focus on our customers, technology and product leadership, and manufacturing and operational excellence, Micron’s comprehensive portfolio of high-performance DRAM, NAND and NOR solutions deliver the speed, efficiency, and scale today’s workloads demand, accelerating intelligence to enrich life for all. • Eaton and Autodesk help simplify and accelerate delivery of increasingly complex electrical systems in commercial buildings
• Eaton Workbench 360 is designed to connect engineering expertise, equipment information and project visibility across Autodesk Revit, Forma and Tandem
• Eaton’s collaboration with Autodesk creates a connected ecosystem from design to operation to deliver projects faster

Pittsburgh – As buildings become more complex, project teams face growing pressure to deliver faster while managing labor shortages, technical complexity and coordination challenges across the building lifecycle. To help address these challenges, intelligent power management company Eaton, and Autodesk, the leader in design and make technology, are expanding their collaboration to connect equipment information, engineering expertise and project data across design, construction and operations workflows. To support these workflows, Eaton developed Workbench 360, a connected experience designed to bring its electrical equipment data, engineering expertise and project information to Autodesk® Revit®, Autodesk Forma® and Autodesk Tandem®, helping teams maintain visibility and context across the building lifecycle.

By helping keep critical information connected throughout the building lifecycle, Eaton and Autodesk aim to reduce manual handoffs, improve visibility and enable teams to better manage increasingly complex building projects. Workbench 360 is designed to help project teams maintain context and visibility as projects progress from design through construction and into operations across building, campus, healthcare and data center environments.

“As buildings become more electrified and infrastructure projects become more complex, customers need new ways to connect design decisions with project execution and long-term operations," said Justin Carron, director of buildings and campuses at Eaton. "Our collaboration with Autodesk helps bring together the expertise, information and workflows needed to make better decisions earlier, improve coordination across project teams and deliver critical infrastructure with greater speed and confidence.”

Through Autodesk Revit, engineers can access Eaton BIM content, product information and application engineering support earlier in the design process. As projects move into execution, Workbench 360 is designed to extend visibility through Forma Build™ into equipment status, submittals, order milestones, shipping information and project updates. In operations, connected equipment and project data can support Autodesk Tandem and Eaton Brightlayer digital energy twin capabilities, helping customers transition from project delivery to long-term asset management and energy optimization.

"One of the biggest challenges in delivering complex projects is keeping critical information connected as work moves from design to construction and operations,” said Sid Haksar, Head of Construction Strategy & Partnerships, Autodesk. “By bringing Eaton’s electrical expertise and equipment data into Autodesk workflows, we can help customers reduce friction between project phases and maintain the context they need throughout the building lifecycle.”
Eaton will demonstrate Workbench 360 at Autodesk University, booth 2216.

Eaton is an intelligent power management company dedicated to protecting the environment and improving the quality of life for people everywhere. We make products for the data center, utility, industrial, commercial, machine building, residential, aerospace and mobility markets. We are guided by our commitment to do business right, to operate sustainably and to help our customers manage power - today and well into the future. By capitalizing on the global growth trends of electrification and digitalization, we’re helping to solve the world’s most urgent power management challenges and building a more sustainable society for people today and generations to come.

Lam Research Announces Retirement of Michael R. Cannon and Sohail U. Ahmed from Board of Directors

/ -- Lam Research Corp. (NASDAQ: LRCX) today announced that Michael ("Mike") R. Cannon and Sohail U. Ahmed have informed the company of their respective decisions to retire from Lam's Board of Directors, effective November 2, 2026, following years of leadership.

"Mike's deep expertise in executive leadership and his passion for innovation have been invaluable in guiding Lam through strategic geographic growth and expanding its technology leadership in deposition, etch and advanced packaging," said Abhi Talwalkar, chair of the board at Lam Research. "Sohail's deep industry experience and understanding of silicon logic and semiconductor processing equipment technologies have been assets to our board. We thank Mike and Sohail for their dedication and many significant contributions and wish them well in their retirements."
Joining the Lam Board of Directors in 2011, Cannon retires after a career spanning more than 40 years of transformational leadership and innovation in several technology industries.

Most recently, Cannon held senior advisory and board roles providing guidance to technology companies on global strategy, business transformation, and operational excellence. At Seagate Technology Holdings, plc, he served on the board for fifteen years including five years as the lead independent director and five years as the board Chairman. Seagate recently announced that he will retire from the board later this year. He has also served on the boards of Dialog Semiconductor plc from 2013 until its sale to Renesas Electronics in 2021, and previously was on the board of Adobe Systems for 13 years.

Previously, Cannon held CEO and other executive leadership positions at top technology companies, most recently as the President of Global Operations at Dell Technologies leading the worldwide transformation of operations, supply chain and logistics functions. Prior to Dell, he was president and CEO of Solectron, a global electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider, where he led the company through a major transformation, including a comprehensive restructuring plan resulting in an increased focus on design services. Previously he was CEO of Maxtor Corporation, a disk drive technology leader, for seven years including a successful IPO in 1998 and the company's acquisition by Seagate in 2006. Cannon also held several senior leadership positions at IBM, including Vice President of the Personal Storage Systems Division, with P&L responsibility for disk drive and storage solutions products. Earlier in his career, he worked as a mechanical engineer in the R&D organization of Boeing and was named an Inventor of the Year in 1983.

Joining the Lam Board of Directors in 2019, Ahmed was formerly senior vice president and general manager of the Technology and Manufacturing Group at Intel Corporation, a leading producer of microchips, computing and communications products, where he was responsible for overseeing the research, development and deployment of next-generation silicon logic technologies for the production of future Intel microprocessors. He held that position from 2015 to 2018. Immediately prior to that, he was corporate vice president and general manager, Logic Technology Department, at Intel from 2004 to January 2015. Ahmed joined Intel in 1984, working as a process engineer, and held progressive technical and management positions in logic process development.

However, because there are no standardized or generally accepted definitions for most non-GAAP financial metrics, definitions of non-GAAP financial metrics are inherently subject to significant discretion (for example, determining which costs and expenses to exclude when calculating such a metric).

As a result, non-GAAP financial metrics may be defined very differently from company to company, or even from period to period within the same company, which can potentially limit the usefulness of such information to an investor.

– Today, Johnson & Johnson announced 30-day results from the FORWARD coronary artery disease (CAD) investigational device exemption (IDE) study evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the Shockwave Javelin Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy (IVL) Catheter. The catheter, an investigational device in the U.S., is designed for the treatment of calcified, difficult-to-cross stenotic de novo coronary artery lesions prior to stenting. The results were presented as featured clinical research at the 2026 Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics (TCT) congress in San Diego, California.
In the 158-patient pivotal cohort, event rates for the primary safety and effectiveness endpoints exceeded pre-specified performance goals. Key findings from the study include:

93.6% technical success rate (primary effectiveness endpoint, defined as successful Shockwave Javelin Coronary IVL-enabled lesion crossing without serious angiographic complications at final imaging).
93.4% freedom from major adverse cardiovascular events (primary safety endpoint, defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction or target vessel revascularization) through 30 days.

Additionally, the study demonstrated low complication rates in a highly complex lesion population. Among treated lesions, 96% were moderately or severely calcified, with a mean diameter stenosis of 81% and chronic total occlusions present in 20% of lesions. Despite this, serious angiographic complications at final imaging were observed in only 1.3% of patients.

“Successfully treating heavily calcified lesions begins with being able to facilitate lesion crossing, an enduring challenge that can limit what physicians can achieve for patients,” said Robert Yeh, M.D., MBA, global co-principal investigator of the study and Section Chief, Interventional Cardiology, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.

“These findings represent an important step toward overcoming that barrier and creating a viable treatment path for patients whose disease may be beyond the reach of conventional balloon-based calcium modification approaches.”
Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of death globally, affecting an estimated 315 million people worldwide and approximately 1 in 20 adults over the age of 20 in the U.S.

. In CAD, the buildup of cholesterol-rich deposits results in narrowing of the coronary arteries, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle. Among lesions that cannot be crossed with a balloon, more than 75% have moderate to severe calcification.

“The FORWARD CAD IDE study shows that difficult to cross lesions may be treated successfully without compromising safety,” said James Spratt, M.D., global co-principal investigator of the study and FRCP, St. George’s University NHS Trust.[vi] “This study suggests that Javelin could help physicians manage patients with limited treatment options.”

a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study conducted in 28 sites in the U.S. and U.K. The study enrolled 158 patients with severely stenosed, de novo calcified coronary artery lesions with moderate to severe calcification defined by angiography and either over 90% stenosis with lesion length <40mm or a chronic total occlusion (CTO) and a J_CTO score of 1. The co-global principal investigators of the study are Robert Yeh, M.D., MBA, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and James Spratt, M.D., FRCP, St. George’s University NHS Trust, and the U.S. principal investigator is Robert Riley, M.D., FACC, Overlake Medical Center & Clinics.

The investigational Shockwave Javelin Coronary IVL platform is designed with a single distal emitter that creates ultrasonic acoustic pressure waves, with a spherical energy field that extends beyond the tip of the catheter. – Johnson & Johnson announced results from three clinical analyses being presented during the Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics annual scientific symposium (TCT 2026) that report positive survival and patient outcomes data when Impella™ heart pumps are used to support a patient’s heart during and after high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (HRPCI). Real-world and observational registry data from 1,379 HRPCI patients across hospitals in the U.S. and Europe show lower in-hospital cardiovascular mortality and lower 30- and 90-day mortality rates than those recently reported in CHIP-BCIS3. These contemporary findings from real-world U.S. and European experience with Impella-supported HRPCI provide important clinical context in contrast to the CHIP-BCIS3 study results.

“Data from these high-impact presentations add to more than two decades of evidence supporting Impella use in complex HRPCI patients,” said Navin Kapur, M.D., chief medical and scientific officer, Heart Recovery, MedTech, Johnson & Johnson. “They also reinforce that outcomes depend not only on the device but how and when it is used, from selecting the right patients and procedural approach to post-procedural management and critical care.”
The following data will be presented during TCT:
TCT 197: Protected PCI with Microaxial-Flow Pump Support: Real-World Evidence from the TRI-GUARD-PCI Registry (Matthias Bossard, M.D., 11/1/26; 11 a.m. PST, station 4).

This multicenter analysis of 279 patients undergoing elective protected PCI with Impella at hospitals in Germany, Switzerland and Austria showed lower 30-day (6.1%) and 180-day (7.9%) all-cause mortality rates than previously reported in the CHIP-BCIS3 trial Kaplan-Meier curve.
“These real-world results provide important insights into outcomes following Impella-supported high-risk PCI in contemporary clinical practice,” said Matthias Bossard, M.D.

, an interventional cardiologist and researcher now at Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia, who conducted this research while at the Heart Center at Luzerner Kantonsspital in Lucerne, Switzerland, in collaboration with Mohamed Ayoub, MD, from Germany. “The findings may help inform patient selection and procedural planning for complex high-risk interventions.”
TCT 888: Peri-procedural and Early Post-Procedural Cardiovascular Mortality Following HRPCI (Vasileios Panoulas, M.D., 11/2/26, 1 p.m. PST, station 2).

Using a multicenter U.S. registry, this analysis of 522 patients who underwent Impella-supported HRPCI showed cardiovascular mortality of 3.4% at time of discharge compared with approximately 8% in the CHIP-BCIS3 study for patients treated with Impella on day 4 post-randomization. Kaplan-Meier curve estimates of cardiovascular mortality were 4.7% at 30 days and 6.5% at 90 days—both numerically lower than the corresponding rates reported in CHIP-BCIS3.
“This analysis provides real-world perspective on the use of Impella during HRPCI and highlights differences from the CHIP-BCIS3 study protocol,” said Vasileios Panoulas, M.D.,

physician at Royal Brompton and Harefield Hospitals in London and the abstract’s lead author. In the CHIP-BCIS3 treatment arm, the device was removed before patients left the catheterization lab whereas in the LOQI study, one in six patients were supported by Impella for more than three hours. “These observations suggest a potential relationship between duration of support, post-procedural management and patient outcomes,” adds Panoulas.

TCT 1228: Clinical Characteristics and Early Mortality in a High-Risk PCI Cohort Similar to CHIP-BCIS3 Undergoing Impella Support: Insights from PROTECT III (Vasileios Panoulas, M.D., 11/3/26, 8:50 a.m. PST, station 10).

This analysis identified patients enrolled in the PROTECT III study who would meet the study entry criteria for the CHIP-BCIS3 trial. The in-hospital all-cause mortality for those 578 Impella-supported patients was 4.7%, which is lower than the estimated ~8% mortality reported in CHIP-BCIS3.

“In the high-risk PROTECT III cohort, Impella-supported HRPCI was performed in patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction and complex coronary anatomy, including frequent left main and multivessel treatment, with lower mortality rates than reported in CHIP-BCIS3,” said Panoulas

, who is presenting this data at TCT. “Understanding mortality after HRPCI requires looking at patient risk at baseline, procedural complexity and the importance of post-procedure patient management.”

– Johnson & Johnson announces a record 26 presentations featuring the clinical science of Impella™ heart pumps will be presented at the Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics (TCT) 2026 conference, taking place Oct. 31–Nov. 3 in San Diego. The breadth of research reflects the company’s continued leadership in generating rigorous clinical evidence to advance the science of heart recovery and improve outcomes for patients facing complex and life-threatening cardiovascular conditions.

Johnson & Johnson MedTech’s robust body of clinical evidence in heart recovery spans more than two decades, including randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective studies, registries and real-world clinical practice. More than 50,000 Impella patients have been studied, and more than 450,000 patients worldwide have been treated with Impella. This evidence base includes approximately 2,700 peer-reviewed publications and has contributed to the recognition of temporary mechanical circulatory support with Impella in 18 clinical guidelines and consensus statements.

Impella clinical data being presented at TCT builds on that scientific foundation and includes new research from centers around the world across high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (HRPCI), cardiogenic shock, myocardial recovery, renal perfusion, physiologic risk and next-generation technology. Among the presentations are three analyses of contemporary U.S. and European experience with Impella-supported HRPCI that provide important clinical context in contrast to the CHIP-BCIS3 study results.

“Scientific leadership requires sustained investment, rigorous evaluation of high-quality data, and a willingness to continually improve how we care for patients,” said Navin Kapur, M.D., chief medical and scientific officer, Heart Recovery, MedTech, Johnson & Johnson. “The record 26 Impella abstracts at TCT reflect our commitment to partnering with the clinical community to generate the evidence needed to advance understanding, inform best practices and help physicians deliver better outcomes for patients worldwide.”

In addition, a novel health-economic model projecting lower lifetime healthcare costs and greater quality-adjusted survival with Impella compared with Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump in heart failure patients undergoing HRPCI will be presented.

CINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) reported first quarter fiscal year 2027 net sales of $23.3 billion, an increase of four percent versus the prior year. Organic sales, which excludes the impacts of foreign exchange and acquisitions and divestitures, also increased four percent versus the prior year. Diluted net earnings per share were $1.97, an increase of one percent versus prior year as the increase in net sales was partially offset by an increase in operating costs. Core earnings per share were $2.00, an increase of one percent versus the prior year.

Operating cash flow was $5.8 billion, and net earnings were $4.8 billion for the quarter. Free cash flow productivity was 93%. Free cash flow productivity is calculated as operating cash flow less capital spending, as a percentage of net earnings. The Company returned $3.9 billion of cash to shareowners via $2.6 billion of dividend payments and $1.3 billion of share repurchases.
*Please refer to Exhibit 1 - Non-GAAP Measures for the definition and reconciliation of these measures to the related GAAP measures.

“Our solid sales, earnings and cash results in the first quarter reflect sharpened execution of our integrated strategy,” said Shailesh Jejurikar, Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer. “While we expect there will continue to be geopolitical and economic challenges, this strong start keeps us on track to deliver within our guidance ranges for organic sales growth, core EPS growth and free cash flow productivity for the fiscal year. We remain committed to our strategy to delight consumers with superior products at a superior value by putting the consumer first in everything we do. We are confident in the near term and excited about the future.”

Net sales in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 were $23.3 billion, a four percent increase versus the prior year. Organic sales, which exclude the impacts of foreign exchange and acquisitions and divestitures, also increased four percent driven by a two percent increase from volume and a one percent increase from favorable mix. Pricing had a minor positive impact on sales for the quarter.
Net sales percentage changes are approximations based on quantitative formulas that are consistently applied.
Acquisitions and Divestitures excluding volume impact.

Beauty segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago. Hair Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by innovation-based pricing in North America and Latin America, favorable product mix and an increase in unit volume. Personal Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by volume growth in Greater China and Europe and favorable product mix, partially offset by trade investments. Skin Care organic sales increased mid-single digits due to favorable premium product mix and a unit volume increase in North America.
Grooming segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago driven by innovation-based pricing, primarily in North America and IMETA, and favorable product mix.

Health Care segment organic sales increased three percent versus year ago. Oral Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by premium product mix and innovation-based pricing, partially offset by a unit volume decline. Personal Health Care organic sales increased low single digits due to higher pricing, primarily in North America and Latin America, and favorable product mix, partially offset by a unit volume decline.

Fabric and Home Care segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago. Fabric Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by volume increases in North America and Europe and favorable geographic mix. Home Care organic sales also increased mid-single digits driven by volume increases in North America and Europe and favorable product mix.

Baby, Feminine and Family Care segment organic sales increased three percent versus year ago. Baby Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by a unit volume increase, primarily in Greater China and North America, and favorable premium product mix, partially offset by lower pricing, primarily in North America. Feminine Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by favorable product mix and innovation-based pricing, primarily in North America, partially offset by a unit volume decline in Europe. Family Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by a unit volume increase, partially offset by merchandising investments.
Diluted net earnings per share increased by one percent to $1.97. Core earnings per share increased one percent to $2.00 and Currency-neutral Core EPS was unchanged versus the prior year.

Reported gross margin for the quarter decreased 160 basis points versus the prior year. Core gross margin and currency-neutral Core gross margin for the quarter decreased 150 basis points versus the prior year and excluded the impact from incremental restructuring charges. The decrease was driven by 140 basis points of higher costs from commodities, 140 basis points of product reinvestments, 50 basis points of unfavorable mix and 10 basis points of rounding and other items, partially offset by 120 basis points of gross productivity savings, 50 basis points of tariff impact from lower costs and recognized recoveries and 20 basis points of increased pricing.

Reported selling, general and administrative expense (SG&A) as a percentage of sales declined 90 basis points versus year ago. Core SG&A as a percentage of sales decreased 80 basis points versus year ago and decreased 70 basis points on a currency-neutral basis. Core SG&A excluded the impact from incremental restructuring charges. The decline was driven by 130 basis points of productivity savings and 100 basis points of net sales growth leverage, partially offset by 120 basis points of reinvestments and 40 basis points of rounding and other items.

Reported operating margin for the quarter decreased 70 basis points versus the prior year. Excluding the impact of non-core restructuring charges, core operating margin decreased 80 basis points versus the prior year and decreased 90 basis points on a currency-neutral basis. Core operating margin included gross productivity savings of 250 basis points.

P&G updated its guidance range for fiscal 2027 all-in sales growth to be in the range of two to four percent versus the prior year, reflecting the acquisition of Thorne as of October 1, 2026. The Company maintained its outlook for organic sales growth in the range of one to three percent versus the prior year. Included in the organic sales growth guidance is a headwind of 30 to 50 basis points from brand, product form and go-to-market discontinuations.

P&G maintained its fiscal 2027 diluted net earnings per share growth to be in the range of one to five percent versus fiscal 2026 diluted net EPS of $6.62. P&G also maintained its fiscal 2027 core earnings per share growth to be in the range of in-line to three percent versus fiscal 2026 core EPS of $6.89. This outlook equates to a range of $6.89 to $7.11 per share, with a mid-point estimate of $7.00, or an increase of approximately one and a half percent.

P&G now expects a commodity cost headwind of approximately $1.4 billion after tax driven by higher raw materials, energy and transportation costs, $300 million after-tax from higher net interest expense, $150 million after-tax from lower non-operating income and $50 million after-tax from unfavorable foreign exchange rates. Combined, these impacts equate to a headwind of $0.79 per share for fiscal 2027, or an eleven percent drag on core EPS growth.

Porsha Williams partners with Charmin to encourage consumers to raise their standards with Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest innovation in more than a decade.
Charmin introduces new Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade.
Distinguished by its 3D durable weave texture, the new Charmin Ultra Strong now has wider sheets that clean better so you can use up to 50% less*

Porsha Williams is teaming up with Charmin to help raise toilet paper standards, bringing the brand's wider-sheet innovation to life through social content and an immersive New York City experience where consumers can discover the difference for themselves.

CINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Today, Charmin unveils the new Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade. Designed to deliver a better clean, new Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets replaces the existing Ultra Strong product line with a wider-sheet design that provides more coverage and helps consumers use up to 50% less* toilet paper. Built on the belief that better changes everything, the innovation is designed to challenge what consumers expect from their toilet paper by delivering an upgrade consumers didn’t know they needed.

For many shoppers, toilet paper has long been a category where people settle for what's familiar, but Charmin wants to challenge that notion. Featuring its signature 3D diamond weave texture, Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets aims to raise the bar for what consumers should expect from their toilet paper. By combining greater coverage with the strength and durability people already love, the innovation creates an upgraded experience that redefines what “good enough” should look and feel like in the bathroom. That’s what happens when you get the upgrade you didn’t know you needed - better changes everything.

"Consumers may not think to ask for a wider sheet, but they do know a better clean when they feel it. With Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, we've taken something people use every day and made it meaningfully better by delivering more coverage, a better clean, and helping consumers use less,” said Alex Perez, Charmin Brand Vice President, Procter & Gamble. “For years, Ultra Strong has provided consumers strength and durability. Now, Charmin is building on that legacy with an innovation designed to redefine what consumers should expect from their toilet paper. Charmin Ultra Strong truly delivers a differentiated clean that consumers can’t unfeel.”

To help raise these toilet paper standards, Charmin is partnering with media personality, entrepreneur and Charmin loyalist Porsha Williams. She will be involved in the brand’s social campaign and will serve as the host of Charmin’s Wider Sheet immersive NYC experience on October 20. Visitors can join in on the fun by snapping photos with a one-of-a-kind Charmin vehicle inspired by the brand's campaign, meet the beloved Charmin bears and get up close with the new Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets to see the difference for themselves.

“Listen, I’m not someone who settles for basic, so why would I do it with my toilet paper?” said Porsha Williams. “When I tried Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, I was mad nobody told me sooner. More coverage, a better clean, AND using less? That’s the kind of upgrade I can get behind. And honestly? Your backside will thank you."

General Motors delivered another solid quarter of earnings, driven by the appeal of our product portfolio, the agility of our team, and disciplined execution.

Our employees, our dealers and our suppliers are all making important contributions that continue to drive our success. Their commitment enables us to win in a dynamic market, and their efforts are leading us to raise our 2026 guidance for the second time.

The business continues to perform very well. Customer demand in North America remains strong driven by our very attractive lineup of pickups and SUVs. Pricing is consistent, and we delivered the best quarter and first half ever for new Super Cruise-equipped vehicles.

Our 8.6% EBIT-adjusted margin in North America was up 2.5 points from a year ago, and we continue to lower our warranty costs, reduce EV losses, and increase operating efficiency. In addition, GM International, inclusive of our China joint ventures, was profitable.
We expect these trends will continue to strengthen our performance into 2027 and beyond because we have multiple engines of margin expansion and growth while maintaining our capital discipline.
Our vehicle portfolio continues to get stronger, with the launch of the next-generation Chevrolet Silverado LD and GMC Sierra LD starting in December
Our software and services ecosystem is expanding
Our manufacturing and sourcing footprint is becoming more efficient, and we will be onshoring significant production to further reduce our tariff exposure
And growth businesses like GM Defense and GM Insurance are creating additional avenues for value creation

All of this supports our commitment to ongoing margin expansion. We know there’s more work ahead, but we are building from a position of strength with a proven track record of execution, and I’d like to thank you for your continued confidence in the General Motors team.

Joint venture would combine Aramco’s subsurface knowledge, advanced AI tools, and powerful computational capabilities with Maaden’s mining and mineral exploration expertise
Exploration activities to mainly focus on copper, alongside other energy transition minerals, in a zone equivalent to nearly 10% of Saudi Arabia’s total land area
Joint venture aims to accelerate discovery, advancing Saudi Arabia’s role in the global energy transition value chain

Aramco, one of the world’s leading integrated energy and chemicals companies, and Maaden, one of the world’s fastest‑growing mining companies and the largest multi‑commodity mining and metals producer in the Middle East, today announced the signing of a shareholders’ agreement to form a Joint Venture (JV) to unlock new opportunities in mineral exploration and hard-rock mining in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Combining the strengths of two leaders in their respective fields, the JV would focus on copper and other minerals critical to the energy transition. Plans for the JV were first disclosed in January 2025.

The JV is expected to be owned 51% by Maaden and 49% by Aramco and would focus on exploration across Zone-4, also known as the Transition Zone, within the Arabian Platform. It represents a major new opportunity for mineral discovery in the Kingdom. Spanning approximately 182,000 square kilometers, nearly 10% of Saudi Arabia’s total land area, the expected exploration area stretches along a 100-kilometer-wide zone running parallel to the Arabian Shield.
Saleh M. Al Saleh, Aramco Vice President of Transition Minerals, said:

“Over 90 years, Aramco has accumulated and analyzed the largest amount of geological and geophysical data ever acquired in a single basin for the Kingdom. This partnership intends to leverage this legacy information to find minerals in the JV area within the basin. Maaden’s expertise, our people, high-performance computing, and AI are expected to play a pivotal role in accelerating the discovery of key transition minerals at low cost.”
Darryl Clark, Maaden Executive Vice President for Exploration, said:

“Maaden has been advancing one of the world’s largest single jurisdiction exploration programs across the Arabian Shield to help unlock the Kingdom’s mineral potential. This joint venture would take that ambition into a new area. By combining Maaden’s exploration and development expertise with Aramco’s extraordinary knowledge of the Arabian Platform, we would have an opportunity to move faster, explore smarter, and create new opportunities to discover the minerals that will power the energy transition.”

Copper, which is increasingly significant for electric vehicles, power networks, energy storage, and renewable energy systems, would be a main focus of the JV. Copper is a major metal making up over 20% of the $1.2 trillion mined metals market. The copper market is currently valued at approximately $250 billion and is projected to grow to over $400 billion by 2035. The JV would also explore for other energy transition minerals including zinc, lead, and rare earth elements that are expected to be crucial to industries of the future.

Leveraging advanced computational algorithms, AI, and high-performance computing, the JV intends to target areas most likely to contain copper and valuable minerals, accelerating the path from regional screening to target definition and discovery. This is expected to support long-term sector development, reinforce the Kingdom’s role in the global minerals value chain, and help meet rising demand for transition minerals.

The effectiveness of the shareholders’ agreement and the incorporation of the JV is conditional upon the fulfillment of certain condition precedents, including, but not limited to, obtaining all the required corporate and regulatory approvals and antitrust clearance.

Acquisition-related items include amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, substantially all of which relate to the amortization of technology-based intangible assets that is recorded in cost of revenues and will recur in future periods until the related intangible assets have been fully amortized. We view acquisition-related intangible assets as items arising from pre-acquisition activities determined at the time of an acquisition. Acquisition-related intangible assets contribute to revenue generation that has not been excluded from our Non-GAAP financial information. Acquisition-related items also include recognition of the step-up of inventories and property, plant and equipment to fair value and the related tax effects of acquisition-related items, as well as any effects from restructuring the ownership of such acquired assets. We also exclude the operating results of acquired and/or consolidated businesses that, as of close, are expected or required to be sold. Additionally, we exclude certain other acquisition-related charges such as third-party acquisition and integration services costs and costs related to temporary debt facilities and letters of credit executed prior to the close of an acquisition.

We exclude certain other items that we view as unrelated to our ongoing businesses, such as major restructuring and restructuring-related costs, asset impairments and awards, settlements and/or damages arising from legal or regulatory matters. We exclude gains and losses driven by the revaluation of our deferred compensation plan liabilities recognized in operating expenses and the offsetting gains and losses on the related plan assets recognized in investment and other income (expense).

Megafactory Texas began production, with planned capacity of 50 GWh. We also advanced LFP supply domestication in the U.S., shipping the first Megapacks built with LFP cells from our factory in Nevada. We continue to invest in the future through R&D and Capex spend across our businesses, including SI, robotics and energy. Much hard work lies ahead, but we are as optimistic as ever. Thank you to our supporters as we continue to execute on many challenging and important projects. Automotive We achieved record quarterly deliveries in several markets, including Canada, Australia, Japan and Taiwan. Given the strong demand we are seeing across various markets, we remain focused on increasing production across our factories and attained record production at Gigafactory Berlin. We began volume production of Tesla Semi, our Class 8 heavy-duty truck. The top variant can go 500 miles at full 82,000 lbs gross combination weight while achieving an efficiency of 1.7 kWh/mile. Energy Generation and Storage We began production at Megafactory Texas. Energy storage demand is increasingly aligned with SI infrastructure demand as grid constraints and power availability create more opportunities for Megapack to be deployed. Megapack excels in off-grid and on-grid applications, supplying large data center loads, buffering oscillating demand, helping interconnection grid-compliance and strengthening the grid – all with less local fossil fuel generation. Robotics Optimus production began in Fremont on our high-volume lines. The bots coming off this line are the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured. While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product. 6

"Free cash flow" is operating cash flow less capital expenditures. Average cost per vehicle is cost of automotive sales divided by new vehicle deliveries (excluding operating leases). “Days sales outstanding” is equal to (i) average accounts receivable, net for the period divided by (ii) total revenues and multiplied by (iii) the number of days in the period. “Days payable outstanding” is equal to (i) average accounts payable for the period divided by (ii) total cost of revenues and multiplied by (iii) the number of days in the period. “Days of supply” is calculated by dividing new car ending inventory by the relevant period's deliveries and using trading days. Constant currency impacts are calculated by comparing actuals against current results converted into USD using average exchange rates from the prior period. NON-GAAP FINANCIAL INFORMATION Consolidated financial information has been presented in accordance with GAAP as well as on a non-GAAP basis to supplement our consolidated financial results. Our non-GAAP financial measures include non-GAAP net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders, non-GAAP net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders on a diluted per share basis (calculated using weighted average shares for GAAP diluted net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders), Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, non-GAAP automotive gross margin and free cash flow. These non-GAAP financial measures also facilitate management’s internal comparisons to Tesla’s historical performance as well as comparisons to the operating results of other companies. Reported earnings increased compared to third quarter 2025 primarily due to reliable operations with higher margins on refined product sales and higher crude oil realizations, partially offset by unfavorable timing effects resulting from the rising price environment.

Production in the third quarter of 2026 was lower than a year ago primarily due to lower entitlements from higher prices and impacts from the Middle East conflict, partly offset by record production at operated assets in Australia, higher production in the Gulf of America and the inclusion of one month of Venezuela production following a change to equity accounting in the quarter.
U.S. refinery crude unit throughput set a new record of 1.09 million barrels per day, reflecting reliable crude unit capacity utilization of nearly 98 percent.

Cash flow from operations in the third quarter of 2026 was higher than a year ago, driven by higher earnings and increased cash distributions from Tengizchevroil LLP (TCO). Adjusted free cash flow benefited from a $1 billion loan repayment from TCO and proceeds from asset sales.
Capex in the third quarter of 2026 was lower than last year largely due to lower spend in the Permian Basin.
Total debt was reduced by an additional $3.5 billion and net debt was down $7.8 billion in the quarter, further strengthening Chevron’s balance sheet.

The company’s Board of Directors declared a quarterly dividend of one dollar and seventy-eight cents ($1.78) per share, payable December 10, 2026, to all holders of common stock as shown on the transfer records of the corporation at the close of business on November 18,
Improved commercial terms and expanded acreage in Venezuela, supporting future investments and the potential to more than double production over the next five years.

Announced plans to continue to strengthen the competitiveness of the company’s Bakken upstream operations by reducing midstream costs by approximately 50 percent and increasing operational flexibility.
Announced an offshore crude oil and natural gas condensate discovery in Angola’s prolific Lower Congo Basin, demonstrating the potential of the company’s exploration program in sub-Saharan Africa.
Signed an exploration agreement with Libya’s National Oil Corporation in the Sirte Basin, advancing Chevron’s North Africa upstream growth strategy and exploration portfolio.
Started production at the new Bunge Chevron Ag Renewables LLC oilseed-processing facility in Destrehan, Louisiana, supplying additional feedstocks for transportation fuels.
Completed the sale of the Cambodia downstream fuels business.

U.S. upstream earnings were higher than a year ago primarily due to higher liquids realizations and lower operating expenses, including the absence of prior year severance and transaction costs related to the Hess Corporation (Hess) acquisition.
Net oil-equivalent production during the quarter was up 3,000 barrels per day
from the year-ago period. The increase was primarily due to higher
production in the Gulf of America following project ramp-ups at Ballymore, Whale and Anchor, partly offset by lower production in the Bakken.

International upstream earnings were higher than a year ago primarily due to higher realizations and higher liftings in Venezuela, partly offset by unfavorable timing effects, unfavorable taxes, unfavorable foreign currency effects, a legal reserve and an impairment charge.

Net oil-equivalent production during the quarter was down 109,000 barrels per day from the year-ago period primarily due to lower entitlements from higher prices and impacts from the conflict in the Middle East, partly offset by record production at operated assets in Australia and the inclusion of one month of Venezuela production following the switch to equity accounting.

primarily due to higher margins on refined product sales.

Refined product sales were relatively flat compared to the year-ago period.

Refinery crude unit inputs were relatively flat from the year-ago period.

Chevron to Divest its Ownership Interests in Hess Midstream and DJ Basin Crude Midstream Assets
Chevron to divest its ownership interests in Hess Midstream and DJ Basin crude oil midstream assets in exchange for extended and improved Bakken midstream commercial terms
Expected to improve Chevron’s Bakken cost structure and increase return on capital employed

— Chevron Corporation (NYSE: CVX) announced today that several of its subsidiaries have entered into a series of definitive agreements with Hess Midstream LP (NYSE: HESM) to restructure the terms of its Bakken midstream contracts and establish new DJ Basin midstream contracts. The revised agreements extend the Bakken contracts and are expected to reduce Chevron's Bakken unit midstream costs by approximately 50%, enhancing future earnings and return on capital employed. In exchange for the improved long-term commercial framework and $200 million in cash consideration, Chevron will transfer to Hess Midstream its ownership interests and general partner position in Hess Midstream, as well as its DJ Basin crude oil midstream assets.

As part of this transaction, Chevron expects to fully deconsolidate Hess Midstream, including approximately $3.7 billion of Hess Midstream's debt. Chevron expects this transaction to be accretive to return on capital employed by 0.5% on an absolute basis and generate long-term future economic value through a lower cost structure and improved earnings. At closing, Chevron expects to recognize a one-time after-tax loss estimated at approximately $3 to $4 billion,
given that the company is unable to recognize future Bakken midstream cost savings as an asset.

“This transaction resets the commercial framework between our upstream and midstream assets in the Bakken and DJ Basins,” said Andy Walz, Chevron’s President of Downstream, Midstream and Chemicals. “It lowers our Bakken cost structure while positioning Hess Midstream to advance as an independent company.” Chevron expects to sustain Bakken production through ongoing technology deployment and operational improvements drawn from its global shale and tight portfolio.
Expected to be treated as a special item.

The transaction has been approved by the Conflicts Committee of the Board of Directors of the general partner of Hess Midstream, comprised entirely of independent directors, following consultation with its independent legal and financial advisors. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals and is expected to close by year-end 2026.

BofA Securities is acting as financial advisor and Latham & Watkins LLP is acting as legal advisor to Chevron. Evercore is acting as financial advisor and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP is acting as legal advisor to the Conflicts Committee of the Board of Directors of the general partner of Hess Midstream.

Strategy and outlook update on 15 December.
We will set out the next phase of our plans to build a simpler, stronger and more valuable bp.
“These are dynamic times with volatility and disruption to trade flows continuing to define energy markets.

The industry as a whole has been showing remarkable adaptability. Refineries have been running close to capacity to make up for shortfalls, shipping has been taking different and longer routes, and releases from strategic and commercial reserves are helping to bridge supply gaps.

I’m proud of the contribution bp is making to keep energy flowing. As a global integrated oil and gas company, our connectivity from the reservoir to the fuel pump is a significant source of strength and resilience, particularly given our ability to connect supply with demand.

We maintained upstream production at around 2.2 million barrels per day, upstream plant reliability and refining availability both improved compared to the previous quarter, and our trading performance was also higher.

This has generated a strong set of results, supported by the higher-price, higher-margin environment and some good progress on performance improvement across the business. Our underlying replacement cost profit for the quarter was $8.5 billion and operating cash flow was $14.8 billion, contributing to a reduction of $8.4 billion in net debt.
We have now delivered our net debt and structural cost reductions targets and have line of sight on the remaining two of the four primary financial targets we set ourselves for 2027.

Last week we announced an important step as we agreed with the State of Louisiana to accelerate the delivery of our Deepwater Horizon settlement commitments. Our intent is now to prioritize the use of excess cashflow to address our remaining Deepwater Horizon liabilities in full.

Deepwater Horizon was a tragedy. Eleven men lost their lives, and communities and the environment across the Gulf Coast were impacted. We will never forget - it changed bp. Its legacy guides us in how we operate today, with safety at the heart of everything we do.

And as we move forward, we will continue working with urgency to turn one good set of results into strong performance quarter after quarter. We have much more to do on the five priorities set out at mid-year to deliver a step change in performance and realize the full potential of this company.

The combined sum of bp’s net debt, hybrids, lease liabilities and Gulf of America settlement liabilities is down by $9.3 billion compared with the second quarter of the year. This is good progress, but we are still too leveraged and further strengthening of the balance sheet remains our number one job. Our goal is a strong balance sheet that, through the cycle, supports the dividend and disciplined investment in service of delivering value to shareholders.

We are moving at speed to simplify bp’s portfolio to assets that best fit our integrated model and deliver the most competitive cash and returns. In the quarter we agreed the sale of our Austrian mobility and convenience business, completed the sale of the Gelsenkirchen refinery, and announced plans to market our North Sea and Archaea businesses. Still to come is the expected imminent closure of the Castrol divestment, unlocking $6 billion to further strengthen the balance sheet.

We have also de-risked exploration and production prospects in Brazil, the Gulf of America and Iraq by bringing in partners. In Venezuela we signed agreements for offshore gas production close to our LNG facilities in Trinidad. We are being rigorous about where we put capital and focusing on the most competitive opportunities. But this quarter we recognized $4.0 billion of impairments linked largely to transition businesses; we know we need to be better stewards of our shareholders' capital.

And in refining this quarter, availability and utilization improved and unit operating costs were down, unlocking greater value from our assets. This improvement needs to be sustained quarter on quarter and replicated across the company.

Senior leaders came together last month to hold up the mirror on past performance, challenge ways of working, and make new commitments on clearer accountabilities and better, faster data-based decision-making. We are giving our people clarity on the work they own, what they are expected to deliver and how success will be measured – supported by a much simpler governance and organizational structure that includes the return to upstream and downstream businesses.

Our goal is to be a resilient business that delivers strong performance in all price environments and grows long-term value for our shareholders. In December we will set out our longer-term plans and capital frame, alongside metrics and targets against which our performance can be judged as we continue to build a simpler, stronger, more valuable bp.
