Looking ahead, bp expects fourth quarter 2026 reported upstream production to be 2,090 to 2,230mboe/d. This includes the impact of continued disruption in the Middle East, activity phasing in bpx energy, seasonally lower gas demand and around 20mboe/d for a weather event in the Gulf of America, partly offset by the recovery from outages. The heightened volatility in the oil and gas prices could also impact PSA contracts.

In its customers business, compared to the third quarter, bp expects a significantly lower result with seasonally lower volumes, a lower midstream result and lower Castrol earnings, subject to the anticipated completion of the divestment. Fuels margins and midstream performance are expected to remain sensitive to market conditions.

In products, bp expects throughput of 1,160-1,210mb/d, reflecting the absence of Gelsenkirchen for the full quarter following its divestment on 31 July and higher maintenance activity. Refining margins are expected to remain elevated and sensitive to the cost of supply and market conditions.
bp expects income taxes paid in the fourth quarter to be around $0.8 billion higher than the third quarter 2026 mainly due to the impact of higher profits on instalment payments.

bp now expects reported upstream production to be 2,210 to 2,250mboe/d, compared with the 2025, 2,312mboe/d. This includes the impact of disruption in the Middle East, the divestment of the Culzean gas field in the UK North Sea and bp's reduced equity interest in Latin America.

In its customers business, bp expects to make continued progress growing cash flows, supported by lower underlying operating expenditure* driven by structural cost reductions*. These benefits will be partly offset by the earnings impact of completed and announced divestments. Reported earnings will benefit from lower depreciation as a result of the assets held for sale accounting treatment of Castrol following the planned divestment. Fuel margins are expected to remain sensitive to conditions and developments in the Middle East and any resulting policy responses.

In products, bp expects throughput of 1,390 to 1,400mb/d, reflecting the completion of the Gelsenkirchen divestment and a significantly lower level of planned turnaround activity. Refining margins are expected to remain sensitive to the cost of supply and market conditions.
bp continues to expect other businesses & corporate underlying annual charge to be around $1.0 billion for 2026. The charge may vary quarter to quarter.
bp continues to expect the depreciation, depletion and amortization to be $17.0-17.5 billion.

bp now expects the underlying ETR* for 2026 to be between 31% and 34%, which reflects the underlying ETR for the nine months of 31%. It is sensitive to a range of factors, including the volatility of the price environment and its impact on the geographical mix of the group’s profits and losses.
bp continues to expect capital expenditure to be $13.5-14.0 billion.
bp now expects divestment and other proceeds to be around $8 billion in 2026, including approximately $6 billion from the announced Castrol divestment.

bp continues to expect Gulf of America settlement payments for the year to be around $1.6 billion pre-tax including $0.4 billion pre-tax paid during the first quarter and $1.1 billion pre-tax paid during the second quarter. The timing of the payment of the recently announced $350 million settlement with the US state of Louisiana is still to be determined.

In August, bp agreed to acquire Woodside Energy’s 70% interest in Block TTDAA 14, the Calypso gas project in Trinidad and Tobago, increasing bp’s stake to 100% and assuming operatorship. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals.

In August, bp and the government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela signed agreements to advance offshore gas development, including the award of an exploration and production licence for Phase 2 of the Loran field in the Plataforma Deltana area. Loran Phase 2 contains an estimated 4 trillion cubic feet of recoverable gas resources.

In September, bp completed the farm down in Indonesia, of a 50% participating interest in the bp operated Agung I and Agung II exploration blocks to INPEX, reducing bp’s working interest to 50%.

Considerations in respect of ongoing geopolitical instability in the Middle East and impact on the economic environment

The impact of ongoing geopolitical instability in the Middle East and the associated economic developments have been considered for the basis of preparation for the interim financial information. Such factors include the economic effect of price volatility, supply disruptions in the region, operability of producing assets and discount rates.

As a result of ongoing geopolitical instability in the Middle East and the related economic impact, the group’s value-in-use impairment testing price assumptions for Brent oil and Henry Hub gas were revised during the third quarter from those disclosed in the

, and also revised since the second quarter 2026. The group has updated its estimate of Brent oil prices to $87/bbl (previously $70/bbl) and Henry Hub gas prices to $3.18/mmBtu (previously $3.80/mmBtu) in real 2024 terms on an average basis for the full year 2026. With reference to the Brent price, this estimate assumes ongoing supply disruptions resulting from geopolitical instability in the Middle East into 2027. With regard to the Henry Hub gas price assumption, the price decrease is based on an expectation of strong production growth for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027 in the US domestic market. No material impairment or reversal of impairment arose in the third quarter 2026 interim period as a result of the changes to these commodity price assumptions. are non-IFRS adjustments to our IFRS profit (loss). They reflect the difference between the way bp manages the economic exposure and internally measures performance of certain activities and the way those activities are measured under IFRS. Fair value accounting effects are included within adjusting items. They relate to certain of the group's commodity, interest rate and currency risk exposures as detailed below. Other than as noted below, the fair value accounting effects described are reported in both the gas & low carbon energy and customer & products segments.

bp uses derivative instruments to manage the economic exposure relating to inventories above normal operating requirements of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products. Under IFRS, these inventories are recorded at historical cost. The related derivative instruments, however, are required to be recorded at fair value with gains and losses recognized in the income statement. This is because hedge accounting is either not permitted or not followed, principally due to the impracticality of effectiveness-testing requirements. Therefore, measurement differences in relation to recognition of gains and losses occur. Gains and losses on these inventories, other than net realizable value provisions, are not recognized until the commodity is sold in a subsequent accounting period. Gains and losses on the related derivative commodity contracts are recognized in the income statement, from the time the derivative commodity contract is entered into, on a fair value basis using forward prices consistent with the contract maturity.

bp enters into physical commodity contracts to meet certain business requirements, such as the purchase of crude for a refinery or the sale of bp’s gas production. Under IFRS these physical contracts are treated as derivatives and are required to be fair valued when they are managed as part of a larger portfolio of similar transactions. Gains and losses arising are recognized in the income statement from the time the derivative commodity contract is entered into.

IFRS require that inventory held for trading is recorded at its fair value using period-end spot prices, whereas any related derivative commodity instruments are required to be recorded at values based on forward prices consistent with the contract maturity. Depending on market conditions, these forward prices can be either higher or lower than spot prices, resulting in measurement differences.

bp enters into contracts for pipelines and other transportation, storage capacity, oil and gas processing, liquefied natural gas (LNG) and certain gas and power contracts that, under IFRS, are recorded on an accruals basis. These contracts are risk-managed using a variety of derivative instruments that are fair valued under IFRS. This results in measurement differences in relation to recognition of gains and losses.

The way that bp manages the economic exposures described above, and measures performance internally, differs from the way these activities are measured under IFRS. bp calculates this difference for consolidated entities by comparing the IFRS result with management’s internal measure of performance. We believe that disclosing management’s estimate of this difference provides useful information for investors because it enables investors to see the economic effect of these activities as a whole.

Under management’s internal measure of performance the inventory, transportation and capacity contracts in question are valued based on fair value using relevant forward prices prevailing at the end of the period.

Fair value accounting effects also include changes in the fair value of the near-term portions of LNG contracts that fall within bp’s risk management framework. LNG contracts are not considered derivatives, because there is insufficient market liquidity, and they are therefore accrual accounted under IFRS. However, oil and natural gas derivative financial instruments used to risk manage the near-term portions of the LNG contracts are fair valued under IFRS. The fair value accounting effect, which is reported in the gas and low carbon energy segment, represents the change in value of LNG contracts that are being risk managed and which is reflected in the underlying result, but not in reported earnings. Management believes that this gives a better representation of performance in each period.

Furthermore, the fair values of derivative instruments used to risk manage certain other oil, gas, power and other contracts, are deferred to match with the underlying exposure. The commodity contracts for business requirements are accounted for on an accruals basis.

In addition, fair value accounting effects include changes in the fair value of derivatives entered into by the group to manage currency exposure and interest rate risks relating to hybrid bonds to their respective first call periods. The hybrid bonds which are classified as equity instruments were recorded in the balance sheet at their issuance date at their USD equivalent issued value. Under IFRS these equity instruments are not remeasured from period to period, and do not qualify for application of hedge accounting. The derivative instruments relating to the hybrid bonds, however, are required to be recorded at fair value with mark to market gains and losses recognized in the income statement. Therefore, measurement differences in relation to the recognition of gains and losses occur. The fair value accounting effect, which is reported in the other businesses & corporate segment, eliminates the fair value gains and losses of these derivative financial instruments that are recognized in the income statement. We believe that this gives a better representation of performance, by more appropriately reflecting the economic effect of these risk management activities, in each period.

the difference between the cost of sales calculated using the replacement cost of inventory and the cost of sales calculated on the first-in first-out (FIFO) method after adjusting for any changes in provisions where the net realizable value of the inventory is lower than its cost. Under the FIFO method, which we use for IFRS reporting of inventories other than for trading inventories, the cost of inventory charged to the income statement is based on its historical cost of purchase or manufacture, rather than its replacement cost. In volatile energy markets, this can have a significant distorting effect on reported income. The amounts disclosed as inventory holding gains and losses represent the difference between the charge to the income statement for inventory on a FIFO basis (after adjusting for any related movements in net realizable value provisions) and the charge that would have arisen based on the replacement cost of inventory. For this purpose, the replacement cost of inventory is calculated using data from each operation’s production and manufacturing system, either on a monthly basis, or separately for each transaction where the system allows this approach; and

The amounts disclosed are not separately reflected in the financial statements as a gain or loss. Tier 1 and tier 2 process safety events

– Tier 1 events are losses of primary containment from a process of greatest consequence – causing harm to a member of the workforce, damage to equipment from a fire or explosion, a community impact or exceeding defined quantities. Tier 2 events are those of lesser consequence. These represent reported incidents occurring within bp’s operational HSSE reporting boundary. That boundary includes bp’s own operated facilities and certain other locations or situations. Reported process safety events are investigated throughout the year and as a result there may be changes in previously reported events. Therefore comparative movements are calculated against internal data reflecting the final outcomes of such investigations, rather than the previously reported comparative period, as this represents a more up to date reflection of the safety environment.

In October AstraZeneca completed a $2bn equity investment in Summit Therapeutics Inc. (Summit). The investment gives AstraZeneca rights equivalent to approximately 12.0% of Summit Therapeutics’ outstanding common stock, or approximately 10.6% on a fully diluted basis.

AstraZeneca and Summit entered into a clinical collaboration agreement to evaluate sonesitatug vedotin in combination with Summit’s PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody ivonescimab. The two companies also entered into a clinical collaboration with Daiichi Sankyo to evaluate

AstraZeneca and Summit intend to enter into an additional agreement initiating a global development programme combining other AstraZeneca cancer medicines, including additional ADCs, with ivonescimab.

In October, AstraZeneca formally opened its new global strategic R&D centre, in Kendall Square, Cambridge, Massachusetts. The state-of-the-art facility builds on the Company’s existing presence in Boston and Cambridge, Massachusetts and will be home to nearly 2,000 world-class researchers and scientists.

AstraZeneca is in a catalyst rich period with more than 180 pipeline projects driving its next wave of growth and scientific innovation. To capitalise on this opportunity, the Company has initiated the Reshaping for Sustainable Growth (RSG) programme to create additional capacity to invest behind its industry-leading pipeline and transformative technologies. Over the next three years, the programme will redeploy resources and strengthen capabilities across AstraZeneca’s existing business and therapy areas. The RSG programme is expected to cost up to $2.0bn in one-time restructuring costs and deliver $1.5bn in annualised pre-tax run-rate benefits. The savings generated will continue to be reinvested back into the Company, principally in the pipeline. The Company anticipates activities to be essentially complete by the end of 2029.

In October, AstraZeneca entered into a strategic drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro. Using advanced AI systems, the collaboration will identify novel drug targets and advance the design of new therapeutics for MASH and cardiomyopathies.

Under the terms of the agreement, insitro will receive an upfront payment of $40m, and is also eligible for up to approximately $1.46bn in potential development and commercial milestones, plus potential single digit royalties based on global commercial sales. AstraZeneca will have exclusive worldwide rights to advance selected programmes identified under the collaboration.

At Climate Week NYC, AstraZeneca’s delegation, led by Pam Cheng, EVP Global Operations, IT and Chief Sustainability Officer, engaged with more than 60 stakeholders, and advancing dialogues on sustainable, equitable and resilient healthcare. The Company announced the next phase of its flagship Young Health Programme in partnership with UNICEF, bringing its total investment from 2010-2030 to more than $100 million. The programme, which supports young people in underserved communities, aims to prevent non-communicable diseases by activating young people to advance health equity and address the health impacts of climate change in more than 60 countries. Pam Cheng gave a live broadcast interview on the Company’s sustainability action at the New York Stock Exchange.

received regulatory approval as the first inhaled respiratory medicine to use NGP. Regulatory filings have also been submitted in China and Japan.

The Company officially launched CARESA (CARe pathways Environmental Sustainability Assessment) a free tool that helps healthcare professionals model the potential environmental impact of patient care pathways and explore choices that could improve health outcomes for patients and the planet.

The European Network on Climate & Health Education, supported by AstraZeneca through the Sustainable Markets Initiative Health Systems Task Force which Pascal Soriot chairs, has helped 61 medical schools integrate sustainability into medical training, engaging over 3,000 faculty members and reaching 6,000 medical students to date.

AstraZeneca received the My Green Lab and International Institute for Sustainable Laboratories (I2SL) 2026 Freezer Challenge Award for the Biotech and Pharmaceutical sector for the third time. The Freezer Challenge is a global initiative that promotes more sustainable laboratory operations through improved freezer and cold storage management, helping reduce energy use and improve efficiency. In addition, in the UK, AstraZeneca maintained the highest achievable rating, Level 4, in the NHS Evergreen Sustainable Supplier Assessment for 2026–2027.

A new report, Addressing Inequalities in COPD and Lung Cancer: A Framework for Action, was launched to help policymakers and health system leaders address inequalities in care. The report was informed by a literature review and international expert input, including from Brazil, Italy, Saudi Arabia, Spain and Vietnam, and the London School of Economics (LSE Health).
In the US, AstraZeneca held community engagement events in Baltimore and Houston to increase awareness of lung health and improve understanding of clinical research.

Through Cancer Care Africa (CCA), AstraZeneca advanced patient support, evidence generation and clinical capacity across several African countries. This includes digitalising the ‘Sanady’ patient support programme in Morocco; generating evidence in Egypt on the potential of AI-supported triage; publishing national lung cancer registry data in Algeria; and strengthening respiratory care capabilities in Kenya through training in pleural procedures, bronchoscopy and endobronchial ultrasound.

Healthy Heart Africa (HHA) partnered with Kenya’s Ministry of Health to launch the country’s first National CKD Guidelines and the second phase of the National CKD Registry. Since May 2025, HHA has screened over 11,000 high-risk individuals across Kenya for CKD. Uganda’s Ministry of Health launched HHA-supported CKD Guidelines.
AstraZeneca continued to advance its work to strengthen health systems through the Partnership for Health System Sustainability and Resilience (PHSSR), which has now collaborated with 36 countries.

Policy roadmaps on early action on NCDs were launched in seven countries, convening government representatives, policymakers and patient groups to help unlock system-level changes, including to advance and accelerate screening programs, early detection capability and sustainable funding for innovative medicines. In Q3, launches in Spain and Greece convened government representatives, policymakers and patient groups to unlock system-level change based on the roadmap’s recommendations. Spain’s State Secretary for Health spoke at the roadmap launch at the Congress of Deputies. In France, PHSSR brought together more than 50 participants to discuss health system sustainability and resilience, including the former French Minister for Solidarity and Health.

PHSSR also engaged stakeholders in Mexico on research recommendations, and Germany’s Monitor Versorgungsforschung, a peer-reviewed healthcare research journal, published an article examining the PHSSR Synthesis Report and its comparison of eight advanced health systems.

Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women worldwide and the leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women.
Approximately 2.4 million breast cancer cases were diagnosed in 2024, with more than 690,000 deaths globally.
In Europe, approximately 540,000 cases of breast cancer were diagnosed in 2024, with more than 140,000 deaths.
HER2 is a tyrosine kinase receptor growth-promoting protein expressed on the surface of many types of tumours including breast cancer.
HER2 protein overexpression may occur as a result of HER2 gene amplification and is often associated with aggressive disease and poor prognosis in breast cancer.
Approximately one in five cases of breast cancer is considered HER2-positive.

HER2-positive early breast cancer is generally treated across two phases: the neoadjuvant (pre-surgical) phase and the adjuvant or post-neoadjuvant (post-surgical) phase. For patients treated before surgery, achieving pathologic complete response (pCR) – defined as no evidence of invasive cancer cells in the removed breast tissue or lymph nodes following neoadjuvant treatment – is an early indicator of improved long-term survival.
However, approximately half of patients (39-66%) treated before surgery do not achieve pCR, increasing their risk of recurrence.
Post-surgery therapy offers a key opportunity to reduce this risk and prevent progression to metastatic disease.
Yet approximately one in four patients with residual disease treated with the historic adjuvant standard of care still experience invasive disease or death.
Once disease becomes metastatic, five-year survival falls from around 90% to approximately 30%.

High risk of recurrence was defined as presentation with inoperable cancer (prior to neoadjuvant therapy) or pathologically positive axillary lymph nodes following neoadjuvant therapy.

The primary endpoint of DESTINY-Breast05 is investigator-assessed IDFS, which is defined as the time from randomisation until first invasive local, axillary or distant recurrence or death from any cause. The key secondary endpoint is investigator-assessed DFS. Other secondary endpoints include overall survival, distant recurrence-free interval, brain metastases-free interval and safety.

IgAN is a rare, inflammatory disease of the kidneys that can lead to chronic kidney disease and progress to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). It begins when the body develops abnormal IgA proteins resulting in immune complexes that are deposited in the kidneys causing damage. The deposition of these complexes activates the complement system, leading to terminal complement-driven inflammation. This results in damage and loss of essential parts of the kidney, including cells in the glomeruli, the part of the kidneys that filters and cleans the blood.
IgAN affects more than 200,000 people in the US.
Approximately half of people with IgAN who have elevated protein levels in urine or reduced kidney function are at high risk of progression to ESKD, or kidney failure, within 10 years of diagnosis.

Richard Lafayette, MD, Professor of Medicine (Nephrology) at the Stanford University Medical Center, Founder and Director of the Stanford Glomerular Disease Center and external scientific committee co-chair of the I CAN trial, said: “For many people living with IgAN, persistent proteinuria remains a significant challenge despite available treatments, signalling ongoing kidney injury and heightened risk of disease progression. Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is a rare, inflammatory disease of the kidneys that can lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD) and progress to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). It begins when the body develops abnormal IgA proteins resulting in immune complexes that are deposited in the kidneys causing damage. The deposition of these complexes activates the complement system, leading to terminal complement-driven inflammation. This results in damage and loss of essential parts of the kidney, including cells in the glomeruli, the part of the kidneys that filters and cleans the blood. Over time, this damage impacts the ability of the kidneys to function properly, resulting in chronic kidney disease that can progress to end-stage kidney disease.
The signs and symptoms of IgAN can include blood in the urine (haematuria), foamy urine (proteinuria), swelling in hands and feet (oedema) and high blood pressure (hypertension).

Most people with IgAN do not experience symptoms in the early stages of the disease, and therefore, it often goes undetected until it has progressed. At diagnosis, irreversible kidney damage may have already occurred.
Approximately half of people with IgAN who have elevated protein levels in urine or reduced kidney function are at high risk of progression to ESKD, or kidney failure, within 10 years of diagnosis.

This is my first full quarter at bp, and it has been marked by one of the most disrupted periods in the global energy market. Through that, bp's team has stepped up, working tirelessly to keep energy flowing for our customers.

Financially, we delivered a strong quarter, with an underlying replacement cost profit of $5.7 billion ($2.5 billion higher than last quarter) and an operating cash flow of $10.9 billion, after a working capital build of $1.0 billion.

We made good progress strengthening bp's balance sheet. We also took steps to simplify and strengthen bp. In recent weeks, we sold our Gelsenkirchen refinery, agreed to sell our retail business in Austria and announced our intention to sell our North Sea business in the UK. Today, we are announcing our intention to sell Archaea, our biogas business in the US.

But there are areas where our performance fell short. Operationally, our plants didn't run as well as they did last quarter - upstream plant reliability was 92.4%, compared to 95.7%, and production was down and our refineries processed less crude. This was due, in part, to planned maintenance and the conflict in the Middle East, but this is a reminder that we have more to do to deliver consistent operational performance.

Since I joined bp, I have spent time with bp's teams on the frontline and met investors, business partners, governments and other key stakeholders. In four months, I've seen enough to know this company can be extraordinary - from our high-quality assets to our integrated model, deep capabilities, strong partnerships and exceptional people.

However, we are not making the most of our potential. Our performance over the past few years has not met our own expectations, let alone those of our shareholders. We have not delivered consistently; we have written off too much value; and our costs and liabilities are not resilient enough in a low price environment.

My job is to help make bp the best we can be. We need to take a clear look at ourselves: assessing what needs to change, stopping what holds us back and building strength where it matters. We have to get fit to grow. To do so, I am laying out five priorities to deliver a step change in performance and grow shareholder value.
Priorities to deliver a step change in performance

This quarter we reduced the total of net debt, hybrids, leases and Gulf of America settlement liabilities by more than 11% compared to last quarter. That is still not enough - we need to do more. Financial resilience gives us greater flexibility to invest to grow through the cycle and reward our shareholders.

to ensure every dollar of capital competes. Our decision to sell Bay du Nord and free up the capital shows that discipline in action. We must keep challenging ourselves, using our balanced investment criteria to make decisions rooted in profitability, cash generation and market realities. I am very clear on this, we need to compete in the weight class we are in.

. We need to run our assets safely, reliably and with greater cost efficiency. We have made progress on reducing structural costs, but we have not improved enough where it matters most: the bottom line. We need to move faster, and we have both the opportunity and the technology to do this. Operational excellence is also about working safely with people, communities and the environment; it helps us work to deliver energy that is secure, affordable and lower-carbon, where it makes business sense - and it is how we will make bp more competitive.

We will be transparent about how we progress - and judge ourselves by our results. I want the organization focused on execution: deliver what we said, faster and with greater intensity. In three words: focus, perform, grow.

Reported production for the quarter was 1,436mboe/d, 5.4% lower than the same period in 2025. Underlying production for the quarter was 1.8% higher mainly due to increased production in bpx Energy and ramp up of major projects partly offset by seasonal maintenance.

In May, bp as operator, confirmed a final investment decision (FID) on the Thunder Horse subsea pump. With plans to deliver first oil in 2028, the project is expected to add gross production of around 15,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day at peak.

In June bp confirmed the preliminary results of the Capricornus-1A appraisal well in Namibia's Orange Basin. This established an oil pay extension from the Capricornus discovery well. Petroleum Exploration License 85 (PEL85), where the well was drilled, is operated by Rhino Resources where Azule Energy has a 42.5% working interest. bp holds a 50% interest in Azule Energy.

In June bp, as operator, announced the commencement of non-associated gas (NAG) production operations on the Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli (ACG) field in the Azerbaijan sector of the Caspian Sea. This marks the first commercial gas production operations on ACG, one of the world's largest oil-producing fields.

In June bp announced the FID for the Greater PAJ Project, a major offshore oil development located in Blocks 31 and 31/21 in Angola, adding expected gross production of around 95,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day at peak. This is operated by Azule Energy, a 50:50 joint venture between bp and Eni. Azule Energy has a 26.67% working interest in Block 31 and a 50% working interest in Block 31/21.
In June, following regulatory approval, bp completed the sale of a 10% shareholding in Pan American Energy Group S.L., reducing its shareholding from 50% to 40%.

It was announced that, effective 1 July 2026, operatorship of the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan (BTC) oil export pipeline was transferred from bp to SOCAR Midstream Operations LLC (SMO), a wholly owned subsidiary of SOCAR.

In July bp agreed to sell its non-operated interest in the Bay du Nord project offshore Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, to Equinor. Completion of the transaction is subject to third party approvals.

In July bp has agreed terms for ConocoPhillips to acquire a 42% interest in BP Energy Company of Kirkuk Limited (BP ECKL), supporting the redevelopment of several large-scale oil fields in the Kirkuk area of northern Iraq. bp has also agreed terms for Turkiye Petrolleri Anonim Ortakligi (TPAO) to acquire a further 15% interest in BP ECKL. Completion of the respective transactions are subject to third party approvals.

In July bp successfully started up the Atlantis Major Facility Expansion project in the Gulf of America, the eighth of its 10 major projects due online between 2025 and 2027, adding two new subsea water injection wells.
In July bp announced its intention to market its North Sea business for a potential sale.
These events build on the progress announced in our first-quarter results, which comprised the following:

Aker BP started oil production from the Solveig Phase 2 (formally called Utsira High) development in the North Sea (bp interest in Aker BP 15.9%). The project has been delivered on schedule, adding approximately 39 million barrels of oil equivalent in recoverable resources to the Solveig field; bp confirmed an oil discovery in the Algaita-01 exploration well offshore Angola. The well was drilled in Block 15/06, and is operated by Azule Energy; bp announced the start-up of the Ndungu full-field, part of the Agogo Integrated West Hub Project (IWH), in the western area of Block 15/06, offshore Angola. Agogo IWH is operated by Azule Energy; bp was the apparent highest bidder on three blocks in the BBG-2 Gulf of America lease sale; bp confirmed start-up of gas production from the Quiluma field, part of the New Gas Consortium in Angola, operated by Azule Energy; and bp agreed to acquire a 60% interest in three offshore exploration blocks in Namibia from Eco Atlantic Oil & Gas. Subject to Namibian government approvals, bp will be the operator of three blocks - PEL97, PEL99 and PEL100 - offshore Namibia in the Walvis Basin, with Eco Atlantic remaining a partner, along with Namibia's national oil company NAMCOR.

Considerations in respect of ongoing geopolitical instability in the Middle East and impact on the economic environment

The impact of ongoing geopolitical instability in the Middle East and the associated economic developments have been considered for the basis of preparation for the interim financial information. Such factors include the economic effect of price volatility, supply disruptions in the region, operability of producing assets and discount rates.

As a result of ongoing geopolitical instability in the Middle East and the related economic impact, the group's value-in-use impairment testing price assumptions for Brent oil and Henry Hub gas were revised during the second quarter from those disclosed in the

, and also revised since the first quarter 2026. The group has updated its estimate of Brent oil prices to $80/bbl (previously $70/bbl) and Henry Hub gas prices to $3.34/mmBtu (previously $3.80/mmBtu) in real 2024 terms on an average basis for the full year 2026. With reference to the Brent price, this estimate assumes that the ongoing supply disruptions resulting from geopolitical instability in the Middle East resolve before the year end 2026. With regard to the Henry Hub gas price assumption, the price decrease is based on an expectation of oversupply in 2026 in the US domestic market, partly offset by supply disruption. No material impairment or reversal of impairment arose in the second quarter 2026 and half year 2026 interim periods as a result of the changes to these commodity price assumptions. The post-tax discount rate used for value-in-use impairment testing of assets other than certain low carbon energy assets was maintained at 8% (31 December 2025 8%).

The principal risks and uncertainties affecting bp are described in the Principal risks and uncertainties (Risk factors) section of bp Annual Report and Form 20-F 2025 (pages 62-66) and are summarized below.
There are no material changes expected in those risk factors for the remaining six months of the financial year.

The risks and uncertainties summarized below, separately or in combination, could have a material adverse effect on the implementation of our strategy, business, financial performance, results of operations, cash flows, liquidity, prospects, shareholder value and returns, and reputation.

- our financial performance is impacted by fluctuations in the prices of oil, natural gas, refined products, and emerging energy commodities due to factors such as volatile energy markets, exchange rates, or structural shifts in demand and supply, policy, or trade (such as carbon pricing or LNG flows).

- failure to adequately access, develop or sustain production of hydrocarbon resources may result in delivery delays, missed strategic targets and adversely impact our financial performance and undermine our reputation.
- failure to invest in the best opportunities or deliver major projects successfully could adversely affect our financial performance and long-term competitiveness.

- the diverse locations of our business activities and operations around the world expose us to a wide range of geopolitical developments (including sanctions, trade route restrictions, civil unrest, conflict, or government intervention).
● Liquidity, capital access and financial resilience

- external market conditions can impact our ability to maintain liquidity, credit strength, or access to capital markets which could impair our ability to operate, meet financial commitments, or deliver our strategy.

- the performance, standards, or compliance of non-operated joint ventures, strategic partners, contractors, sub-contractors, or other third parties could expose bp to legal, operational, financial, or reputational harm.
● Digital, cyber security and data risk

- increasing reliance on digital infrastructure, growing AI adoption, and evolving cyber threats exposes bp and our third-party suppliers and contractors to data loss, infrastructure failures, or system compromise which could result in operational disruption, regulatory breaches, significant fines and reputational harm.
● Climate change and the transition to a lower carbon economy

- developments in policy, law, regulation, technology and markets, including societal and investor sentiment, related to the issue of climate change and the transition to a lower carbon economy could increase costs, reduce revenues, constrain our operations and affect our business plans and financial performance.

- failure to maintain a competitive strategy, underpinned by a strong portfolio of assets, cost performance, innovative technology, projects and long-term growth opportunities, could negatively impact our investors' confidence in our ability to grow long-term shareholder value and returns.
- failure to retain, develop, and attract the talent, leadership, capabilities and behaviours required to deliver our strategy could weaken performance, culture, and long-term value creation.
● Process safety, personal safety, and environmental risks

- bp's operations and business activities are exposed to a wide range of safety, operational integrity, and environmental risks - particularly under growing complexity and delivery intensity - which could result in major incidents that harm people or the environment, disrupted operations, damage to bp's reputation, legal liability, undermine our financial standing or threaten our licence to operate.

- hostile acts such as terrorism, civil unrest, armed conflict, sabotage, activism, piracy, insider threats, workplace violence, cyber-enabled physical attacks, or threats to personnel security such as kidnapping or detention could harm our people, disrupt operations, compromise critical assets, or damage our reputation.
- failure to supply products to customers, meet technical specifications or regulatory standards could lead to harm, operational disruption, reputational damage, or legal and financial consequences.

- ethical misconduct, non-compliance with law and regulation or changes in law and regulation could increase costs, constrain our operations and affect our strategy, business plans and financial performance. Incidents of ethical misconduct or non-compliance could also damage our reputation and result in litigation, regulatory action, penalties and potentially affect our licence to operate.
● Financial and physical commodity trading activities

- we undertake physical and financial trading across global commodity and financial markets. Risk associated with our trading activities could arise from a failure to maintain robust oversight, controls, and disciplined execution in our trading activities which could result in business disruption, financial loss, regulatory action, or reputational damage.
● Integrity of financial and non-financial reporting

- failure to maintain integrity in financial and non-financial reporting may result in material misstatement or regulatory breach, which could lead to regulatory action, legal liability and reputational damage.

bp uses derivative instruments to manage the economic exposure relating to inventories above normal operating requirements of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products. Under IFRS, these inventories are recorded at historical cost. The related derivative instruments, however, are required to be recorded at fair value with gains and losses recognized in the income statement. This is because hedge accounting is either not permitted or not followed, principally due to the impracticality of effectiveness-testing requirements. Therefore, measurement differences in relation to recognition of gains and losses occur. Gains and losses on these inventories, other than net realizable value provisions, are not recognized until the commodity is sold in a subsequent accounting period. Gains and losses on the related derivative commodity contracts are recognized in the income statement, from the time the derivative commodity contract is entered into, on a fair value basis using forward prices consistent with the contract maturity.

bp enters into physical commodity contracts to meet certain business requirements, such as the purchase of crude for a refinery or the sale of bp's gas production. Under IFRS these physical contracts are treated as derivatives and are required to be fair valued when they are managed as part of a larger portfolio of similar transactions. Gains and losses arising are recognized in the income statement from the time the derivative commodity contract is entered into.

IFRS require that inventory held for trading is recorded at its fair value using period-end spot prices, whereas any related derivative commodity instruments are required to be recorded at values based on forward prices consistent with the contract maturity. Depending on market conditions, these forward prices can be either higher or lower than spot prices, resulting in measurement differences.

bp enters into contracts for pipelines and other transportation, storage capacity, oil and gas processing, liquefied natural gas (LNG) and certain gas and power contracts that, under IFRS, are recorded on an accruals basis. These contracts are risk-managed using a variety of derivative instruments that are fair valued under IFRS. This results in measurement differences in relation to recognition of gains and losses.

The way that bp manages the economic exposures described above, and measures performance internally, differs from the way these activities are measured under IFRS. bp calculates this difference for consolidated entities by comparing the IFRS result with management's internal measure of performance. We believe that disclosing management's estimate of this difference provides useful information for investors because it enables investors to see the economic effect of these activities as a whole.

Under management's internal measure of performance the inventory, transportation and capacity contracts in question are valued based on fair value using relevant forward prices prevailing at the end of the period.

Fair value accounting effects also include changes in the fair value of the near-term portions of LNG contracts that fall within bp's risk management framework. LNG contracts are not considered derivatives, because there is insufficient market liquidity, and they are therefore accrual accounted under IFRS. However, oil and natural gas derivative financial instruments used to risk manage the near-term portions of the LNG contracts are fair valued under IFRS. The fair value accounting effect, which is reported in the gas and low carbon energy segment, represents the change in value of LNG contracts that are being risk managed and which is reflected in the underlying result, but not in reported earnings. Management believes that this gives a better representation of performance in each period.

Furthermore, the fair values of derivative instruments used to risk manage certain other oil, gas, power and other contracts, are deferred to match with the underlying exposure. The commodity contracts for business requirements are accounted for on an accruals basis.

In addition, fair value accounting effects include changes in the fair value of derivatives entered into by the group to manage currency exposure and interest rate risks relating to hybrid bonds to their respective first call periods. The hybrid bonds which are classified as equity instruments were recorded in the balance sheet at their issuance date at their USD equivalent issued value. Under IFRS these equity instruments are not remeasured from period to period, and do not qualify for application of hedge accounting. The derivative instruments relating to the hybrid bonds, however, are required to be recorded at fair value with mark to market gains and losses recognized in the income statement. Therefore, measurement differences in relation to the recognition of gains and losses occur. The fair value accounting effect, which is reported in the other businesses & corporate segment, eliminates the fair value gains and losses of these derivative financial instruments that are recognized in the income statement. We believe that this gives a better representation of performance, by more appropriately reflecting the economic effect of these risk management activities, in each period.

the difference between the cost of sales calculated using the replacement cost of inventory and the cost of sales calculated on the first-in first-out (FIFO) method after adjusting for any changes in provisions where the net realizable value of the inventory is lower than its cost. Under the FIFO method, which we use for IFRS reporting of inventories other than for trading inventories, the cost of inventory charged to the income statement is based on its historical cost of purchase or manufacture, rather than its replacement cost. In volatile energy markets, this can have a significant distorting effect on reported income. The amounts disclosed as inventory holding gains and losses represent the difference between the charge to the income statement for inventory on a FIFO basis (after adjusting for any related movements in net realizable value provisions) and the charge that would have arisen based on the replacement cost of inventory. For this purpose, the replacement cost of inventory is calculated using data from each operation's production and manufacturing system, either on a monthly basis, or separately for each transaction where the system allows this approach; and

P&G Shareholders Also Elect All 12 P&G Director Nominees at 2026 Annual Meeting

CINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) announced at today’s Annual Meeting of Shareholders that the P&G Board of Directors declared a quarterly dividend of $1.0885 per share on the Common Stock and on the Series A and Series B ESOP Convertible Class A Preferred Stock of the Company, payable on or after November 16, 2026 to Common Stock shareholders of record at the close of business on October 23, 2026, and to Series A and Series B ESOP Convertible Class A Preferred Stock shareholders of record at the start of business on October 23, 2026.

P&G has been paying a dividend for 136 consecutive years since its incorporation in 1890 and has increased its dividend for 70 consecutive years. This reinforces our commitment to return cash to shareowners, many of whom rely on the steady, reliable income earned with their investment in P&G.

Also at today’s Annual Meeting, P&G shareholders elected all 12 P&G Director nominees, with each receiving strong support according to preliminary voting results. Company shareholders also voted in favor of two Board proposals: to ratify the appointment of P&G's independent registered public accounting firm and for an advisory vote on executive compensation. Additionally, Company shareholders voted against three shareholder proposals.

The results of the vote announced today are considered preliminary until final results are tabulated and certified by the independent Inspector of Elections. Final results will be reported on a Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

P&G serves consumers around the world with one of the strongest portfolios of trusted, quality, leadership brands, including Always®, Ambi Pur®, Ariel®, Bounty®, Charmin®, Crest®, Dawn®, Downy®, Fairy®, Febreze®, Gain®, Gillette®, Head & Shoulders®, Lenor®, Olay®, Oral-B®, Pampers®, Pantene®, SK-II®, Tide®, Vicks®, and Whisper®. The P&G community includes operations in approximately 70 countries worldwide. Please visit https://www.pg.com for the latest news and information about P&G and its brands. For other P&G news, visit us at https://www.pg.com/news.

with Toyota Industries Corporation At the end of the year ended March 31, 2026, Toyota reclassified its holdings of Toyota Industries Corporation ("Toyota Industries") (automotive segment) shares and related other comprehensive income as held for sale. For the first half ended September 30, 2026, Toyota completed the sale of its shares in Toyota Industries.

• NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design debut RFD4-Proteina, a new open model that combines programmable protein design with search capabilities, unlocking new frontiers in biology.

• Siemens Healthineers is advancing the next generation of adaptive radiotherapy, using NVIDIA intelligence to increase access to life-saving cancer care with agentic co-planning, patient-specific simulation and robotic control.

• Automata, Benchling, Biolevate, Boltz, Danaher, Hologen and Therna Biosciences are using the NVIDIA BioNeMo open platform to develop scientific agents that connect drug design, autonomous laboratories and biological discovery, helping researchers move from hypothesis to experiments faster.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced collaborations with leading global healthcare and research organizations to advance protein design — including through a newly released open model, RFD4-Proteina — accelerate drug discovery and bring greater precision to cancer care.

Life sciences researchers must search vast biological design spaces and aim to shorten the cycle between computational design and laboratory testing to discover new medicines. Cancer care teams face a different challenge: translating complex imaging and treatment data into precise plans for each patient.
NVIDIA open models, accelerated computing and physical intelligence can help experts evaluate more possibilities faster, from designing new proteins to planning adaptive radiotherapy.

“Agentic and physical AI are opening new possibilities across medicine, from designing proteins and powering autonomous laboratories to improving personalized cancer care,” said Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare at NVIDIA. “Together with healthcare and life science leaders, we’re accelerating scientific discovery and advancing more precise, accessible care around the world.”

NVIDIA and the UW Institute for Protein Design Introduce RFD4-Proteina Proteins are molecular tools that perform many of life’s essential tasks, and designing new versions could open paths to new medicines, diagnostics and industrial applications. But finding a protein capable of performing a designed function requires searching an immense range of possible designs.
NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design are debuting RFD4-Proteina, a new NVIDIA BioNeMo™ open model that combines programmable protein design with search capabilities.

The model generates targeted protein designs, enabling scientists and agents to search and refine designs using molecular inputs, constraints and scoring objectives. Potential applications include designing proteins to interrupt disease processes or detect signs of disease in diagnostic tests.

In testing reported in the research draft, RFD4-Proteina achieved higher computational design success rates and generation throughput than the evaluated baselines across four benchmark suites: protein binding, small-molecule binding, enzyme scaffolding and DNA binding. The model helps researchers explore and prioritize candidates for laboratory testing, where experiments establish how a design performs under tested conditions.

“We are moving from an era of discovering the proteins nature has made to one in which we can design entirely new ones,” said David Baker, 2024 Nobel Laureate in chemistry and director of the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington. “RFD4-Proteina expands what scientists can create, from proteins that could advance drug discovery to enzymes that break down pesticides. Making the model open will allow researchers around the world to build on these capabilities and pursue solutions once beyond the reach.”

RFD4-Proteina is available today through partners including Amazon Bio Discovery, Anthropic’s Claude Science, Benchling, Databricks, Google Cloud, Hugging Face, Nebius, OpenAI and Tamarind Bio, enabling researchers and developers to integrate the open protein design model into agent, cloud and scientific computing workflows.

Siemens Healthineers Advances Cancer Care With NVIDIA Siemens Healthineers and NVIDIA are collaborating to develop the next generation of adaptive radiotherapy with agentic and robotic intelligence, combining imaging and oncology expertise with accelerated computing and simulation to simplify workflows and expand access to care.

By 2050, approximately 35 million people worldwide are projected to be diagnosed with cancer each year. Care teams face growing pressure to deliver precise, personalized treatment while managing limited specialist capacity. Greater efficiency can help expand access to care while maintaining the precision needed to deliver prescribed doses to tumors and protect surrounding healthy tissue.

Siemens Healthineers is working with NVIDIA to further develop adaptive radiotherapy through agentic co-planning, patient-specific simulation and real-time computing. NVIDIA Nemotron™ open foundation models are being explored to power agentic co-planning, with the aim of helping oncologists evaluate and refine personalized treatment strategies. The models could then be combined with NVIDIA CUDA®-accelerated dose calculation for rapid patient-specific simulation and the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to connect live sensor data with AI and simulation to support adaptive treatment.

“Adaptive radiotherapy is built on a single principle: treatment should adapt to the patient, not the other way around,” said Arthur Kaindl, head of Varian, the Siemens Healthineers cancer-care business. “We’ve made important advances in precision and adaptation — most recently, with the launch of the Accela system. Our collaboration with NVIDIA builds on that progress, exploring how AI and real-time computing could give clinicians greater speed and insight to make informed decisions, adapt treatment with greater confidence and deliver personalized care to more patients.”

Scientific Agents Advance Drug Discovery and Development Life sciences is one of the world’s most important scientific frontiers, with global scientific R&D reaching $3.8 trillion and annual pharmaceutical budgets approaching $300 billion.

Scientific agents and autonomous laboratories can help turn more of that investment into evidence, insight and, ultimately, new treatments by connecting design, experimentation and learning in a continuous cycle.

To accelerate discovery and free up scientists for work only they can do, research and laboratory technology companies are using NVIDIA BioNeMo — an open development platform that enables AI-driven biology and drug discovery — alongside Nemotron and other NVIDIA technologies to develop scientific agents and the specialized models and tools that connect drug design, scientific data and laboratory workflows:
• Benchling is grounding agents in experimental data, research context and connected scientific workflows.
• Biolevate is connecting biological data, specialized scientific tools and agentic reasoning across drug discovery and development.

• Boltz is developing specialized models and tools that scientific agents can use to predict molecular structures and design and evaluate candidates. It is also previewing a scientific agent to plan workflows, apply the right models and interpret results to guide the next experiment.
• Automata is connecting scientific agents with automated laboratory infrastructure so they can initiate experiments and capture structured, contextualized results through workflows.

• Genedata’s AI co-scientist will coordinate protein design and testing in the protein design foundry within Danaher’s autonomous lab. The workflow will incorporate RFD4-Proteina, helping scientists use experimental results to guide the next round of designs.

• Hologen is combining its large medicine models with NVIDIA Nemotron to build AI clinical scientists that help researchers turn imaging and clinical data into insights about patient outcomes to inform clinical trial design.
• Therna Biosciences is using large language model reasoning to connect experimental evidence and RNA medicine design, helping scientists turn biological insights into therapeutic candidates.

NVIDIA Open Models Streamline Hospital Operations, Expand Access to Specialized Care Healthcare systems across Europe are working to expand access to specialized care while reducing the administrative demands on already-stretched care teams.
Avelios, Corti, Dedalus, Dawn Health and Sword are also building on NVIDIA Nemotron, powering everything from AI scribes and AI-assisted clinical care to personalized patient support services.

PolyAI is building on NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to speed the path to care through its multilingual dialog deployment with medical software provider Corilus, which has a network spanning more than 70,000 healthcare professionals across Belgium and France.
Apian and VitVio are extending this into the physical world, using NVIDIA Cosmos™ world models and NVIDIA Omniverse™ libraries to build digital twins that monitor and improve hospital operations.

• Leading global telecom operators are expanding NVIDIA-powered computing across their networks to deliver advanced services closer to people and businesses, improve wireless experience and automate network operations.

• T-Mobile completes the world’s first AI-RAN call on a commercial network, while BT, Deutsche Telekom and Elisa announce AI-RAN pilots on live networks using Nokia’s CUDA-accelerated anyRAN software on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer, and NVIDIA introduces new Aerial RAN Computer configurations for high-capacity sites.
• Nine EMEA telecom operators are building and expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure across centralized and distributed locations.
• Operators and software partners are adopting NVIDIA Nemotron open models to deliver agentic services and develop agents for autonomous network operations.

GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced that leading global telecom operators are turning their networks into distributed intelligence platforms, adding NVIDIA accelerated computing to centralized data centers, metro sites and cell sites so they can serve models and applications closer to the people, businesses and machines that use them.

T-Mobile has completed the world’s first AI-RAN call on a live network in Bellevue, Washington, with NVIDIA and Nokia. Deutsche Telekom is advancing physical AI for industries, and Orange is introducing new voice intelligence services for enterprises and emergency responders. Elisa has completed Europe’s first field trial of AI-RAN, running voice, mobile data and vision AI together on a single accelerated computing platform over 5G, and BT is preparing live AI-RAN trials in the U.K. Nokia is bringing its anyRAN software on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) for trials at BT, Deutsche Telekom, Elisa and Orange.

Nine operators across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) are building or expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure, while Nokia and Cisco are incorporating NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models into the software operators use to run autonomous networks.

“Telecom networks were built to carry the world’s conversations. Now, they will also carry the world’s intelligence,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Leading global operators are turning their land, power and connectivity into a distributed AI infrastructure — bringing intelligence closer to the industries, people and robots that use it. With Nokia, we’re extending accelerated computing into the radio network itself, creating the foundation for AI-native 5G.”

Intelligence is built in five layers: land, power and shell, chips, infrastructure, models and applications. Telecom operators already own sovereign infrastructure at the first layer, with data centers, regional sites and cell sites that have power, fiber and spectrum.

By adding NVIDIA accelerated computing, open models and applications on top, operators are building the full intelligence stack into their networks. At distributed sites, a common converged platform based on the AI-RAN architecture can serve open models, power robotics, voice and agentic applications, and run intelligent 5G software.
Europe’s Leading Telcos Build Distributed Infrastructure Infrastructure sits at the foundation of telecom’s transition to distributed service platforms.

Deutsche Telekom plans to expand its NVIDIA-powered Industrial AI Cloud, which hosts open models — including NVIDIA Nemotron and Soofi — and serves robotics companies such as Agile Robots. At distributed sites, Deutsche Telekom is piloting AI-RAN trials with Nokia and NVIDIA, and demonstrating NVIDIA ARC to run inference between the device and the network edge.

A GTC Berlin demonstration with Agile Robots shows the approach: on-robot intelligence handles real-time perception and action, a model at the distributed edge supports fine-tuning and coordination across robots, and the central infrastructure provides capacity for larger training workloads.

Orange is hosting open models, including NVIDIA Nemotron, as a managed service on top of its Live Intelligence trusted AI platform, enabling new advanced services for enterprises. At distributed sites, Orange is deploying NVIDIA ARC for voice intelligence applications using Nemotron Speech, demonstrating new services to help emergency and field services teams translate across multiple languages in real time with low latency and reliability.
Elisa has deployed NVIDIA ARC at a distributed network location, running a voice intelligence application that serves as an enterprise assistant, and is using open models to build edge applications.
EMEA telcos are building or expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure:
• New infrastructure: CRA in the Czech Republic, etisalat in the United Arab Emirates, Silknet in Georgia and TIM in Italy.
• Expansions: Cassava in Africa, Deutsche Telekom in Germany, Fastweb + Vodafone in Italy, Kazakhtelecom in Central Asia and Orion Telecom in Serbia.

AI-RAN Brings Accelerated Computing Into the Radio Network AI-RAN extends accelerated computing into the radio access network (RAN), turning it into an intelligence workload that runs on the same platform as advanced services, so operators can get more out of their spectrum while serving demand from sites close to users.
Globally, nearly 20 telecom operators have publicly announced AI-RAN collaborations using Nokia anyRAN software and NVIDIA ARC.

• T-Mobile recently marked the world’s first AI-RAN call on its commercial network in Bellevue, Washington, running on commercial ARC servers, Nokia’s NVIDIA CUDA-accelerated RAN software and massive multiple-input multiple-output radios, and connected to an existing 5G Standalone core and a commercial smartphone.
• BT is planning live AI-RAN trials in Birmingham, England, with Nokia and NVIDIA in 2027.

• Deutsche Telekom has validated Nokia and NVIDIA’s commercial AI-RAN platform in Bonn and Oulu labs, including AI-enhanced uplink channel estimation to improve uplink user throughput, with plans to move to field trials in 2027.

• Elisa simultaneously ran voice, mobile data and video analytics on the NVIDIA ARC platform, marking a European first in Elisa’s over-the-air field environment using 5G spectrum. The trial clears the way for distributed deployment and commercial AI-RAN services in 2027.
• Orange is testing Nokia 5G software on NVIDIA ARC, focusing on AI-RAN spectral efficiency improvements and support for edge services in live networks.

NVIDIA is introducing two ARC configurations — MGX 2U and MGX 4U — designed for dense, high-capacity intelligence and radio workloads, typically deployed at centralized RAN sites. Powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO™ 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, the configurations will offer x86 and NVIDIA Vera CPU options. Dell Technologies, Quanta Cloud Technology and Supermicro will offer ARC-ready servers.

Open Models Power Autonomous Network Operations Leading telcos are using open models and agents to speed progress toward fully autonomous network operations. NVIDIA Nemotron open models and NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software are now integrated into leading partners’ commercial software, powering specialized agents built for telecom network workflows.

Nokia is integrating NVIDIA Nemotron into its Autonomous Networks Suite and using NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software to build and deploy trusted agents that manage operations across fixed, radio, core and transport networks.

Cisco has fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron models and integrated them into Crosswork AI, creating a common agentic layer across its Crosswork Network Automation software to manage IP and optical transport networks. The company is also using NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to help telcos operate agents safely.

TCS is working with telcos to fine-tune NVIDIA Nemotron models and use NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to build specialized agents that validate radio-site builds, detect, diagnose and auto-remediate network issues, and deliver multilingual voice experiences. BT is adopting Nemotron to build agents that inspect field-installation photos, detect problems and help reduce repeat site visits.

NTT DATA is extending its NextGenOSS platform with fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA Agent Toolkit to build agents that detect early network degradation, identify likely root causes and recommend next actions.

• Eaton Reports Record Third Quarter 2026 Results
• Third quarter sales increased 28%, with organic sales growth of 19%, above the high end of guidance

• Twelve-month rolling average organic orders increased 39% in Electrical Americas, 51% in Electrical Global and 20% in Aerospace, with order dollars reaching record levels in all three segments, driven by broad end-market strength
• Strong year-over-year total backlog growth of 46% in Electrical and 33% in Aerospace
• Record segment margins of 25.3%, above the high end of guidance, with Electrical Americas margins improving 230 basis points sequentially
• Announced agreement to acquire COL Group, expanding manufacturing capacity and power distribution capabilities for data center and utility markets in Europe
• Full year 2026 earnings per share expected to be between $10.39 and $10.49; adjusted earnings per share expected to be between $13.70 and $13.80​

DUBLIN – Intelligent power management company Eaton Corporation plc (NYSE:ETN) today reported strong third quarter 2026 results, including earnings per share of $2.77. Adjusted earnings per share were a record of $3.68, excluding charges of $0.62 per share related to intangible amortization, $0.30 per share related to acquisitions and divestitures, and income of $0.01 per share related to a multi-year restructuring program.

Sales in the quarter were a record $8.9 billion, up 28% from the third quarter of 2025. The sales increase consisted of 19% growth in organic sales, 8% growth from acquisitions, and 1% growth from foreign exchange.

Segment margins were a record 25.3%, 30 basis points above both the high end of the guidance range and the third quarter of 2025, driven by higher sales and improved performance amid continued capacity investments to support growth.

The Company continued to generate solid cash flow, supporting investment in growth initiatives while maintaining financial flexibility. Operating cash flow was $1.31 billion, and free cash flow was $1.03 billion.

Paulo Ruiz, Eaton chief executive officer, said, “Our strong third quarter performance reflects the focus and discipline our teams have demonstrated all year as we expand capacity, strengthen execution and position the business to meet accelerating customer demand. We delivered organic growth and segment margins above the high end of our guidance, driven by strong demand across our markets and continued momentum across our Electrical businesses. Record orders grew sequentially, backlog continued to expand, and we remain well-positioned to help customers deliver on their critical power infrastructure investments. These results reinforce our confidence in the remainder of the year.”

In the quarter, the company also announced an agreement to acquire COL Group, a leader in medium-voltage electrical distribution solutions, expanding the company’s European power distribution capabilities and manufacturing footprint and enhancing its ability to support growing customer demand across data center and utility markets.
For the full year 2026, the company anticipates:
• Adjusted earnings per share between $13.70 and $13.80
For the fourth quarter of 2026, the company anticipates:
• Adjusted earnings per share between $4.05 and $4.15

Demand remained robust across key end markets, as sales for the Electrical Americas segment were a record $4.2 billion, up 22% organically from the third quarter of 2025. Operating profits were a record $1.2 billion, up 20% over the third quarter of 2025, and operating margins in the quarter were 29.8%, up 230 basis points sequentially.
The twelve-month rolling average of orders in the third quarter was up 39% organically. Total backlog at the end of September remained strong and was up 33% over September 2025.

Sales for the Electrical Global segment were a record $2.7 billion, up 58% from the third quarter of 2025. The sales increase consisted of 27% growth in organic sales and 31% contribution from Boyd Thermal in its second full quarter post-acquisition. Operating profits were a record $576 million, up 75% over the third quarter of 2025. Operating margins in the quarter were 21.1%, up 200 basis points over the third quarter of 2025.
The twelve-month rolling average of orders in the third quarter was up 51% organically. Total backlog at the end of September was up 121% over September 2025.
On a rolling twelve-month basis, the book-to-bill ratio for the Electrical businesses remained strong at 1.2.

Aerospace segment sales were a third quarter record $1.2 billion, up 11% from the third quarter of 2025. The sales increase consisted of 6% growth in organic sales and 5% growth from the Ultra PCS acquisition. Operating profits were a third quarter record $298 million, up 6% over the third quarter of 2025. Operating margins of 24.9% were down 100 basis points over the third quarter of 2025.

The twelve-month rolling average of orders in the third quarter was up 20% organically. Total backlog at the end of September was up 33% over September 2025. On a rolling twelve-month basis, the book-to-bill ratio for the Aerospace segment remained strong at 1.2.

The Mobility segment posted sales of $852 million. Organic sales increased 9%. Operating profits were $146 million, up 39% from the third quarter of 2025. Operating margins in the quarter of 17.2% were up 370 basis points from the third quarter of 2025.

Eaton is an intelligent power management company dedicated to protecting the environment and improving the quality of life for people everywhere. We make products for the data center, utility, industrial, commercial and institutional, machine building, residential, aerospace and mobility markets. We are guided by our commitment to do business right, to operate sustainably and to help our customers manage power ─ today and well into the future. By capitalizing on the global growth trends of electrification and digitalization, we’re helping to solve the world’s most urgent power management challenges and building a more sustainable society for people today and generations to come.

Founded in 1911, Eaton has continuously evolved to meet the changing and expanding needs of our stakeholders. With revenues of $27.4 billion in 2025, the company serves customers in 180 countries. For more information, visit www.eaton.com. Follow us on LinkedIn.

Comments on the

determination of the impact of exchange rate fluctuations and changes in the scope of consolidation The impact of exchange rate fluctuations is determined by translating the financial statements for the fiscal year of entities with a functional currency other than the euro at the prior fiscal year’s exchange rates, without any other restatements. The impact of changes in the scope of consolidation is determined as follows: — for the fiscal year’s acquisitions, by deducting from revenue for the fiscal year the amount of revenue generated during that fiscal year by the acquired entities, as of their initial consolidation; — for the prior fiscal year’s acquisitions, by deducting from revenue for the fiscal year the amount of revenue generated over the months during which the acquired entities were not consolidated in the prior fiscal year; — for the fiscal year’s disposals, by adding to

revenue for the fiscal year the amount of revenue generated by the divested entities in the prior fiscal year over the months during which those entities were no longer consolidated in the current fiscal year; — for the prior fiscal year’s disposals, by adding to revenue for the fiscal year the amount of revenue generated in the prior fiscal year by the divested entities. Profit from recurring operations is restated in accordance with the same principles.

Moët & Chandon began its second season as the Official Champagne of Formula 1 Grand Prix races. Dom Pérignon launched three new vintages: Vintage 2017, Rosé Vintage 2010 and Plénitude 2 2008. ACCOUNTING POLICIES 1.1 General framework and environment The consolidated financial statements for the first half of 2026 were established in accordance with the international accounting standards and interpretations (IAS/IFRS) adopted by the European Union and applicable on June 30, 2026. These standards and interpretations have been applied consistently to the periods presented. The consolidated financial statements for the first half of 2026 were approved by the Board of Directors on July 27, 2026. The consolidated financial statements presented are “condensed”, which means that they only include notes that are significant or facilitate understanding of changes in the Group’s business activity and

financial position during the period. The interim financial statements are prepared according to the same rules and methods as those used to prepare the annual financial statements, with the exception of the determination of the income tax rate, calculated based on a forecast for the fiscal year. In addition, the comparability of the interim and annual financial statements may be affected by the seasonal nature of the Group’s business activities, which generally see a higher volume of business in the second half of the year than in the first half (see Note 24, “Segment information”). 1.2 Changes in the accounting framework applicable to LVMH Standards, amendments and interpretations for which application became mandatory in 2026 The application of standards, amendments and interpretations that took effect on January 1, 2026 did not have a material impact on the Group’s financial

statements. Other changes in the accounting framework and standards for which application is mandatory with effect later than January 1, 2026 The application of IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements – in particular the format of the income statement – is mandatory with effect from January 1, 2027. Its impact on the main performance measure used by the Group is limited. The Group’s operating profit will be adjusted in particular due the reclassification of “Cost of commercial foreign exchange derivatives” and “Income/(Loss) from joint ventures and associates”. These preliminary findings are based on the analyses carried out to date and may be subject to change in the second half of 2026, in particular due to new interpretations or clarifications that may be issued. 2. announced in January 2026, LVMH sold businesses in Hong Kong and Macao as well as its investments in partnerships in Japan and Indonesia (see Notes 8 and 25). Agreements to sell airport concessions in Los Angeles and San Francisco (United States) as well as businesses in Okinawa (Japan) were signed in March and June 2026, respectively. The effective completion of these transactions is planned for the second half of 2026. Concurrently with the disposal of businesses in Hong Kong and Macao, LVMH subscribed for a capital increase in China Tourism Group Duty Free Corporation Ltd in the amount of 47 million euros (see Note 9). Assets and liabilities related to DFS are presented within “Assets and liabilities held for sale”, in accordance with IFRS 5 (see Note 24). No other significant changes in ownership interests in consolidated companies took place in the first half of 2026.
