FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS AND MARKET RISK MANAGEMENT 23.1 Organization of foreign exchange, interest rate and equity market risk management Financial instruments are mainly used by the Group to hedge risks arising from Group activity and protect its assets. The management of foreign exchange and interest rate risk, in addition to transactions involving shares and financial instruments, is centralized. The Group has implemented a stringent policy and rigorous management guidelines to manage, measure and monitor these market risks. These activities are organized based on a segregation of duties between risk measurement (middle office), hedging (front office), administration (back office) and financial

control. The backbone of this organization is an integrated information system that allows transactions to be checked quickly. The Group’s hedging strategy is presented to the Performance Audit Committee. Hedging decisions are made according to an established process that includes regular presentations to the Group’s Executive Committee and detailed documentation. Counterparties are selected based on their rating and in accordance with the Group’s risk diversification strategy. 23.2 Summary of derivatives Derivatives are recorded in the balance sheet for the amounts and in the captions detailed as follows: (EUR millions) Notes June 30, 2026 Dec. 31, 2025 June 30, 2025 Interest rate risk Assets: Non‑current 4 3 4 Current 12 19 14 Liabilities: Non‑current (8) (39) (56) Current (31) (10) (11) 23.3 (22) (27) (50) Foreign exchange risk Assets: Non‑current 54 85 182 Current 236 592 835

Hedging instruments are used to reduce the foreign exchange risks arising from the fluctuations of currencies against the exporting and importing companies’

functional currencies, and are allocated to either trade receivables or payables (fair value hedges) for the fiscal year, or to transactions anticipated for future fiscal years (hedges of future cash flows). Future foreign currency-denominated cash flows are broken down as part of the budget preparation process and are hedged progressively over a period not exceeding one year unless a longer period is justified by probable commitments. As such, and according to market trends, identified foreign exchange risks are hedged using forward contracts or options. In addition, the Group is exposed to foreign exchange risk with respect to the Group’s net assets, as it owns assets denominated in currencies other than the euro. This foreign exchange risk may be hedged either partially or in full through foreign currency borrowings or by hedging the net worth of subsidiaries outside the eurozone,
using appropriate financial instruments with the aim of limiting the impact of foreign currency fluctuations against the euro on consolidated equity.

The future of quantum computing will depend on bringing quantum and classical computing together at unprecedented scale. Leadership-class classical computing is essential to managing quantum systems, accelerating complex simulations, correcting errors and integrating quantum processors with HPC clusters at scale. With leadership technologies spanning CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs and open software, AMD is uniquely positioned to build that foundation.

Today, AMD is applying its classical computing leadership to that challenge through a new codesign platform for quantum error correction established by IBM and the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). The collaboration provides a shared environment to evaluate the architectures, software and workflows that future hybrid quantum systems will require.

The new codesign platform will draw on the experiences of all three partners. IBM brings quantum computing technology, ORNL brings its scientific research and computing environment, and AMD brings the classical computing technologies and open software to connect quantum processing with scientific workloads.

The first deployment brings together IBM quantum computers, including the 120-qubit IBM Quantum Nighthawk, and the Umbra HPC system, powered by AMD EPYC™ CPUs and AMD Instinct™ GPUs, in a colocated environment.

“Building useful quantum systems requires the quantum and classical computing communities to solve system design challenges together," Ralph Wittig, Corporate Fellow, Head of Research & Advanced Development, AMD. "AMD brings expertise across CPUs, GPUs and FPGAs, from real-time control to leadership-class supercomputing. With IBM, Oak Ridge and our ecosystem partners, we are applying that experience to develop and test how quantum processors, classical computing and software can work together at scale.”
This work builds on AMD’s experience powering leadership-class supercomputers and an ongoing collaboration with IBM across GPU-accelerated scientific calculations and FPGA-based error decoding.

Integrating quantum and classical computing requires matching different processing requirements within one system. Control and feedback demand precise timing and rapid responses. Scientific calculations require substantial parallel processing. And orchestration coordinates work across all these resources.

AMD works together with the ecosystem and its partners through deep codesign to utilize its broad high-performance portfolio to address the classical computing requirements of quantum systems from real-time control through leadership-scale scientific computing. AMD brings expertise across these requirements:
• AMD EPYC™ CPUs provide the orchestration and general-purpose performance needed to coordinate complex hybrid classical-quantum systems.
AMD EPYC™ CPUs provide the orchestration and general-purpose performance needed to coordinate complex hybrid classical-quantum systems.
• AMD Instinct™ GPUs accelerate simulation, optimization and the parallel scientific computations surrounding quantum workloads.
AMD Instinct™ GPUs accelerate simulation, optimization and the parallel scientific computations surrounding quantum workloads.
• AMD Versal™ adaptive SoCs provide the low-latency control, readout and decoding capabilities required near the quantum processor.
AMD Versal™ adaptive SoCs provide the low-latency control, readout and decoding capabilities required near the quantum processor.
• AMD ROCm™ open software ecosystem helps developers connect HPC and AI applications and this hardware into increasingly integrated quantum-classical environments.
AMD ROCm™ open software ecosystem helps developers connect HPC and AI applications and this hardware into increasingly integrated quantum-classical environments.
Together, these technologies give quantum developers, system builders and research institutions a scalable classical foundation they can design around today.
AMD and Its Role in Quantum's Future

Error correction is what stands between the quantum computers we have today and the ones that can perform real science. Solving for that takes work on both quantum and classical computing, with a large part of it being on the classical side. Error correction requires quantum researchers to understand processors and classical computing as the two systems work side by side. The new codesign platform gives AMD, IBM and Oak Ridge National Laboratory a shared environment to investigate those requirements together as they continue support for the Department of Energy’s Quantum Genesis Mission and its progress toward a scientifically relevant quantum computer by 2028.

Plans call for connecting the platform with the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF), which also houses, ORNL’s new Lux SI (Super Intelligence) + HPC supercomputer, powered by AMD EPYC CPUs and AMD Instinct GPUs. Those connections will extend the research environment to the full-scale system necessary to explore how integrated quantum, AI and scientific computing can accelerate scientific discoveries and national security.

For AMD, the work reflects a foundational principle: Advances in quantum computing depend on progress in classical computing. By working with IBM and ORNL to investigate those requirements now, AMD shapes the computing foundation that future quantum computers will need. AMD is codesigning a holistic system with quantum companies, research institutions and technology providers.

The Intel 14A process design kit (PDK) 0.9 gives foundry customers a more mature, silicon-validated environment for designing products on the Intel 14A process node. This milestone is an important step toward the Intel 14A PDK 1.0 and high-volume manufacturing readiness.

Silicon process technologies provide a range of transistors, interconnects and specialized features that chip designers leverage to build their products. For a foundry customer to use these features, they need a way to incorporate them into their designs.

This is where the process design kit (PDK) comes in. A PDK serves as the interface between the process technology and the design tools engineers use to turn their ideas into silicon. If you think of a chip as a microscopic but vast city, a PDK is the digital building codes, approved building materials, and helpful resources that allow a designer to create a successful product.

Intel Foundry recently announced the general availability of the PDK 0.9 for the Intel 14A process node, an important milestone that allows customers to use the technology in an environment closer to full scale production. We asked Ben Sell, who leads Intel 14A and advanced nodes development, and Ali Farhang, who oversees PDKs and design enablement, to talk about the importance of this release, PDKs in general, and what’s next for the Intel 14A node.
Let’s start with the basics. What exactly is a PDK, and why is it important when you develop a new process technology?

Ali: A Process Design Kit, or PDK, is essentially the ultimate reference guide for a chip designer to create a product on a specific manufacturing process. It brings together the models, design rules, and other supporting materials that electronic design automation (EDA) tools use to help a customer bring their product from concept to mass production.

Just as importantly, the PDK release lifecycle serves as the clock that orchestrates technology development. Each revision represents a milestone of technology maturity, synchronizing our internal research and development, EDA and IP ecosystem partners, and customer design teams on a single, shared schedule.
Can you tell us what it means for Intel Foundry to announce general availability of the Intel 14A PDK 0.9?

Ben: From a customer perspective, the PDK 0.9 gives customers the confidence to design products on Intel 14A, as the technology is reaching the industry-standard performance and yield maturity expected at this stage of development, supported by silicon-backed validation.

Process technologies take time to mature for production, but customers want early access to begin design evaluation to enable time-to-market. With PDK 0.9, customers can create designs that go into the fab for production around the time a process node is certified. As we approach PDK 1.0, it says that we are confident that this process technology is on track for high volume manufacturing.

Ali: In the foundry business, trust is paramount. For fabless customers, selecting a foundry is one of the most consequential decisions they make. If a foundry does not deliver, the impact on a customer’s business can be profound. The general availability of Intel 14A PDK 0.9 is a critical milestone demonstrating that Intel Foundry can execute on its commitments.
How are things going so far with Intel 14A, and how does that translate into your confidence in the PDK releases?

Ben: We are pleased with the pace of progress on Intel 14A and encouraged by the feedback we are receiving from customers. That progress reflects both a strong technology foundation and the growing maturity of how we develop and deliver a foundry process.

Intel 14A builds on proven backside power delivery architecture with PowerDirect and gate-all-around transistor technology with RibbonFET 2, and with Turbo Cells added to give designers greater flexibility on optimizing performance and efficiency depending on their needs. The node incorporates extensive learning and manufacturing knowledge from Intel 18A, increased investment in inline detection, modeling and simulation to identify issues earlier, and several strategic initiatives to accelerate the pace of development.

Together, these capabilities are helping us improve Intel 14A performance, yield, variability and cycle time while staying aligned to our committed schedule that customers depend on to build their products.

That execution discipline is what gives us confidence in the PDK releases. Each release is grounded in silicon, so customers receive a progressively more accurate and complete representation of the technology. The PDK 0.9 is an important proof point that many customers use as a gate to start a design.
How is Intel Foundry working with the ecosystem around Intel 14A development?

Ali: Intel is partnering closely with leading EDA providers, including Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens, and Keysight, along with a broad ecosystem of IP partners, to deliver a comprehensive design platform for our foundry customers.

Earlier this year, Cadence, Keysight, Siemens and Synopsys announced design-tool certifications; in addition, Cadence and Intel launched a DTCO (Design Technology Co-Optimization) collaboration focused on optimizing Intel 14A for next-generation AI-driven design tools and IP.

As we advance toward future PDK releases, we continue to deepen engagement with ecosystem partners to validate and optimize design tools, IP, and flows, ensuring readiness at every stage of technology development. This ongoing collaboration provides customers with a predictable path to adoption, supported by a trusted ecosystem of certified solutions that accelerates design productivity and time-to-market.

Ben: From a technology development perspective, we are bringing in the broader ecosystem to help us achieve our results. This has required evolving our collaboration model with equipment and material suppliers, and earlier engagement from our process experts with suppliers to drive improvements in process and equipment capabilities. We hold regular executive summits and engineering review meetings to accelerate progress against critical deliverables.
What are you looking forward to next?

Ben: I am excited to translate the progress we are making on Intel 14A to customer success. Our immediate focus is to continue to improve performance, yield, variability and cycle time as we move toward the PDK 1.0 and volume production ready milestones. I am also looking forward to seeing customer designs advancing on Intel technologies and giving them the confidence they need to build their products with Intel Foundry as a trusted partner.

Ali: I’m looking forward to sustaining this level of quality across future releases and continuing to earn our customers’ trust by delivering on our commitments with a customer-first mindset. Our next major milestone is the Intel 14A PDK 1.0, expected in the first quarter of 2027.

I’m equally excited about the roadmap of node enhancements and performance scaling steps that will follow as Intel 14A matures. Our goal is to provide a highly stable, continuously optimized platform so our customers have the long-term capabilities they need to create differentiated, successful products for the AI era.

Ben Sell is a corporate vice president and general manager leading the front-end technology development for Intel Foundry. Ben joined Intel in 2002 and has been involved in the development of multiple advanced process nodes dating back to 65nm including 32nm, 22nm, 14nm, Intel 4 and Intel 18A. He started his career at Infineon Technologies working in DRAM capacitor pathfinding.

Ali Farhang is Corporate Vice President and General Manager of the Foundry Design Technology Platform (DTP) organization at Intel Foundry. With over 35 years of semiconductor leadership, Ali oversees the co-optimization of technology and design (DTCO), PDK development, foundational IP, reference flows, and strategic ecosystem enablement. He spent 25 years at Intel in lead product and technology enablement leadership roles before rejoining the company in 2025, following executive tenures as Corporate VP of Central Engineering at Micron and in the IP startup ecosystem.
What is a process design kit?

A process design kit, or PDK, is the reference guide chip designers use to create products on a specific manufacturing process. It brings together models, design rules and supporting materials used by electronic design automation tools.
What does the Intel 14A PDK 0.9 enable?

The Intel 14A PDK 0.9 gives customers a more mature, silicon-backed representation of the process technology for product design and production planning. It is an important milestone on the path toward the PDK 1.0 and high-volume manufacturing readiness.
What technologies are included in Intel 14A?

Intel 14A builds on the technologies in Intel 18A with RibbonFET 2 gate-all-around transistors, PowerDirect backside power delivery, and Turbo Cells, while incorporating manufacturing and development learning from Intel 18A.
What role does the ecosystem play in supporting Intel 14A development?

In addition to their use by customers, PDKs are also leveraged by electronic design automation (EDA) and IP providers to validate and certify their design tools and reusable IPs. Intel is working with a variety of ecosystem members to support the Intel 14A design platform.
What is the next Intel 14A PDK milestone?
The next major milestone is the Intel 14A PDK 1.0, expected in the first quarter of 2027.

What New: Intel announced a collaboration with SAP to bridge business IT systems and the operational technology that controls physical equipment and processes through Physical AI. This initiative establishes a model in which business intent can drive physical action while status, outcomes and exceptions flow back into enterprise systems – a closed loop in action.

SAP and Intel demonstrated this through a proof of concept (PoC) showing how Physical AI can automate warehouse material handling by connecting the SAP Extended Warehouse Management’s (SAP EWM) business context and workflow orchestration with Intel-powered edge AI and robotics hardware and software, turning enterprise requests into autonomous robot tasks.

Requests are initiated in SAP EWM and are dispatched to autonomous robots with Intel’s edge AI hardware and software. The robots transport materials and report task status and completion back to SAP EWM, creating a closed loop between enterprise workflows and physical execution. The PoC demonstrated operational improvements, including a reduction in transport distance and less repetitive manual handling.

Why it Matters: Unlike standalone robot automation, the approach closes the IT/OT loop. SAP supplies the business context, governed workflows and process rules, while Intel provides an open, real-time edge AI foundation that enables robots to perceive, navigate and act locally. Status and exceptions are returned to enterprise systems, creating a reusable blueprint for a business-aware physical workforce that can scale across sites, robot vendors and use cases.

“Organizations want to connect AI directly to physical operations. By combining SAP’s enterprise context and orchestration with Intel’s edge AI and robotics technologies, we can help customers move Physical AI from business decision to real-world execution.” said John Healy, Vice President and General Manager, Industrial and Robotics, Intel.

“Physical AI can reshape operations by connecting enterprise systems with operational technology. SAP and Intel are creating solutions to help customers integrate AI-driven automation into core processes while preserving flexibility across robotics platforms, deployment models and ecosystem partners across both hardware and software.” said Dr. Lukasz Ostrowski, Head of Physical AI and Robotics, SAP Research and Innovation, SAP SE.

Intel’s Ricky Watts joins SAP President and Chief Product Officer of Autonomous Suites, Manoj Swaminathan on stage to discuss how Intel and SAP are working together to connect enterprise intelligence with Physical AI in the real world.
Intel and SAP showcase Physical AI in action with a live robotics demo at SAP TechEd.
From Proof of Concept to Enterprise Physical AI

The collaboration is designed to translate critical business decisions made in SAP systems into efficient, precise and responsive physical execution through SAP’s physical AI solutions and Intel’s foundational physical AI hardware and software capabilities.

Intel brings an edge AI and robotics foundation designed to operationalize and scale multimodal AI, including scalable heterogeneous compute (CPU, GPU and NPU working together) for local perception, inference, navigation, inspection and real-time control. Intel’s physical AI approach combines heterogeneous compute, industrial-ready silicon, real-time capabilities, and open software, including OpenVINO Physical AI, Physical AI Studio and Robotics AI Suite. Intel’s common hardware and software foundation can help consolidate mixed workloads, reduce integration fragmentation, preserve ecosystem choice and support progression from proof of concept to repeatable deployment.

The open, robot-agnostic architecture is designed to preserve customer choice across robot vendors, operating systems, AI models, and cloud or on-premises deployment approaches. It is also designed to support scaling across platforms, sites and use cases without vendor lock-in.

Together, SAP and Intel aim to turn this proof of concept into a repeatable blueprint for enterprise Physical AI—helping customers scale intelligent automation across sites, robot platforms and operational use cases while preserving choice and flexibility.

The Youth Olympic Games Dakar 2026 are under way in Senegal from October 31 to November 13, bringing together some 2,700 young athletes across 25 sports for the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent.

As a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner, Samsung Electronics is supporting the Games with Galaxy technology — from Victory Selfie and broadcast integrations to the Samsung Open Station, an experience space inside the Youth Olympic Village. Having supported the Youth Olympic Games since the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010, Samsung is going beyond technology at Dakar 2026 to support young athletes’ personal growth as well.

For the athletes competing at Dakar 2026, reaching the Olympic stage is the result of years of dedication. But some of the most lasting lessons come from what happens along the way — overcoming setbacks, building resilience, discovering what matters beyond results.

That is why, on November 3, Samsung hosted “Beyond the Medal: Your Journey Shapes What Comes Next,” a mentoring session at the Samsung Open Station inside the Youth Olympic Village. By bringing in athletes who have walked the Olympic path before them, the session aimed to inspire pride and motivation in the next generation — and to share the spirit of openness at the heart of Samsung’s Olympic partnership.

Two IOC Athlete Role Models1 — Senegalese canoe slalom Olympian Jean-Pierre Bourhis (31) and Ugandan swimmer Jamila Lunkuse (29) — joined New Zealand tennis bronze medalist Marcus Daniell (36) for a conversation with young athletes.

Moderated by Lefa Makgato, CSR Manager at Samsung Electronics Africa, the session brought the three mentors together with 28 young athletes from 12 countries to share the journeys that shaped them — and offer a guide for exploring where life beyond sport might lead.
Open the Way: Finding Your Own Path
Makgato opened by asking each mentor where their Olympic journey began.

For Bourhis, who represented Senegal at Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 and is featured in Samsung’s “Voices of Galaxy: Paddling for the Future,” the dream took shape in 2008, when Togo’s Benjamin Boukpeti won a bronze medal in kayaking at Beijing 2008.
“As a kid, I realized an African paddler could reach the podium,” he said. “Rio 2016 showed me the way could be opened. Now my job is to keep it open for others.”

Lunkuse, who made her Olympic Games debut at 15, recalled that swimming began with friendship rather than ambition. “I wasn’t thinking about medals or the Olympics,” she said. “I just enjoyed being part of something with my friends, and that’s what built my love for the sport.”

Daniell, who ended New Zealand’s 109-year wait for an Olympic tennis medal at Tokyo 2020, pointed to choosing tennis over football at 14. “Because I’d given up a sport I loved, I knew I had to fully commit,” he said.
Break Your Boundaries: Learning Through Challenges
The conversation then turned to the biggest challenges each mentor faced.

With almost no whitewater facilities in Senegal, Bourhis had to build his training base in France — while holding down a full-time job as an engineer in electric vehicle repair. “As an engineer, I see a limit as a problem to solve, not a wall,” he said. “I train before work, during lunch, or late at night. What keeps me going is purpose.”

Lunkuse spoke openly about the anxiety she faced ahead of Rio 2016. “I became so focused on qualifying times that I no longer enjoyed it,” she said. “It was only when I took time away that I could see what I was going through and what help I needed — and that’s what got me to Rio 2016.”

Daniell described a knee injury in 2022 that kept him out for nearly two years. “What got me through was having something bigger than tennis,” he said. “Everyone fails. Those who last are the ones who learn to pick themselves up when they fall.”
Beyond the Game: Turning Experience Into Opportunity
Finally, Makgato asked how the lessons of sport carried into what came next.

Through nonprofit work, Bourhis is building a canoeing ecosystem in Senegal. “We’re building it step by step — and building canoes locally makes the sport more affordable, creates local jobs, and leaves a lasting legacy,” he said. “I want to give the next generation the tools to build their own way.”
Lunkuse, a youth coach and World Aquatics Athletes’ Committee member, urges young athletes to look beyond results. “Results do not define your value,” she said.

Similarly, Daniell — an IOC Athletes’ Commission member and founder of High Impact Athletes, a nonprofit connecting athletes with charities — advised: “Look for a goal beyond personal success. For me, that was what kept pushing me forward.”
Opening Possibilities for the Next Generation

Makgato closed the session with a story of her own. Growing up in a small township in South Africa, she first encountered a computer at 18 — at one of Samsung’s Solar Powered Internet Schools. She later joined Samsung Electronics Africa, where she now leads CSR programs across the continent, including Solve for Tomorrow, giving the next generation the kind of opportunity she once received. Having seen firsthand how a single opportunity can change a life, she had good reason to stand before the young athletes that day.

“I know firsthand how access to technology and education opens doors you may never have imagined. Where you are today doesn’t determine where you’re going,” she said. “We wanted to encourage young athletes to stay open to new ideas and recognize the potential they have to shape their own futures.”

• IOC Athlete Role Models (ARMs) have been part of the Youth Olympic Games since Singapore 2010. Selected by International Federations for each sport, these experienced Olympians stay on site to speak with young athletes and lead workshops on topics such as career management and injury prevention, helping shape the athletes of tomorrow. ↩︎

Samsung Electronics today announced that its updated Sleep Apnea feature1 is now available on Galaxy Watch and Ring.2 Following United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance in July, the updated feature has also received approval from Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS). With this update, Samsung becomes the first company in the world to bring sleep apnea risk detection on a smart ring.

The updated Sleep Apnea feature, available through the Samsung Health Monitor app, marks a significant leap forward from its predecessor. The enhanced algorithm analyzes a user’s vitals during sleep in greater depth and now provides insight into the level of breathing disruptions detected — going beyond the previous sleep apnea risk assessment to deliver more comprehensive, meaningful information that helps users better understand their condition, which can lead to productive conversations with healthcare professionals.

Most notably, Samsung is extending sleep apnea risk detection to a smart ring for the first time. Galaxy Ring’s comfortable, lightweight design makes it easy to wear through the night and convenient for sleep measurement, encouraging nightly wear. With the feature’s low data requirement, users can gain meaningful insight into their sleep health from as little as two nights of monitoring within a 10-day period. By offering the feature on both Galaxy Watch and Galaxy Ring, Samsung lets users monitor their sleep health in the way that best fits their lifestyle.

Samsung’s original Sleep Apnea feature previously received groundbreaking U.S. FDA De Novo authorization in February, 2024 — the first of its kind for a wearable device designed to detect signs of moderate to severe sleep apnea. Building on that clinically validated reliability, the updated feature has now also been approved by Korea’s MFDS last October. Samsung will continue to expand the feature’s availability so more people around the world can detect possible signs of sleep apnea and take proactive steps toward better sleep health. This underscores Samsung’s dedication to accessible preventive care, with sleep health serving as a fundamental pillar.

“Samsung has long worked to make sleep health a simple and seamless part of everyday life,” said Jongmin Choi, Head of Health R&D Group, Mobile eXperience (MX) Business, Samsung Electronics. “This approval from Korea’s MFDS, along with our introduction of the world’s first support for a smart ring, reflects our commitment to accessible innovation. We are giving people the tools to help spot possible early signs of sleep apnea and take charge of their wellbeing.”

• The Sleep Apnea feature is an over-the-counter (OTC) software-only, mobile medical application operating on a compatible Samsung Galaxy Wearable and Phone. This feature is intended to detect signs of moderate to severe sleep apnea in the form of significant breathing disruptions in users 18 years and older, over a two-night monitoring period. It is intended for on-demand use and requires two nights of valid data within a 10-day period. This feature is not intended for users who have previously been diagnosed with sleep apnea. Users should not use this feature to replace traditional methods of diagnosis and treatment by a qualified clinician. ↩︎
• Available on Galaxy Watch 9 running Wear OS 7.0 or higher. Support for Galaxy Watch 7/8 will expand through future software updates. ↩︎

Seoul, October 28, 2026 – SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com) announced today that it has recorded 104.6155 trillion won in revenues, 83.3338 trillion won in operating profit (with an operating margin of 80%), and 39.7756 trillion won in net profit (with a net margin of 38%) in the third quarter.

During the earnings presentation, CEO Kwak Noh-Jung explained the background of the company’s decisions regarding the Solidigm IPO and its principle to share the returns from strategic investment with shareholders.

“The IPO was intended to raise external capital for the expansion of Solidigm’s production facilities, and thereby to lighten our own investment burden and broaden our capacity for shareholder returns,” CEO Kwak said. “However, after carefully considering recent financial market conditions and other factors, we concluded that proceeding at this time would not be the best way to achieve the originally anticipated outcome. We have therefore discontinued our review.”

“Our principle has been to share the majority of the gains from successful strategic investments with our shareholders. These gains help replenish our capacity for shareholder returns, which may temporarily decline as we prepare for the future, allowing us to continue investing boldly in sustainable growth while protecting shareholder interests,” he continued. “In line with this principle, we have decided to return the gains realized from our investment in Kioxia this year to shareholders through a special dividend and we will remain committed to upholding this principle so that our shareholders can directly benefit from the returns from our strategic investments.”
Record quarterly results in both revenue and operating profit and revenue surpasses 100 trillion won for the first time

In a market environment in which prices of key products have risen on the back of growing demand for AI memory, the company once again posted all-time-high quarterly results in both revenue and operating profit, underpinned by the competitiveness of its high-value-added products. In particular, revenue exceeded 100 trillion won for the first time in the company’s history. Revenue and operating profit increased by 32% and 38%, from the previous quarter, respectively.
* Q2 2026: Revenue of 79.3187 trillion won, Operating Profit of 60.5426 trillion won

By product, DRAM results were driven by a significant increase in sales of server DDR5 while HBM4 shipments began in earnest. In NAND, sales of 321-layer TLC eSSD expanded, and high-value-added products for data centers continued to grow across the board.

The company’s financial structure has also become significantly concrete. At the end of the third quarter, cash and cash equivalents stood at 114.5 trillion won, up 26.5 trillion won from the end of the previous quarter, while borrowings decreased by 2.8 trillion won to 15.8 trillion won. As a result, net cash increased to 98.7 trillion won.
Memory supply shortage to persist through 2030

SK hynix analyzed that a virtuous cycle has taken hold in which AI-driven productivity gains and new revenue generation in areas such as software development, customer service, and search lead to greater AI adoption, which in turn drives increased investment in infrastructure. It also projected that, as the drivers of AI investment move beyond the early stage, when a small number of companies accounted for most of it, and broaden to include general enterprises and nation-level initiatives, the global AI data center infrastructure market will continue to grow steadily.

The company likewise expects the memory market to sustain its growth, led in the short term by enterprise and personal AI and, over the mid-to-long term, by physical AI such as autonomous driving and robotics.

The company assessed that supply, on the other hand, is not keeping pace with the growth of the market. Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.
Expanding production capacity and strengthening product competitiveness to achieve a further step up in growth next year

Building on these favorable conditions, the company plans to accelerate the expansion of production capacity and the strengthening of product competitiveness in order to sustain the current growth momentum, and to scale up revenue and profit one step further next year.

First, the company plans to rapidly increase the portion of its 10nm-class 6th generation (1c) process technology and expand sales of DDR5 and LPDDR5 SOCAMM for AI servers, thereby further strengthening its DRAM portfolio centered on high-value-added products.

To respond to surging HBM demand, the company will ramp up M15X to maximum capacity by the end of the year to increase HBM4 production. Accordingly, the company expects HBM4 to surpass HBM3E in both shipment volume and revenue in the fourth quarter and to establish itself as a mainstream product.

In NAND, the company will raise the ratio of its 321-layer process to more than half of its domestic production capacity in the fourth quarter, and thereby increase the supply of high-performance, high-capacity eSSD. Over the mid-to-long term, the company intends to develop NAND into a core solution that enhances the throughput and economic efficiency of AI services, based on HBF and system optimization technologies.
Long-term agreements secured for more than 50% of 2027~2028 production capacity and the company to drastically expand investment next year

To improve mid-to-long term demand visibility and solidify its growth foundation, SK hynix is expanding long-term agreements (LTAs) with customers. The company has currently signed LTAs with 14 major customers, including leading global cloud service providers (CSPs), and is also proactively discussing with a number of customers the possibility of extending the contract terms, which are typically five years.

The LTA volume secured to date corresponds to more than 50% of total production capacity for 2027 and 2028. In particular, by introducing a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers, the company has established a structure that secures stable profitability while allowing flexible responses to market changes.

Backed by the demand visibility, the company is also moving to expand its production capabilities. Next year, with the Yongin Phase 1 entering full-scale operation and domestic and overseas infrastructure investment gaining momentum, investment is expected to increase significantly. The company nevertheless plans to adjust the scale and timing of its investment flexibly, after carefully weighing customer demand, product competitiveness, profitability and investment efficiency.
Most of the gains from the Kioxia investment to be shared with shareholders, with approximately 100 trillion won in shareholder returns to be executed this year

As previously indicated in August, SK hynix announced its additional shareholder return plan. For fiscal year 2026, the company will pursue shareholder returns totaling approximately 100 trillion won, comprising cash dividends of 30 trillion won or more and share repurchases and cancellations of 60 trillion won or more in total, including the 40 trillion won announced in August. Through this, the company intends to fulfill its commitment to return 50% or more of free cash flow (FCF). Of this, the 40 trillion won share repurchase announced in August was completed last week, and the shares will be cancelled shortly.

The company also set out its principles: the dividend amount will be determined on the basis of operating results; if significant investment gains arise, they will be returned additionally through special dividends; and share repurchases will continue every quarter.

At today’s meeting, the Board of Directors resolved on a third-quarter cash dividend of 14 trillion won and a share repurchase of 20 trillion won. Of the shares to be repurchased, 10 trillion won, earmarked for shareholder returns, will be cancelled in full, while the remaining approximately 10 trillion won will be used for employee compensation and is not included in the shareholder return total.

The third-quarter dividend is 20,000 won per share, consisting of a 10,000-won dividend reflecting improved earnings and a 10,000 won special dividend that shares the gains from the Kioxia investment. The company has decided to return to shareholders most of the gains realized from its Kioxia investment this year.

“The customer trust built through our technological competitiveness is leading to long-term contracts, and our business structure is transforming into one with earnings stability and mid-to-long term demand visibility,” CEO Kwak emphasized. “We will carry our HBM competitiveness over to next-generation products, and we will also increase the rewards we share with our shareholders as our business outcome and investment result grow.”

If you want to compete, you need to be multi-model. And if you want to take advantage of everything that different AI models have to offer, you need a great harness. But building one that works seamlessly across multiple models and surfaces is incredibly hard. You need to solve for performance, quality, and cost. And then you have to maintain it, which is even harder.

Luckily, the GitHub engineering team built a best-in-class, truly multi-model harness, which we’ve adopted company-wide. The Microsoft Copilot harness powers Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, the GitHub Copilot app, the CLI, VS Code, and more. And today, we’re making that harness available through Microsoft Foundry. That gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. You get the right model for the job without switching the harness or the rest of your tech stack. That frees up your time, energy, and resources to focus on your bottom line.
What’s a harness, and why is it hard?

If the model supplies the intelligence, the harness is everything around the model. It’s the orchestration layer that gives an agent the right instructions, context, execution environment, and controls to accomplish meaningful work. And a harness worth its salt has support for open standards like MCP and agent skills, as well as agent plugins.

This is a fast-moving space. A frontier model today might fall behind tomorrow. And building your own harness or model router to keep up can be painful and slow. Now, you can build on the same harness Microsoft and GitHub ship in our own products, and you don’t have to maintain it.

We invest in science and engineering work to continually improve and evolve the harness and ensure high-quality, efficient, and low-cost performance across a range of models and workloads. The benefits compound for us and our customers who use the harness to build and run their own agents. Improve the harness, and every surface it touches benefits.
Born in GitHub, battle-tested at enterprise scale

The Copilot harness was built by the same GitHub engineers behind new technologies like our multi-model orchestration. And those technologies are only possible because we built our own harness. Designed to be fast, token-efficient, and predictable, it was our original, high-quality harness. And it had the highest satisfaction among our most demanding audience: developers. That’s why we’re standardizing all of our Copilot experiences on the strongest foundation possible.

The harness is built to perform across model families, with 20+ frontier models plus bring your own key, so you can use the right model for the right job. Instead of doing the work to keep up with and eval new models, lean on us to intelligently route work to the right model or models based on the task.

Our harness is flexible and configurable to any type of app, agent, or service. We recently ported the harness runtime to Rust, which has resulted in industry-leading performance and reductions in both session overhead and time-to-first token. And because the Copilot harness powers surfaces across Microsoft, it’s battle-tested and proven performant at the scale of millions of users and hundreds of real-world use cases.

A unified harness lets us ship faster, learn faster, and improve Copilot over time. And because the agents you build in Foundry can run on the same harness we’ve adopted across Microsoft, our continuous harness improvements will benefit your agents, too.

The SDK is available to download, or you can run the harness in the cloud, all managed by Foundry. Our platforms remain open and interoperable, so you can continue to bring in any harness and framework you want, too.
With the Copilot harness, Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox, with governance and optimization built in from day one. You bring the instructions, skills, tools, and model choice.
This is an important step towards our vision of a stronger system around the model that preserves choice. It represents the best of GitHub, brought to the Microsoft platform and beyond.
We’ll keep pushing the harness forward, so you can focus on what only you can build.

Last year at Ignite, we introduced the concept of Frontier Transformation and how it is different from any technology-led pursuit, because it requires us to focus on business outcomes first. It starts with a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. There is no path where this notion of infinite cognitive compute replaces human purpose. Frontier Transformation is an opportunity for a wholesale reinvention of how you think about your unique ideas coming to life and how your organization can thrive in your industry.

Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. We are taking a platform approach toward enabling the same: Copilot as the place to call home for interacting with AI to empower human ambition; the Microsoft IQ platform to compound and amplify your intelligence from within while protecting your unique differentiation; and Agent 365 to enable Trust and Observability at every layer of the stack so that you can govern, manage, secure and get business value and return out of the capabilities you deliver.

Our latest earnings are another important marker on that journey. Behind the numbers are thousands of customers, partners, developers and employees putting AI to work in meaningful ways. We have so many inspiring stories from our customers that highlight these outcomes, and below are some of our favorites.

Volkswagen has scaled Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees as it expands the role of AI in decision-making and knowledge-based processes across the enterprise. Building on Copilot Chat adoption that reached more than 300,000 monthly active users, employees are now using Copilot with Work IQ for more advanced scenarios, bringing greater organizational context to decision-making and knowledge-based work. Volkswagen is also working with Microsoft to further scale its Intelligent Data Foundation on Microsoft Fabric to make data easier to find, understand and use across the entire company. With this investment, Volkswagen is demonstrating how companies have evolved from using Copilot as a productivity tool to an operating system to empower human ambition.

Following a successful pilot, Fujitsu is scaling Microsoft Copilot across its global workforce of approximately 100,000. Copilot usage has surpassed 90%, and the company is using the tool to connect employees with specialized agents and business systems. AI agents are already automating roughly 75% of initial responses and triage for a service desk that receives nearly 300,000 inquiries annually, while new agents are supporting work across sales, systems engineering, procurement, finance and accounting. As customer zero, Fujitsu is using Copilot as the front door to a multi-agent work environment and using insights from its own AI adoption to better serve its customers.

KOHLER is using GitHub Copilot to transform software development, with one organization improving code releases by 25% and reducing error defects by 75%. These engineering breakthroughs are part of a broader effort to embed AI processes across the company, spanning IT, finance, marketing, supply chain and operations. Microsoft Copilot has reached 98% adoption, saving an average of 2 to 5 hours per month as employees are making informed decisions and getting answers faster in the flow of their work. Employees across the company have also created more than 3,000 agents to date, with hundreds active daily.

At Krafton, Microsoft Security Copilot and Microsoft Defender XDR are helping the security team respond to a growing volume and complexity of threats. The global gaming company automated key parts of security operations, from alerting and investigation to reporting, combining Microsoft Security solutions with its own systems and data to quickly gather context that helps distinguish real threats from false positives. This approach is having immediate results: security alert recognition time has fallen by approximately 95% to less than one minute, investigation work that previously took tens of minutes now takes about three minutes and roughly 95% of report creation has been automated. By taking on repetitive work, AI is giving Krafton’s security professionals more time to focus on responding to real threats and making critical security decisions.

To accelerate discovery across decades of scientific data, NASA is making complex information easier to explore through Microsoft Copilot. NASA employees are using Copilot to sift through massive amounts of academic literature and streamline daily tasks, and specialized assistants are helping researchers navigate complex Earth science data through natural language, extending access to information that once required significant technical expertise. Hydrology Copilot, for example, can analyze variables like precipitation and soil moisture to help communities better understand water conditions, prepare for droughts and anticipate flood risks, while automatically performing calculations and analyses.

To transform frontline work, Williams, a US natural gas company, is using Microsoft Copilot to help employees spend less time searching documents and completing manual processes, and more time on critical field operations. Copilot helps teams generate plans, interpret procedures, assess regulatory requirements, troubleshoot issues and complete safety reporting, while employees can create agents tailored to their own workflows. Demonstrating that the person closest to a problem is often the best one to solve it, one operations technician built an anomaly detector using Copilot that compares equipment data against baseline statistics and alerts teams to potential issues before they become costly or dangerous. Since deploying Copilot, AI adoption at Williams has grown from single digits to more than 90%, helping employees accelerate operations, improve reporting and compliance and identify equipment issues earlier.

Bristol Myers Squibb has rolled out Microsoft Copilot to 25,000 employees, reaching 96% adoption, and is now putting AI agents to work across everyday use cases such as document review and project management in support of the company’s mission to bring more medicines to more patients faster. One agent, called RABIT, analyzes meeting transcripts, surfaces action items and delivers insights directly within employees’ workflows.

Facing rising patient demand and financial pressures, Brown University Health is using Dragon Copilot to give clinicians more time to focus on patients. The health system adopted Dragon Copilot, and an early pilot across 420 clinicians found users spent less time on after-hours documentation and reported lower cognitive burden. Building on that experience, Brown University Health deployed Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio across departments, which led to the creation of more than 24 AI agents to support clinical workflows, hospital policies, patient access and operations. These AI solutions are not only supporting clinicians in the flow of their work but also helping to improve the patient experience and access to care.
Microsoft IQ compounds and protects your intelligence

BNY has made AI part of how its employees work through Eliza, its in-house AI platform built with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot and GitHub Copilot – with plans to add Work IQ. More than 300 solutions now run on Eliza, ranging from inquiry management to client onboarding, and 100% of employees have been trained on the platform. Across the bank, that scale is translating into meaningful results: client transaction inquiries are being resolved 80% faster and AI-assisted client onboarding is 20% faster on average. Through the Microsoft CEO Co-Innovation program, BNY also worked with Microsoft to develop an AI research capability with Foundry that investigates complex data issues, analyzes context across multiple sources, identifies likely root causes and recommends next steps, bringing AI-assisted reasoning into processes that have traditionally relied on human investigation alone.

Docusign is helping 1.9 million customers across 180 countries turn agreement data into actionable business insights. The company built an Intelligent Agreement Management platform on Microsoft Azure and used Microsoft Foundry to shift from general-purpose models to a system of task-specific models that better understand context. This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents in a single day, with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production, while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected.

To help marketers create more effective content, Kantar turned decades of proprietary advertising intelligence into action with Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry. Working with Microsoft Frontier Company, Kantar connected its LINK AI platform to its proprietary intelligence, AI models and creative workflows, enabling marketers to evaluate, optimize and generate content before it goes to market. The new approach can process and score large volumes of videos 20x faster while reducing platform operating costs by 4x, helping customers move from insight to action in minutes rather than hours. By bringing its unique intelligence into a continuous loop of observation and improvement, Kantar is creating new ways to help marketers turn insight into better creative and business outcomes.

Kinaxis, a Canadian supply chain software company, runs Maestro, its AI-driven supply chain orchestration platform, on Microsoft Azure. Maestro helps businesses make better decisions faster amid constant disruption. It brings together traditionally disparate business data like sales orders, inventory and production capacity with external signals like weather, market shifts and breaking news to give planners a near real-time view of their supply chains. With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change.

Moody’s is making more than a century of credit and risk intelligence directly accessible through Microsoft Copilot, giving customers trusted, protected context for complex decisions. Through a federated connector built using Model Context Protocol, customers can access live, decision-grade Moody’s intelligence through Researcher in Copilot and within Word, Excel and Teams, without copying or exporting the underlying data. A single question can synthesize information across credit ratings, company financials, ownership information and physical risk models, helping customers reach insights in minutes instead of spending hours or days on research and analysis. This brings trusted, connected intelligence directly into workflows where customers make complex decisions.

To turn conversations into actionable intelligence at global scale, Plaud, an AI hardware and software company, is using Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to power transcription, summarization and AI inference across long-form audio and multilingual scenarios. Serving more than 2 million users worldwide, Plaud increased transcription accuracy and processing speed by 35% and improved inference performance by 30%, helping professionals turn spoken content into structured outputs and insights. Even as its user base doubled, the company used Foundry’s elastic scaling and flexible deployment models to reduce overall compute costs by 35%, while strengthening its ability to meet security, privacy and compliance requirements across global markets.

Rockwell Automation built a Maintenance Copilot using Microsoft Foundry to put decades of manufacturing expertise in the hands of employees. The AI assistant brings together expert knowledge from veteran engineers, manufacturing data and machine manuals, allowing technicians to quickly identify likely causes of equipment issues, see how colleagues have solved similar problems and access step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. At its Singapore factory, the approach has helped reduce machine downtime by 33% and cut servicing and spare-part costs by about 25%. Rockwell estimates it has also reduced the time it takes new workers to learn to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three months.

With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring. After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide, TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on.

Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production, the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence.
Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack

To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale. With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities. With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation.

Insight Enterprises, a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale. As a Microsoft customer zero organization for Agent 365, Insight Enterprises is quick to adopt new capabilities internally and pass those learnings on to clients. With Microsoft engineering, it tested how Microsoft and third-party agents could be observed, managed, governed and secured through a unified control plane. To date, Insight Enterprises has discovered 9,734 agents with visibility into which are active, what data they can access and how to monitor their activity over time. The experience has helped Insight Enterprises build practical AI governance expertise it can bring to customers, including organizations in highly regulated industries.

KPMG is adopting Microsoft Agent 365 to manage and secure AI agents across its global organization, providing centralized observability and control as it scales agentic AI. Agent 365 will also strengthen KPMG Workbench, its multi-agent platform built on Microsoft Foundry that coordinates agents across client service delivery platforms. At the same time, KPMG is expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 276,000 professionals worldwide, helping embed AI more deeply across audit, tax and advisory services. Together, these capabilities are giving KPMG the confidence and security to move agents from experimentation into enterprise-wide deployment, while helping clients do the same.

Operating in one of the most highly regulated industries, where protecting sensitive customer information is essential, Truist Financial Corporation is using Agent 365 to manage, govern and observe more than 13,000 AI declarative agents across its organization. Truist manages its agent ecosystem with discipline: every agent has an accountable owner and agents are automatically disabled after 45 days of inactivity. That rigor is driving strong retention and adoption, with more than 8,000 agents active each month. Building on this trusted foundation, Truist has advanced its broader AI strategy through their investment of more than 50,000 Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite seats.

Every quarter gives us an opportunity to step back and look at the progress we are making with our customers and partners around the world. What continues to strike me is not simply the pace of change, but the ambition we see from organizations using technology to achieve aspirations that simply weren’t possible before. We look forward to working alongside you on the path to becoming Frontier, and we hope to see many of you at Microsoft Ignite this year in November to share the latest innovations that will enable you to reach that destination.

SAN FRANCISCO and LOS ANGELES — September 16, 2026 — Today at Dreamforce, Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), the #1 AI CRM, and Live Nation Entertainment (NYSE: LYV) announced an expansion of Live Nation’s use of Agentforce, bringing 24/7 fan support to Live Nation venues across the U.S.

This expansion builds on Live Nation’s innovation at BottleRock Napa Valley, a weekend of music alongside food, wine, and culinary experiences. With multiple stages and experiences happening at once, fans are constantly deciding what to see, where to go, and what to do next. To help fans arrive prepared and make it easier to discover everything the festival had to offer, Live Nation debuted Melody: an agentic festival guide providing on-demand expertise powered by Service Cloud.

Fans could ask Melody questions about artist set times, stage locations, and more, while receiving personalized recommendations, including food near stages and must-see artists. With communication and data guardrails applied to every interaction, Melody also maintained conversation history and session context. This allowed Melody to understand follow-up questions and provide more relevant responses over the course of a conversation.

Built with a fully headless React architecture embedded directly in the BottleRock app, Melody was deployed in under 30 days from concept to production, in partnership with Salesforce’s Forward Deployed Engineering team and Salesforce Professional Services. During the 12-day launch window leading up to BottleRock 2026, Melody logged over 37,000 fan interactions and 17,000 customer service sessions. This helped attendees arrive better prepared, with 85% getting the answers they needed within three responses.
Live Nation is now building on those learnings with Venue Agent, bringing the same focus on useful, on-demand information to even more fans.

According to Live Nation research, 78% of fans want guidance ahead of a show to help make their experience smoother, including transportation and event information. Venue Agent gives fans 24/7 access to that information by answering questions across Live Nation venue websites — seamlessly responding to inquiries about parking, what to bring to the venue, accessible seating, door times, and more. Branding and event information are automatically customized, creating a more personalized experience for each venue and fans.

Live Nation leverages a single agent system, powered by Service Cloud with Data Cloud, to deliver accurate, venue-specific answers. Instead of building separate agents for every venue, the company’s headless Venue Agent uses Data Cloud to instantly identify where to pull the correct information. If a fan asks for a human or has a question outside the agent’s knowledge, the conversation is routed directly through Slack to the fan engagement team that is monitoring the agents and on hand to quickly respond to requests outside the agent’s knowledge.

Salesforce becomes the Title Sponsor and Technological partner of FIDE.

Partnership brings the Agentforce 360 portfolio, including Slack, to the world’s largest chess events and forums, powering real-time player rankings and AI-driven fan experiences for over 800 million global fans.

SAN FRANCISCO and LAUSANNE, September 10, 2026 — Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), the #1 AI CRM, today announced a landmark multiyear partnership with the International Chess Federation (FIDE), becoming the Title Sponsor of the FIDE World Championship Matches 2026–28 and the official AI partner of the FIDE World Chess Championship and FIDE Rankings. The collaboration will utilize the full power of Agentforce 360 — the complete portfolio of Salesforce AI solutions that power the Agentic Enterprise — to unify every layer of its operations, player rankings, and fan connections onto a single platform. This includes leveraging Slack to further connect FIDE’s global teams and streamline workflows.
A partnership built for the championship

The partnership between FIDE and Salesforce covers the 2026 and 2028 World Championship Matches, the 2027 Women’s Match, and the world rankings. The official world championship matches and rankings will be presented as the Salesforce FIDE World Chess Championships and Salesforce FIDE Rankings.
A new standard for chess: Intelligence meets innovation

FIDE has been the governing body of chess since 1924, today overseeing 204 national member federations, 1.5 million rated players, and tens of thousands of rated events per year across 195 countries. With Agentforce 360, FIDE will run its entire operation on a single, intelligent platform, unlocking new ways to connect with players, federations, and fans around the world.

Fans will experience this transformation firsthand through the Chess Concierge Agent, powered by Agentforce 360, that answers questions on ratings, rules, and live tournament status for 1.2 million monthly visitors in any language. Internally, Agentforce 360 will help FIDE more efficiently run its operations. This includes powering Move of the Day: a workflow that analyzes moves from elite competition and surfaces them to the FIDE expert panel via Slack for final selection. Slack will also connect FIDE’s federations and commissions worldwide, giving officers behind-the-scenes visibility into ratings and operations.

Core to FIDE’s authority is its rating system, the universally recognized measure of every chess player’s skill that is used to track standings, history, and predictive analysis. FIDE’s ELO Player Rating Agent will offer a conversational lookup of any FIDE player, including historical trends, current standings, insights into results, and predictions. It also automates the rating data pipelines across 204 federations, replacing manual batch processes with near-real-time ratings. Underpinning this is Data 360, which will unify FIDE’s player database of active online chess players and 60,000+ annual event streams to offer consolidated real-time fan and player profiles.

We’re truly honored to partner with FIDE and bring the power of the Agentic Enterprise to a sport with such rich history and passionate fans.

“Chess is one of the world’s most beloved games, cherished by hundreds of millions of people across every culture and corner of the globe,” said Patrick Stokes, President, Applications and Marketing, Salesforce. “We’re truly honored to partner with FIDE and bring the power of the Agentic Enterprise to a sport with such rich history and passionate fans. The International Chess Federation (FIDE) is the governing body of the sport of chess, and it regulates all international chess competitions. Constituted as a non-governmental institution, it was recognized by the International Olympic Committee as a Global Sporting Organization in 1999.

FIDE currently has its headquarters in Lausanne, but it was initially founded in 1924 in Paris under the motto “Gens una Sumus” (Latin for “We are one Family”). It was one of the very first International Sports Federations, alongside the governing bodies of the sports of Football, Cricket, Swimming, and Auto Racing. It is now one of the largest, encompassing 204 countries as affiliate members, in the form of National Chess Federations. Chess is nowadays a truly global sport, with dozens of millions of players in all the continents, and more than 60 million games on average played every day.

Tokyo, Japan — Sony Group Corporation ("Sony") today announced the launch of the Sony Onchain Entertainment Incubation Program, a global incubation program for startups and creators, beginning October 29, 2026. Through the program, Sony aims to foster the growth of "onchain entertainment" which leverages blockchain technology to enable more direct connections between creators and fans, as well as new forms of value creation and community building.

Recent advances in blockchain technology are opening new possibilities not only for the ownership and use of content and digital assets, but also for how creators engage with fans and build communities. As a company with diverse entertainment businesses, Sony is working to create next-generation entertainment experiences by leveraging these technologies.

The program will invite creators from around the world that use Soneium, a blockchain, to create new entertainment experiences and business models by bringing together content, communities and digital assets. These may include initiatives that build new relationships between creators and fans, deliver new forms of value through community participation, or explore new revenue opportunities leveraging digital content, among other efforts to explore the potential of onchain technology in entertainment.

Selected projects will receive support toward commercialization, including access to Soneium's technology infrastructure, opportunities for co-creation with Sony Group companies, business development and marketing support, opportunities for community engagement, and access to fundraising opportunities. Through these forms of support, the program aims to help projects move beyond technical validation toward services and experiences that deliver tangible value to users.

Since 2024, Sony has been advancing initiatives in the onchain space centered on Soneium. Through two previous incubation programs, Sony has selected and supported a total of 43 projects from around the world.

Building on the knowledge and networks developed through these initiatives, the new program will focus specifically on onchain entertainment. Through co-creation with creators, startups and communities, Sony aims to foster new entertainment experiences in which people can discover and engage with content, support creators and communities, and share in the value they help create.

Sony Group will continue to explore the possibilities enabled by onchain technology and, through co-creation with innovators around the world, contribute to the future of entertainment by creating value for both creators and fans.

Broadcom Fixes 89 New Open Source Vulnerabilities in TrueSource Spring Enterprise, Reaching 408 Total in 2026

PALO ALTO, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO), a global technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, today shipped fixes for 89 novel vulnerabilities in TrueSource Spring Enterprise to its critical infrastructure customers and others who qualify for early access, ahead of public disclosure. This brings the total number of vulnerabilities fixed across TrueSource offerings to 408.

Patches only secure an environment once deployed. To close that gap, Spring Enterprise adds TrueSource Hub to help enterprises assess application exposure, prioritize critical fixes, and track status. Additionally, build plugins for Application Advisor automate patching within existing Maven or Gradle workflows, generating update pull requests to streamline merging approved fixes.
A sustained investment in open source security

Building on its June 2026 open source commitment, Broadcom uses Frontier AI scanning and advanced research to find and fix vulnerabilities. TrueSource Spring Enterprise delivers simultaneous fixes across all supported versions, giving legacy releases immediate access, while providing security-only patches for current versions to speed deployment. Detailed vulnerability information will be published when fixes reach the community and CVEs are issued.

Scale & Impact: Reaching a massive footprint of downloads of Spring and Reactor libraries in 2026, Broadcom engineers fixed 406 new vulnerabilities, delivered over 1,090 fixes (including 798 backports), reviewed 2,600+ reports, and filtered out 3,000+ false alarms.
Key High/Critical Broadcom Fixes Earlier This Year:
• Spring (June): Fixed a remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-41855, CVSS 8.1) across four supported lines simultaneously.
• Netty Dependency (June): Discovered a DNS redirection vulnerability (CVE-2026-47691, CVSS 10.0) and addressed with the community maintainers and fixed for all supported Spring versions.
• RabbitMQ (July): Fixed a credential forgery vulnerability (CVE-2026-67404, CVSS 9.2) across four supported lines at once.

“Security isn’t a one-time initiative; it’s an ongoing commitment. In June, we pledged to identify and resolve Spring vulnerabilities faster than ever, and today’s release demonstrates our continued momentum,” said Purnima Padmanabhan, general manager, Tanzu Division, Broadcom. “Our customers receive critical fixes early in a deployable format, with complete visibility into where patches belong and confirmation when they land. Crucially, fixes are contributed back to the open source community—because open source remains resilient only when businesses actively invest in ecosystem health.”
See it, prioritize it, fix it, prove it

Most enterprises know they run open source. Few can say exactly which applications run which versions, which are out of support, and which need a fix published this morning. TrueSource Spring Enterprise closes that gap with four capabilities that work together:

• Assess every repository. TrueSource Hub connects to an organization’s code repositories and shows the security state of the open source components every application depends on, across Java, Python, and JavaScript libraries, container images, and data services, along with its patch status, in a live view rather than a one-time audit.

• Prioritize the fixes that matter. When Broadcom publishes a fix, Hub shows which applications need it and how exposed they are, so security and engineering leaders can direct effort to the applications that carry the most risk. TrueSource works with the vulnerability scanners that teams already use. Snyk, for example, is actively partnering with Broadcom so that customers can recognize Broadcom-patched Spring versions as fixed, with the goal of reducing unnecessary alerts and keeping teams from chasing alerts for already-resolved vulnerabilities.

• Apply patches in the build. For Spring applications, Spring Application Advisor plugins integrate directly into existing Maven and Gradle builds. Fixes and version upgrades arrive as reviewable pull requests built on deterministic recipes verified by TrueSource engineers. Additionally, the new integration with JFrog Zero-Touch Remediation delivers instant protection. By automatically delivering verified, backward-compatible TrueSource fixes to builds, security teams can stop waiting on manual pull requests and dependency overrides - keeping software secure with zero friction.

• Prove it through pipeline audits. Every build records its source and the libraries it contains and reports that to TrueSource, so security leaders can show their boards and leadership exactly which libraries shipped and where each fix was applied.
TrueSource by Broadcom is Broadcom’s portfolio of enterprise open source software, verified by engineers and delivered from one trusted source. It has three offerings:

• TrueSource Spring Enterprise for the Spring framework Broadcom maintains, with CVE-only patches, the security fix and nothing else, delivered for every supported version at the same time so teams can apply them without an upgrade, plus the tooling announced today.

• TrueSource Trusted Artifacts for verified open source libraries in Java, Python, and JavaScript, and the Secure Images catalog of container images, covering the middleware, runtimes, and backing services applications depend on.

• TrueSource Data Services for the data engines applications rely on: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Valkey, and RabbitMQ, with self-service provisioning, fleet management across environments, and enterprise support for the engines themselves, including prescribed high availability and disaster recovery.

TrueSource Spring Enterprise, featuring TrueSource Hub and build plugins, is generally available today. Its 87 fixes are accessible immediately to early-access and critical infrastructure customers, with public CVE release to follow. TrueSource Spring Enterprise, Trusted Artifacts, and Data Services are offered via tiered site licensing. Learn more at https://www.broadcom.com/products/software/truesource.
