NEW YORK and CHARLOTTE, N.C. and PALO ALTO, Calif., Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Blackstone (NYSE: BX), Citi (NYSE: C) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) (the "Lead Financial Partners") today announced a $63 billion transaction to enable the deployment of AI compute capacity, leveraging Broadcom Inc.'s (NASDAQ: AVGO) technology, for Anthropic. This transaction is part of the strategic compute capacity agreement previously announced by Broadcom, with expected deliveries starting in calendar 2027.

The transaction will be executed through a newly formed special purpose vehicle ("SPV") with committed financing from the Lead Financial Partners to support the purchase of Broadcom XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions to be leased to Anthropic. The first lien portion of the financing is being arranged by Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley, with Blackstone as the sole provider of the committed portion of the second lien financing. Broadcom is providing residual value support to the SPV for the amount equivalent to the first lien portion of the financing. This transaction highlights the deep collaboration across the AI technology and financial ecosystems.

Jon Gray, President and COO, Blackstone, said, "The rapidly growing demand for AI is creating an enormous opportunity to finance compute capacity at scale. We're proud to help advance this buildout with Broadcom."

Dan Simkowitz, Co-President of Morgan Stanley, said, "This transaction represents an important milestone in enabling the next buildout of AI compute capacity. Morgan Stanley has been at the forefront of innovation in designing scalable capital solutions for AI infrastructure, and we are proud to continue to advance new financing structures through this transaction."

Vis Raghavan, Head of Banking and Executive Vice Chair at Citi, said, "Financing AI demands capital solutions at unprecedented scale. Citi is proud to pioneer innovative structures and leverage our global capital markets structuring and distribution expertise to help accelerate the buildout of critical AI infrastructure that will power the future of technology for years to come."

Jim DeMare, Co-President of Bank of America, said, "Advancing AI responsibly requires turning ambitious technology plans into tangible compute infrastructure. Bank of America's infrastructure financing expertise, advisory capabilities and broad capital solutions platform enable us to deliver innovative structures and mobilize institutional capital at scale. This transaction brings together Broadcom's leading technology and significant bank capital to accelerate the buildout of compute capacity that will power the next wave of AI innovation."

Hock Tan, President and CEO of Broadcom Inc., said, "Today's transaction underscores the power of our advanced technology and our strong conviction in the AI ecosystem. Fundamentally, the need for AI compute continues to grow at an extraordinary pace. This validates that there is capital available to finance such growth and that Broadcom is uniquely positioned to enable it."

Kirkland & Ellis LLP is serving as legal counsel to Blackstone. Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal counsel to Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley. Sullivan & Cromwell LLP is serving as legal counsel to Broadcom, with Evercore serving as financial advisor.
Additional information about the transaction is available on the Investors section of Broadcom's website at https://investors.broadcom.com/.

Applied Materials to Increase its Strategic Investment in BE Semiconductor Industries

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) today announced it is increasing its investment in BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (Besi) (Euronext Amsterdam: BESI), a leading manufacturer of assembly equipment for the semiconductor industry, to approximately 20 percent of Besi’s outstanding shares. The share purchase would add to Applied Materials’ current investment in Besi, which Applied initially made in April 2025.

The companies have a longstanding strategic collaboration, which began in 2020 and was recently expanded with Besi joining Applied Materials’ EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner. The expanded partnership extends the companies’ co-innovation beyond hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures and applications supporting the semiconductor industry’s AI-driven scaling roadmap. Areas of collaboration include next-generation 3D IC scaling, logic and memory integration, scaling of thermo-compression bonding and new die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration platforms.

“Applied Materials is adding to its investment in Besi as hybrid bonding technology and next-generation interconnect architectures become increasingly critical enablers of energy-efficient AI compute performance,” said Dr. Prabu Raja, President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “We also look forward to furthering our strategic collaboration with Besi and delivering the innovative products and technologies our customers need to scale AI systems.”

Applied Materials has entered into an accelerated share purchase agreement for the Besi shares, and the delivery of the shares is subject to the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the HSR Act).

Applied Materials views its investment in Besi as long term. Applied currently has no intention to increase its investment in Besi beyond approximately 20 percent, and Applied does not intend to seek board representation at Besi.

Today, we’re introducing spaces, an interactive way to build a more personalized Muse. A space is a custom experience you create inside Muse by describing your idea, like a holiday gift tracker, a daily word game, or a planning board for your next DIY project. It’s shaped around your routines, goals, and interests, and can be as practical or entertaining as you want. Every space you create becomes part of Muse, so you can keep it where you want and come back to it any time.
From An Idea to Something Real

Have an idea you’ve been meaning to try? Tell Muse about it, and it builds it for you. Your initial idea is just the starting point. As you use your space, you can keep adjusting it with Muse, whether that’s adding what’s missing, trying a new look, or changing how it works.

You can also choose where your spaces live in Muse. Add them to your sidebar, move them into your main tabs, hide the ones you don’t need right now, and schedule when they appear. For example, keep your weekly planner up front during the workweek, then swap it for your weekend plans on Saturday.
Spaces can help you get things done, have a little fun, or give your creative projects a home. Here are a few ideas:
• A shopping hub that brings holiday and birthday gift ideas, wishlists from Instagram saves, and your Marketplace listings and buyer messages into one view
• A school dashboard that finds the events relevant to your kids in school emails and adds them to your calendar
• A music tracker for the artists you love, with new releases and upcoming shows
• A wedding planner with your RSVP list, vendor invoices, and to-dos
• A trivia game that quizzes you on your favorite movies, music, or sports team
• A podcast studio to keep your episode ideas, research, and scripts together
• An order tracker for your small business, with new orders, customer messages and what needs to ship today
• A client hub for your freelance work, with projects, deadlines, and invoices
• A trip planner with your flights, hotel, reservations and a day-by-day itinerary.
Got a half-finished idea sitting in your notes app, a spreadsheet you keep meaning to clean up, or a hobby you want to dive into? Chances are you can turn it into a space.
A Space That Keeps Up With You

Your spaces are personal from the start. Connect the apps you use, and your spaces keep themselves up to date in the background, so new concert dates, price changes, or savings progress show up without you having to ask. You can check things off, add notes, and make edits right in your space, and everything will be there when you return.
Starting today, spaces are available everywhere Muse is available. We’re also exploring ways for you to share your spaces with others to build a more collaborative experience in Muse.
We’re also rolling out specialized versions of our models to Muse, trained with learnings from Muse Wonder, to make your overall experience even better.

At Connect 2026, we previewed real-time conversations with your Muse. Now we’re rolling it out in the Muse app on mobile, web and on Mac — just tap the phone icon in the top-right corner to start talking.
Sometimes it’s easier to think out loud. With voice, you can talk through an idea with your Muse and let it take shape without worrying about the exact prompt.

Planning a trip? Start with the half-baked idea: the city you’ve always wanted to see, the kind of place you’d want to wake up in, the one meal you’d plan the rest of the trip around. Your Muse picks up the thread and works while you talk — on a walk, making dinner, or wherever you are.

Some things are better rehearsed out loud. Prepare for a job interview, run through a presentation, or talk through a pitch — hearing a response and answering in the moment makes it feel more like the real thing.
See Muse Respond in Real Time

As your Muse speaks, the avatar uses subtle expressions and gestures that match the tone of the conversation. It reacts while you talk, so you can tell it’s following along. And you choose how present you want it to be: voice only, the avatar alongside your conversation, or full screen when you want to talk face to face.

Give your Muse a voice with some personality. Want the energy of a New Yorker or the flair of a pirate? With hundreds of voices to choose from, you can pick a style that feels right for your mood and change it whenever you want.

Our Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology lets you have fluid conversations in real time. Speak to your Muse, as you do with real people. Hear responses right away. You can even interrupt if you need to. Wherever the conversation goes, Muse keeps up with you.
Voice and expressive avatars are rolling out now in the Muse app in the US to start. Voice conversations with your Muse are coming soon to AI Glasses and Muse Charm.

Announcement was made in the presence of global and local leadership and reinforces Honda’s confidence in the potential of the Brazilian market
MANAUS, Brazil, November 5, 2026 – Honda today held a ceremony in Manaus, Amazonas state, marking 50 years of motorcycle production in Brazil.

As part of the celebrations for this historic milestone and reaffirming its confidence in the growth potential of the Brazilian market, the company announced a new investment cycle for its motorcycle manufacturing operation in Brazil.

The company will invest BRL 3.3 billion from 2026 to 2030 and expand its annual production capacity to 2.3 million motorcycles by 2029, strengthening the competitiveness of its operations and meeting the growing demand of the Brazilian market. This amount is in addition to the BRL 1.6 billion investment announced last year.

The announcement was made in the presence of Toshihiro Mibe, President, CEO & Representative Director of Honda Motor Co., Ltd.; Keisuke Tsuruzono, President of Honda South America; members of Honda’s global and local leadership teams; and company associates.

The investment comes amid an expanding motorcycle market in Brazil, driven by consumers’ increasing demand for agile, affordable, and efficient mobility solutions. Present in the daily lives of millions of people, Honda motorcycles contribute to income generation, strengthen mobility in both urban and rural areas, expand access to opportunities, and represent independence, leisure, and freedom.
This initiative reinforces Honda’s commitment to the sustainable development of its business and to creating value for customers and business partners.

The Manaus factory, responsible for all Honda motorcycle production in Brazil, plays a central role in the company’s growth story in the country. Over its 50 years of operation, the plant has produced more than 33 million motorcycles, consolidating Honda’s leadership in the segment and its contribution to the development of Brazil’s manufacturing industry.

The investment will enable the construction of two new plants within the manufacturing complex. Each of these new plants will have its own assembly line as well as supporting manufacturing processes. Currently, Honda’s Manaus factory operates four assembly lines distributed across two production plants.
With these investments, installed annual production capacity will reach 2.3 million motorcycles by 2029.
The expansion will also contribute to the region’s economic and social development through the creation of 2,000 new jobs to support increased production.
Under Honda’s global strategy of “producing where there is demand,” the company began manufacturing operations in Brazil in 1976.
Today, the Manaus plant is the most vertically integrated* motorcycle production facility within the Honda Group worldwide, producing approximately 7,200 motorcycles per day.
The facility manufactures 20 models, ranging from 110cc to 1,100cc.
In addition to serving the Brazilian market, the operation exports motorcycles to 19 countries, including the United States, Australia, and Mexico.

Honda employs 9,200 associates directly at the Manaus plant and maintains a state-of-the-art Development and Technology Center responsible for product, process, and manufacturing engineering activities.

The company’s activities also generate positive impacts throughout its value chain. With more than 1,200 dealerships nationwide and over 120 direct suppliers, Honda contributes to economic and social development across different regions of Brazil.

In addition, the company maintains initiatives focused on environmental sustainability, community development, and road safety through investments in industrial eco-efficiency, safety technologies for its products, and rider education programs delivered through Honda Traffic Education Centers (CETH).

Since the beginning of its manufacturing activities in Brazil, Honda has contributed to the sustainable development of the Amazon region. By establishing its factory in the Manaus Free Trade Zone, the company helped drive local industrialization, create qualified jobs, and develop a skilled workforce.
Over the past five decades, Honda has continuously invested in technology, innovation, and professional development, establishing an operation that is recognized globally within the Honda Group.

* A vertically integrated facility is one in which most components of the final product are manufactured in-house. At the Manaus plant, this includes items such as frames, wheels, seats, and engines, ensuring not only vehicle assembly but also the internal production of key components.
Comment from Toshihiro Mibe, President, CEO & Representative Director, Honda Motor Co., Ltd.

“The Manaus factory is one of the core facilities within Honda’s global motorcycle operations, distinguished by its high levels of productivity, quality, and manufacturing efficiency. Reaching this 50-year milestone has only been possible thanks to the tremendous support of our customers and business partners, as well as the dedication and commitment of our associates, to whom I express my sincere gratitude. Honda will continue investing in Brazil’s future, contributing to mobility and economic development in local communities. Building on this strong business foundation and the passion that drives this operation, we will continue advancing Honda’s growth over the next 50 years.”
Comment from Keisuke Tsuruzono, President of Moto Honda da Amazônia Ltda.

“As we celebrate 50 years of motorcycle production in Brazil, I would like to express my gratitude to all those who made this journey possible. The Brazilian market continues to offer significant growth potential. This investment, aimed at expanding the production capacity of the Manaus factory and strengthening its competitiveness, demonstrates our unwavering confidence in the future of Brazil, the Amazon region, and Honda’s business. We will continue striving to provide products and services that exceed our customers’ expectations.”
- Combining Honda’s motorcycle development expertise with the latest e-MTB technology to deliver a new riding experience -

MILAN, Italy, November 3, 2026 - Honda unveiled its first high-end electric-assist mountain bike (e-MTB), the Honda RN0, at EICMA 2026 (Milan Motorcycle Show; Press days: November 3–4; Public days: November 5–8) in Milan, Italy.

Developed jointly with ROTWILD, a German manufacturer of high-end e-MTBs, the Honda RN0 combines Honda’s extensive motorcycle development expertise with the latest e-MTB technologies, which continue to evolve, particularly in Europe.

Weighing approximately 24kg, the lightweight Honda RN0 features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm. By combining a highly stable frame with an electronically controlled electric-assist drive unit, the Honda RN0 delivers the fun of riding expected of a next-generation e-MTB. It also combines high pedaling efficiency with excellent terrain-following performance, delivering outstanding riding performance across a wide range of conditions, from technical trails to long-distance rides.
Key features of the Honda RN0
The concept behind the Honda RN0 is “New Terrain, Same Dream.”
“New Terrain” *1 represents Honda’s first venture into the premium e-MTB market and its entry into a new field.

“Same Dream” expresses Honda’s enduring commitment to expanding people’s possibilities and delivering the joy of riding, the spirit of exploration, and the excitement of taking on new challenges, regardless of changes in product categories or the environments in which its products are used.
Honda began researching and developing mountain bikes in the 2000s, and in 2005, its RN01 won the overall series championship in the UCI*2 Mountain Bike Downhill World Cup.

Although Honda did not subsequently introduce another mountain bike to the market, the passion for mountain biking, which was developed through its research and development activities, has been passed down. The Honda RN0 carries this legacy forward into a new model. Its name embodies two ideas: “Ride Natural,” expressing a sense of connection with nature, and “Reach New Peaks,” representing the pursuit of new heights.

The Honda RN0’s most distinctive features are its proprietary carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm. An efficient structural layout extending from the head tube to the rear axle delivers high rigidity and excellent feedback from the riding surface. This allows riders to intuitively understand terrain conditions and enjoy outstanding stability and control across a variety of surfaces.

The combination of the carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm provides the high rigidity characteristic of motorcycle chassis design, delivering exceptional straight-line stability. At the same time, carefully engineered flexibility allows the frame to deform slightly, improving tire contact with the ground during cornering.

The Honda RN0 is available in three frame sizes—S, M, and L—to accommodate riders of different builds. The geometry of each size incorporates ROTWILD’s extensive mountain bike development expertise and is optimized for the wide range of riding conditions encountered in all-mountain riding, from steep climbs to descents.

The rear suspension uses a single-pivot swingarm with a linkage system. This configuration minimizes unwanted suspension movement during pedaling while allowing the suspension to respond smoothly to impacts from the terrain, achieving an effective balance between pedaling efficiency and shock absorption.

The frame features a two-tone color scheme combining Pearl Moon Ash Gray and Mat Ballistic Black Metallic. The premium finish gives the Honda RN0 a distinctive presence, even against the backdrop of natural outdoor environments.
The Honda RN0 is equipped with industry-leading components.
The front suspension features a FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima fork with 160mm of travel, while the rear suspension uses a FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima shock.

The front and rear wheels are DT Swiss H1900 SPLINE units designed specifically for e-MTBs. A mullet configuration*3, combining a 29-inch front wheel with a 27.5-inch rear wheel, delivers an outstanding balance of stability and agility.
Schwalbe Albert EVO Trail tires and SHIMANO DEORE XT four-piston disc brakes provide excellent grip and braking performance across a wide range of terrain conditions.

The Honda RN0 features a new SHIMANO drive unit. Despite weighing just 2.3kg, the lightweight unit delivers a maximum torque of 100Nm and maximum output of 750W, supported by a 720Wh battery. It provides powerful assistance across a broad range of riding conditions, from steep climbs to high-speed trails.
The AUTO ASSIST function automatically adjusts the level of assistance according to the gradient of the terrain and the rider’s pedaling effort.
The AUTO SHIFT function automatically changes gears to maintain an optimal cadence,*4 allowing riders to concentrate on the trail ahead.

In addition, the Assist Carryover function smoothly maintains drive power for a short period after the rider stops pedaling, helping the motorcycle maintain momentum when negotiating obstacles and other challenging terrain.

A 2.2-inch full-color display is integrated into the top tube, providing clear information on speed, remaining range, assist mode, and other riding data. The system also supports device charging through a USB-C port. Integration with the SHIMANO app allows riders to customize the SHIMANO drive unit’s settings and lock or unlock the bike’s electronic systems.

Since its founding, Honda has supported people’s mobility and their pursuit of new challenges through a wide range of products and technologies, including the Honda A-Type, which combined a bicycle with an auxiliary engine, the Honda Racoon series of electric-assist bicycles, and the RN01 mountain bike developed exclusively for downhill racing.
The Honda RN0 represents a new challenge that builds on this history.

Honda aims to achieve carbon neutrality across all products and corporate activities in which it is involved by 2050 and is advancing electrification in its motorcycle business. Going forward, Honda will continue to deliver the joy and freedom of mobility to more people through products that meet increasingly diverse customer needs, while contributing to the realization of a carbon-neutral society.
*1 “Terrain” refers to a field or area of activity.
*2 UCI: Union Cycliste Internationale (International Cycling Union).
*3 A bicycle configuration that uses different wheel sizes at the front and rear.
*4 The number of pedal revolutions per minute.

DOHA, Qatar, November 3, 2026 — Passenger traffic in the Middle East is forecast to grow 4.3% annually despite current industry headwinds, supporting trade, tourism and commerce across the region over the next 20 years, according to Boeing’s [NYSE: BA] 2026 Commercial Market Outlook. The region’s airplane fleet is projected to double to more than 3,500 airplanes to support twice the travel demand, underscoring the aviation sector’s continued resilience.

Airlines in the Middle East are expected to take delivery of nearly 3,000 new airplanes over the next two decades to support fleet expansion and replace older airplanes. Around 85% of the Middle East fleet in 2045 will consist of modern, fuel-efficient airplanes delivered over the next 20 years.

“The Middle East has long established itself as one of the world’s most important aviation crossroads, connecting people and economies throughout Asia, Africa and Europe,” said Shahab Matin, Boeing managing director of Commercial Marketing, Middle East and Africa. “The region’s airlines have proven to be resilient and continue to adapt as conditions evolve. Carriers have ambitious long-term growth plans supported by strong demand fundamentals, modern fleets and continued investment in aviation infrastructure.”

The Middle East’s share of global passenger traffic is double the region’s share of the world’s population, reflecting the scale of Middle East carriers’ long-haul networks. The Middle East region is forecast to see nearly 6% growth on major Asia routes over the next two decades and triple the 2025 volumes by 2045.

Widebody airplanes remain central to region’s growth Boeing forecasts demand for 1,370 new widebody airplanes in the Middle East, representing nearly half of the region’s new airplane deliveries through 2045. This share of widebody jet deliveries is the highest of any region and more than double the global average.

The region will also require 1,505 single-aisle airplanes to support short- and medium-haul network growth. Single-aisle airplanes will continue to support year-round point-to-point service and strengthen domestic and intra-regional connectivity. As Middle East economies diversify and tourism grows, demand for more frequent and flexible travel options is expected to support continued growth for low-cost carriers and single-aisle operators.

STRATFORD, Conn., Nov. 6, 2026 – Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company (NYSE: LMT), has been selected to deliver the S-92A+™ helicopter, the next-generation variant of its S-92® helicopter, to the Republic of Korea Air Force (ROKAF) for its Presidential Helicopter II program.

Lockheed Martin and Sikorsky's partnership with the Republic of Korea spans more than 70 years, including Black Hawk, Seahawk and S-92 helicopter programs. Since taking delivery of three S-92 helicopters in 2007, the ROKAF has relied on the platform for nearly two decades of safe and reliable presidential transport. S-92 helicopters have also supported Korea Coast Guard search and rescue operations, along with firefighting and other lifesaving missions for South Korea's National 119 Rescue Headquarters, part of the country's National Fire Agency.

For the new presidential fleet, Korea Aviation Engineering & Maintenance Service (KAEMS), a subsidiary of Korea Aerospace Industries, will perform in-country mission equipment completion for the S-92A+ helicopters. The contract also includes additional special mission equipment and sustainment support, including critical spare parts and field service representation.

“We are deeply honored that the S-92A+ has been selected as the Republic of Korea’s presidential helicopter. Building on the Republic of Korea Air Force’s long-term experience operating the S-92A, we are confident the S-92A+ will continue supporting this critical mission with the highest standards of safety and reliability,” said Wonik Lee, South Korea country executive for Lockheed Martin. “The S-92 platform’s shared heritage in presidential transport across the Republic of Korea, the United States and other nations makes this selection especially meaningful. Together with Korean aerospace partner KAEMS’ participation in the program, this milestone reflects Lockheed Martin’s longstanding commitment to the ROK-U.S. alliance, national defense and defense industry cooperation.”

For head-of-state and VIP transport, the S-92 combines best-in-class safety and reliability with long-range, all-weather capability and a spacious, quiet cabin tailored for executive travel. The S-92A+ builds on these proven strengths with upgraded engines, a new Phase IV main gearbox and increased payload or fuel capacity to enhance performance and mission flexibility.

With more than 2.6 million fleet flight hours, an average lifetime availability rate of over 90% and more than 300 aircraft delivered across 28 countries, the S-92 supports head-of-state and VIP transport, offshore energy and search and rescue missions. The platform also serves as the foundation for the U.S. Marine Corps' VH-92A Patriot® presidential helicopter, continuing Sikorsky's legacy of transporting every U.S. president since 1957.

Sikorsky is ramping up S-92A+ production at its facilities in Stratford, Connecticut, and Owego, New York, with capacity to produce up to 12 aircraft annually. These efforts reflect Sikorsky's continued commitment to modernizing the S-92 platform and supporting its global customer fleet today and into the future.

• New flagship global early-career program combines engineering, AI and real-world energy challenges
• Inaugural cohort of 50 will complete two six-month rotations, supported by learning, mentoring and customer exposure

Schneider Electric, a global energy technology leader, today launched Energy Tech Accelerator, a 12-month global early-career program that will recruit an inaugural cohort of 50 participants across five global hubs, Boston, Paris and Grenoble, Dubai, Bangalore, and Shanghai, to work at the intersection of artificial intelligence, engineering and sustainable energy. Participants will work on meaningful business and customer challenges while gaining dedicated learning, mentoring, customer exposure and opportunities to build a connected global community.

“At Schneider, our goal is to Advance Energy Tech to the next level to deliver greater business outcomes for our customers. By leveraging Data & AI, we connect the physical and digital worlds to deliver Energy & Industrial Intelligence to our Customers,” said Olivier Blum, chief executive officer of Schneider Electric. “Turning that intelligence into solutions that help our customers operate more efficiently and sustainably requires people who can combine deep knowledge of energy and industrial processes with AI. That is why we are launching Energy Tech Accelerator: to attract and develop people who understand AI, are passionate about the energy transition and want to make a tangible contribution to a more sustainable future.”

Energy Tech Accelerator is part of Schneider Electric’s investment in the workforce capabilities needed as energy systems become more digital and connected. The program gives emerging talent responsibility and practical experience from the start.

“Advancing energy technology is ultimately about people,” said Charise Le, chief human resources officer of Schneider Electric. “Early-career talent should not have to wait years to make a meaningful contribution. Through Energy Tech Accelerator, participants will learn across the business, take on real challenges and build the capabilities and confidence to help shape a more sustainable energy future.”

The program is designed for curious, analytical and globally minded early-career engineers who are excited by AI, digital technology and sustainable transformation. Applications open Nov. 2. Candidates can learn more and apply at Energy Tech Accelerator Graduate Program.

• Built using the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, the Immersive Twin pilot connects Schneider Electric, AVEVA, and ETAP technology in one digital platform
• Digital twin connects AI workload requirements with power, cooling, electrical, and operational models to accelerate AI Factory deployment and improve token efficiency
• Pilot at Start Campus’ Sines data center campus is expected to optimize operations for Nscale

Global energy technology leader Schneider Electric, industrial software leader AVEVA, full-stack AI cloud platform Nscale, and data center developer and operator Start Campus, today announced the successful pilot of an end-to-end digital twin developed using the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, part of NVIDIA DSX Sim.

The Immersive Twin pilot marks a significant step toward bringing Schneider Electric’s digital twin technology, powered by AVEVA software, into real-world AI infrastructure, allowing Nscale to accelerate token production and optimize token efficiency.

The deployment is focused on Nscale’s operations within the SIN01 data center on the 1.2 GW SINES Data Campus in Portugal, developed by Start Campus. As one of Europe’s largest and most sustainable AI factories, the SINES Data Campus is designed to support successive generations of AI infrastructure. It will soon become home to more than 66,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, representing one of the largest AI deployments in the region. By combining engineering and operational data with advanced power and cooling simulations and workload requirements, the new Schneider Electric and AVEVA Immersive Twin provides a unified view of data center performance to help identify opportunities to optimize infrastructure before changes are implemented on-site.

Using the digital twin, Nscale expects to achieve faster time to token, greater token efficiency, enhanced operations, increased flexibility, and reduced risk when updating or modifying its technology stack.

"Working with Start Campus, Schneider Electric and NVIDIA, we’re using digital twins to model how AI data centers operate in the real world — from power and cooling to token delivery,” said David Power, Chief Technology Officer at Nscale. “This gives us a clearer view of where full-stack optimizations can be realized before changes are made on the ground. It’s about using intelligence and simulation to build and operate AI infrastructure more efficiently, and sustainably at scale.”

The successful pilot reflects the strength of a collaborative, end-to-end approach, bringing together complementary expertise from across the AI ecosystem, including energy management, engineering, simulation and AI infrastructure operations to create a more complete view of data center performance.

The Immersive Twin pilot supports the full lifecycle of AI factories—from design through operations—by building an OpenUSD-based digital twin that connects Schneider Electric, ETAP, AVEVA, and third-party technologies. It enables rapid “what-if” scenario testing across power, cooling, and process behavior to validate design decisions, assess upgrade impacts, reduce procurement risk, and continuously optimize performance by linking IT and OT data. In parallel, it advances interoperability through simulation-ready asset files, accelerating seamless integration into digital twins.

Start Campus provides the real-world infrastructure, engineering expertise and operational environment to demonstrate how digital twin technology can transform the design, development and operation of AI data centers. Bringing this data, technology and expertise together enables Nscale to use the digital twin to model and test “what-if scenarios” for new configurations or technologies before implementation, speeding up deployment times while significantly reducing risk.

“Building a credible, end-to-end digital twin requires collaboration across the AI ecosystem,” said Pankaj Sharma, Executive Vice President, Software & Service with Schneider Electric. “By advancing energy tech, and connecting Nscale’s workload and IT infrastructure requirements with Start Campus’s physical facility and infrastructure data, while pairing it with Schneider’s digital twin technology, we’re bringing together critical perspectives needed to model AI factories more holistically and identify opportunities to optimize performance, efficiency and token production.”

"AI infrastructure needs to evolve as quickly as the technology it supports,” added Robert Dunn, Chief Executive Officer at Start Campus. “Our collaboration with Schneider Electric, Nscale and NVIDIA has taught us that operators and customers design, develop and operate data centers best when they work from the same model. By using digital twin technology to simulate how a jump in rack density moves through the power train and the liquid cooling loop before it becomes a physical reality, we can test new hardware generations, agree the configuration with our customer and build it once. That accelerates deployment, improves efficiency and maximizes the value of every megawatt. This is an important step towards delivering resilient AI infrastructure at scale."

This latest pilot expands Schneider Electric, AVEVA and ETAP’s work with NVIDIA. Last year, the three companies joined the Alliance for OpenUSD (AOUSD) to accelerate digital twin and AI factory development through the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint.

Additionally, the companies continue to collaborate on reference architectures, integrated infrastructure and software solutions that will power and cool the next generation of AI factories, and use NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to simulate and improve energy efficiency in real-world environments.

NEW DELHI (6 November 2026) – GE Vernova (NYSE: GEV) today announced it has been officially chosen by PowerGrid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) to deliver a critical 6 GW High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission corridor. The project was booked in the fourth quarter of 2026.
This project will serve as a vital energy highway, enabling the efficient transport of 6 GW of power from the renewable energy-rich region of Barmer, Rajasthan, to the load center in South Kalamb.

By connecting remote renewable energy zones to the national network, this 800 kV project aims to provide the infrastructure needed to stabilize power flow for millions of homes and businesses. As India’s electricity demand continues to grow, this high-capacity link is essential to ensuring that the country’s grid remains reliable and resilient while supporting its decarbonization goals.

“India is at the forefront of the global energy transition, characterized by an unprecedented scale of renewable integration and rapidly evolving grid requirements,” said Philippe Piron, President and CEO of GE Vernova’s Electrification Segment. “This project represents more than just transmission capacity; it is an investment in the reliability and future-proofing of India’s power system. We are proud to work with PGCIL to deploy the advanced technology required to bridge the gap between renewable energy production and national consumption, ensuring long-term system performance.”

"As India accelerates its renewable energy journey, the development of robust, high-capacity transmission infrastructure is paramount,” said Sandeep Zanzaria, CEO & Managing Director at GE Vernova, T&D India. “The Barmer–South Kalamb HVDC corridor is a strategic project for PGCIL, designed to efficiently integrate large-scale renewable capacity from Rajasthan into the national grid. By leveraging advanced transmission technologies, we are strengthening the backbone of India’s power system, ensuring reliable, high-quality electricity reaches consumers across the country while supporting our national commitment to a sustainable and resilient energy future."

GE Vernova will deliver the complete design for the ±800 kV, 6,000 MW (2x3000 MW) bipolar HVDC link between Barmer II and South Kalamb. The project scope encompasses the creation of new converter stations, the supply of all major equipment, and the full management of site erection, testing, and commissioning. By overseeing the end-to-end delivery of this link, GE Vernova ensures a synchronized approach that prioritizes grid stability and system efficiency, suitable for large scale renewable energy links such as Barmer.

The project will feature GE Vernova’s most advanced LCC (Line Commutated Converter) valve, which will be manufactured at the Pallavaram factory in India. It will also include the eLumina™ control system which provides the digital intelligence required to manage complex power flows, enabling the grid to respond dynamically to changing conditions.
This collaboration further strengthens GE Vernova’s long-standing relationship with PGCIL, reinforcing a shared vision of a modernized, resilient, and decarbonized power grid for the future.

Event marks the start of a three-year initiative to inspire the next generation of energy leaders in the Upstate

GREENVILLE, S.C. – November 2, 2026 – The GE Vernova Foundation today celebrated the official launch of Engineers of Change in Greenville, with the first students beginning programming this fall. The launch event brought together GE Vernova leadership, local government officials, Clemson University partners, and community leaders to highlight the program’s role in creating a pipeline for future innovators who will build a more sustainable energy future.

First announced in April 2026, Engineers of Change is a three-year, $4.5 million initiative in two locations – Greenville, South Carolina and Staffordshire, UK. In Greenville alone, the program aims to reach 3,000 students. By bringing engineering to life through hands-on learning, real-world design challenges, and direct mentorship from industry professionals, the program aims to ignite curiosity and confidence in students ages 13–18.

“Meeting the world’s growing energy needs will require not only breakthrough technology, but people — bold thinkers, problem-solvers, and next-generation leaders,” said Kristin Carvell, President, GE Vernova Foundation and Chief Communications Officer, GE Vernova. “Our goal with Engineers of Change is to teach young people in Greenville more about this exciting career path and the purpose and impact that comes along with it and inspire them to pursue a career in engineering.”
The launch event at the Advanced Manufacturing Works (AMW) facility featured a panel discussion with industry experts and educators, as well as live engineering demonstrations.
The program focuses on two core components:
• Engineering Spark: Introduces students ages 13–14 to foundational engineering concepts through dynamic, hands-on learning.

• Engineering Catalyst: An immersive, two-year program for students ages 15–18 featuring design challenges and career readiness workshops designed to equip students with the skills to pursue engineering.

“The GE Vernova Foundation has been a dedicated partner in expanding opportunity and connecting education to the workforce needs of our communities,” said Ben Ayers, President of Clemson University. “Engineers of Change puts that partnership into action by giving young people in the Upstate hands-on experiences, mentorship and a clear view of the opportunities available to them in engineering and energy. We are grateful for the GE Vernova Foundation’s continued investment and, as the program’s first university partner in the United States, proud that Clemson is helping prepare the next generation of innovators and problem-solvers.”

Engineers of Change is delivered in collaboration with Clemson University’s PEER program and the global nonprofit FHI 360, ensuring that programming is aligned with local workforce needs. Through this collaboration, the GE Vernova Foundation continues to put its purpose, The Energy to Change the World, into practice.

“We are proud to see Engineers of Change take root here in Greenville,” said Mayor Knox White. “This partnership creates a unique pathway for our students, providing them with the practical skills and encouragement to pursue engineering as a mission-driven career that can change the world.”

GE Vernova and the GE Vernova Foundation continue to invest heavily in the future of Greenville, driving impact through both education and community-building. Since 2021, the company and the Foundation have together granted nearly 300 scholarships—including the John Lammas Annual Scholarship for engineering students and GE Vernova STAR Scholarships supporting employees' children—while also funding skilled trades and technical programs, such as granting $100,000 for Future of Energy Skills scholarships in Greenville.

Additionally, the 2026 opening of the GE Vernova Park in Greenville marked a major milestone in creating vibrant, connected communities. Serving as the home pitch for Greenville Triumph SC and Greenville Liberty SC, the venue welcomed over 45,000 fans in its inaugural season while doubling as a year-round hub for soccer clinics, yoga, and World Cup watch parties. Through shared volunteer efforts like Hands On Greenville Day and programs like the Triumph's "Read to Score" initiative—which rewarded 2,703 students for literacy—GE Vernova is proud to invest in the social, physical, and educational well-being of the Upstate region.

At Cloudflare Connect, Mastercard is showing how Agent Pay for Machines helps AI agents pay for digital services while keeping people and businesses in control.

AI agents are becoming more capable, reliable and able to work with one another. Increasingly, they also need to pay for things. An agent might buy data from one provider, use an AI model from another and pay for computing power from a third. In other words, AI agents are becoming economic actors.
But how does an agent actually pay?

Paid digital services today typically require an account, API key, prepaid credits or billing relationship with each provider. That works when an agent uses one or two services. It becomes harder when the agent needs to choose different services as a task unfolds, paying only for what it uses along the way.
Then there’s trust. Who gave the agent permission to spend? How much can it spend? What can it spend that money on? And who is it paying?

Those questions need to be answered instantly, at machine speed. That's why we built Agent Pay for Machines. It builds on x402, an open protocol that lets digital services request payment online, and connects it with the trust, security and reach of the Mastercard network.

Today at Cloudflare Connect, Mastercard is showing how Agent Pay for Machines allows AI agents to securely purchase digital services on behalf of businesses while staying within approved budgets and permissions.

Following end-to-end pilots with Cloudflare, Ant International, AIsa, Base, BVNK, Coinbase and Hype, we’re also opening Agent Pay for Machines Early Access, giving developers access to the APIs, tools and documentation needed to begin building and testing agent-to-agent commerce experiences.
Payments aren't the hard part. Authority is. The challenge is making sure the right agent can complete the right transaction with the right permissions.
Authorize once. Transact many times. Guarantee payment now. Settle later.

The idea is simple. A business gives an agent a job and a spending limit. When the agent encounters a paid service, the service responds with “402 Payment Required,” the internet's way of saying that payment is needed to continue.
The agent creates a digitally signed payment voucher, which is a secure promise to pay within its approved limit. The provider verifies it, delivers the service and the work continues.

These interactions happen off-chain at machine speed. Providers can combine vouchers and redeem them later. Agents keep working and paying for what they need without unlimited spending authority or a new billing relationship for every service.
Giving agents a trusted way to transact
At Cloudflare Connect, we're bringing this to life with Hype, a marketing agency that already uses AI agents in its campaign work.
Please accept functional cookies to watch this video.

In the pilot demo, Hype gives an AI agent a task and a defined budget: Plan a sample campaign for a protein bar launch. Running on an agent platform such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, the agent discovers registered Agent Pay for Machines providers and returns with a two-step plan: Conduct social media research from AIsa and create campaign images through Cloudflare AI Gateway.

Hype approves the funding, limiting the agent to the defined task and budget. Then the agent gets to work. When payment is needed, the service responds with “402 Payment Required” through Cloudflare Monetization Gateway. The agent signs a voucher, the seller verifies it and the work continues.
First comes the research from AIsa. Then come eight campaign images from Cloudflare.
Nine payments. Two independent merchants. One approved budget. No separate accounts, API keys or invoices. The agent pays only for what it uses while Hype stays in control.

Behind the scenes, Coinbase Developer Platform provides the wallet infrastructure used to fund the agent, while Base provides the on-chain settlement network. BVNK then acts as the agent wallet, using Mastercard Global Money Platform to handle the payment and settlement on both sides, in fiat or stablecoins. Sellers can then get paid in their preferred currency, token or rail.
This same model can support AI models, data, computing power, APIs and other digital services.
Start building for an open agent economy

Agent Pay for Machines is designed to work across the ecosystem. Agent platforms run agents, wallets and payment providers supply funds, and merchants offer services. Mastercard connects them through a common layer of trust.
Through Agent Pay for Machines Early Access, we’re making the first version of our buyer- and seller-side APIs available to developers, along with a toolkit, sandbox and developer documentation.

This is just the start. Our roadmap will be shaped by what customers and partners need. We want developers to test Agent Pay for Machines, try different use cases and tell us what would make it more useful.
Whether you’re building agents, platforms, payment infrastructure or services for agents, we want to build with you.

The web gave software a way to communicate. APIs gave software a way to use services. Now AI agents need a way to pay for them. That’s what we’re building. Together, we can make the agentic economy open, interoperable and trusted from the start.
What is Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines?

Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines helps AI agents pay for digital services on behalf of businesses within approved budgets and permissions. It builds on x402, an open protocol for requesting payments online, with Mastercard providing a common layer of trust across participants.
How does Agent Pay for Machines work?

A business gives an AI agent a task and a spending limit. When payment is required, the agent creates a digitally signed payment voucher within that limit. The provider verifies the voucher before delivering the service. Vouchers can be combined and redeemed later.
How does Mastercard help businesses stay in control of AI agent payments?

Businesses set the task, permissions and spending limit for the AI agent. Agent Pay for Machines allows the agent to transact within those defined parameters rather than giving it unlimited spending authority.
What can AI agents pay for with Agent Pay for Machines?

AI agents can use Agent Pay for Machines to pay for digital services such as AI models, data, computing power and APIs. In the pilot, an agent pays for social media research and AI-generated campaign images within one approved budget.
How can developers access Agent Pay for Machines?
Developers can access the first version of our buyer- and seller-side APIs through Agent Pay for Machines Early Access, along with the toolkit, sandbox and developer documentation.

NEW YORK, NY – October 22, 2026 – Goldman Sachs today announced the launch of the Goldman Sachs Small Business AI Institute, a significant extension of its signature 10,000 Small Businesses program aimed at supporting AI adoption and application. The Institute is partnering with the world’s leading AI companies – Anthropic, Google, Meta and OpenAI – to provide entrepreneurs across America with the training and tools they need to integrate AI into their operations and grow and scale their businesses.

The Institute is part of a new $500 million commitment the firm is making to fund the next chapter of 10,000 Small Businesses and deliver education, access to capital and support services to another 10,000 businesses. Since its launch in 2010, nearly 20,000 entrepreneurs across all 50 states and four U.S. territories have completed the program. Graduates add jobs four times faster than similarly-sized U.S. businesses and together represent more than $32 billion in annual revenue and over 350,000 jobs.

"Goldman Sachs has invested in small businesses for more than 15 years, because that is where job creation happens," said David Solomon, Chairman and CEO of Goldman Sachs. "Every major technology shift has rewarded the businesses that adapt most quickly. This commitment makes sure the entrepreneurs who are creating America's jobs can lead in the AI economy."

The Institute will focus on three key pillars: delivering high-quality AI education to small business owners across the country, publishing research on AI use by small businesses and supporting AI-enabled expansions to access to capital for small businesses.

As part of its initial activities, the Institute will develop a new learning series with Anthropic on applied AI for small businesses, hands-on workshops for Goldman Sachs’ 10,000 Small Businesses alumni and research collaborations on small business AI use. In addition, the Institute will work with Google to deliver its Grow with Google AI Professional certificate to almost 20,000 small business owners and their employees, including three months of no-cost access to Google AI Pro. Meta will collaborate with the Institute to help support entrepreneurs with AI tools and training for their businesses through Muse for Small Business. The Institute is also partnering with OpenAI to deliver tailored AI workshops across the country with 10,000 Small Businesses community college partners.

“We believe AI will create the greatest boom in entrepreneurship and small businesses that the world has ever seen. This is an incredible moment for anyone with an idea for a new endeavor because the gap between imagining it and bringing it to life is getting much smaller. We're excited to work with Goldman Sachs to help more entrepreneurs build and grow with ChatGPT,” said Sam Altman, Co-founder and CEO of OpenAI.

“Small businesses make up a significant share of the American economy, but they have never had the resources of bigger companies. AI is the first technology that can finally close that gap, and Anthropic is committed to making sure those gains reach startups and family businesses, not just large enterprises. We're glad to work with Goldman Sachs to help these small business owners rely on Claude to improve how work gets done and even build AI into their product offerings," said Daniela Amodei, Co-founder and President of Anthropic.

"Small businesses are the economic engine and heart of communities, and new technologies give them a powerful way to accelerate growth, profitability and hiring,” said Ruth Porat, President and Chief Investment Officer of Alphabet and Google. “By partnering with Goldman Sachs and the Small Business AI Institute, we are putting practical tools and training directly into the hands of nearly 20,000 entrepreneurs—helping them build for their future."

“Muse for Small Business has affirmed our longstanding belief in the importance of small businesses to both Meta and the economy. Small business owners are entrepreneurs, job creators and revenue drivers and we are proud to empower over 200 million of them on our platforms. We're excited to join Goldman Sachs' Small Business AI Institute to continue to bring the benefits of super intelligence to small business owners,” said Dina Powell McCormick, President and Vice Chairman of Meta.

According to a survey released today of over 2,400 10,000 Small Businesses graduates, 86 percent reported using AI in their business – a dramatic increase from 56 percent in 2024. However, only 15 percent said that AI is fully integrated into their core operations. More than three-quarters of graduates said they could use additional training and resources.

“The AI economy is a small business economy,” said Asahi Pompey, Global Head of Corporate Engagement at Goldman Sachs. “We want to enable AI adoption by delivering support that is practical, accessible and immediate."
For more information on the Goldman Sachs Small Business AI Institute, visit gs.com/SBAI.

Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses is a $1.25 billion commitment to help entrepreneurs create jobs and economic opportunity by providing a comprehensive business education program and access to capital and business support services. Since its launch over 15 years ago, 10,000 Small Businesses has served nearly 20,000 small businesses across the United States. The program has reached businesses from all 50 states, Puerto Rico, and Washington, D.C. Learn more at www.gs.com/10ksb.

New Brunswick, N.J., November 9, 2026 – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) today announced promising first-in-human Phase 1 results for the investigational combination of pasritamig and JNJ-9401, two bispecific antibodies designed to work together to drive the body’s immune response against advanced prostate cancer. At the recommended regimen, 73 percent (11 of 15 patients) achieved reductions of at least 50 percent in prostate-specific antigen (PSA), a marker used to monitor prostate cancer activity, including 47 percent (7 of 15 patients) who achieved reductions of at least 90 percent. Results were presented in a late-breaking oral session at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC) 2026 Annual Meeting (Abstract #1175).1

The combination represents the first dual-tumor-antigen-targeted bispecific antibody regimen clinically evaluated in prostate cancer, targeting kallikrein-related peptidase 2 (KLK2) and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) through complementary T-cell signals designed to activate and enhance the function of immune cells against cancer. In the study, deep and sustained PSA responses were observed, with all seven patients who achieved reductions of at least 90 percent remaining on treatment for more than six months without disease progression. No Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events were reported in this early analysis.1
A first-of-its-kind approach: targeting two prostate cancer proteins with complementary T-cell signals

For patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), treatment remains challenging as the disease progresses and available options become more limited.2 Median overall survival is approximately two to three years, highlighting the need for continued innovation.3,4 While immunotherapies have transformed the treatment of some cancers, their role in prostate cancer has historically been limited, and immune checkpoint inhibitors have shown minimal clinical benefit.5

Bispecific antibodies are designed to help the immune system recognize and attack cancer by activating T cells, a process that can be enhanced by generating two complementary signals.6,7 Pasritamig, a first-in-class bispecific antibody targeting KLK2, has demonstrated single-agent antitumor activity,8 and is designed to provide the first signal by directing T cells toward prostate cancer cells. JNJ-9401, a novel bispecific antibody targeting PSMA, provides a second signal designed to strengthen and sustain T cell activity.
Expert and company perspectives on the potential of this dual-antigen targeted bispecific regimen

“Prostate cancer has long been difficult to treat with immunotherapy, which makes the activity we’re seeing particularly interesting,” said Laura Graham, M.D.,* Assistant Professor of Medicine-Medical Oncology at the University of Colorado School of Medicine. “By combining two complementary approaches to T-cell activation, we are exploring a new way to engage the immune system against this disease. The depth of PSA reductions observed in this study, including responses sustained for six months or longer, provides encouraging early evidence for the pasritamig-JNJ-9401 combination that warrants further investigation in a larger Phase 3 study.”

“This novel dual-antigen-targeted bispecific regimen combines pasritamig, a foundational component of our prostate cancer pipeline, with JNJ-9401, highlighting the potential of complementary mechanisms working together,” said Yusri Elsayed, M.D., M.H.Sc., Ph.D., Global Therapeutic Area Head, Oncology, Johnson & Johnson. “With this combination now in Phase 3 development, we are building on the early promise of this approach as we work to bring new treatment options to patients with advanced disease.”
Early results show promising deep and sustained PSA reductions

The ongoing, open-label, multicenter Phase 1 study is evaluating the safety and preliminary clinical activity of pasritamig in combination with JNJ-9401 in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), also known as metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant prostate cancer (mAPMR).1

These preliminary findings are based on a small number of patients at the recommended regimen, and further evaluation is needed to determine the clinical benefit and safety of the combination in a larger population.1

As of June 15, 2026, 144 patients had enrolled in the study. Patients treated at the recommended regimen were heavily pretreated, having received a median of four prior lines of systemic therapy (range, two to six). Among the 15 patients treated at this regimen, 73 percent achieved PSA reductions of at least 50 percent and 47 percent achieved reductions of at least 90 percent. Four patients achieved undetectable PSA levels. All seven patients who achieved PSA reductions of at least 90 percent remained on treatment for more than six months without disease progression.1

At the recommended regimen, no Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events, dose-limiting toxicities, or treatment-related adverse events leading to discontinuation or death were reported. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS), an inflammatory reaction that can occur when T cells are activated, was observed in three patients (20 percent). All cases were mild (Grade 1), presenting as temporary fever, and none required treatment with tocilizumab. No cases of immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) were reported.1

The recommended regimen consists of JNJ-9401 200 mg administered subcutaneously every six weeks in combination with pasritamig 300 mg administered intravenously every six weeks, following two initial weekly pasritamig step-up doses. The findings suggest the combination has potential to be administered on this schedule in an outpatient setting.1
Advancing a new generation of immunotherapy combinations into Phase 3

The combination is being evaluated in the ongoing Phase 3 KLK2-comPAS (NCT07164443) study, which is investigating whether adding JNJ-9401 to pasritamig can improve outcomes for patients with mCRPC.[9] The study represents an important next step in Johnson & Johnson’s broader development program for pasritamig, which is being evaluated both as a single agent and in combination with other therapies across advanced prostate cancer.

About the studyThe Phase 1 study (NCT06095089) is an open-label, multicenter trial evaluating the safety and clinical activity of pasritamig in combination with JNJ-9401 in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) who have received at least one prior systemic therapy. In Part 1, JNJ-9401 was dose escalated in combination with fixed-dose pasritamig, with primary objectives of evaluating safety and determining the recommended regimen. Dose expansion was initiated at the recommended regimen, including a frontline mCRPC cohort. The recommended regimen is JNJ-9401 200 mg administered subcutaneously every six weeks in combination with pasritamig 300 mg administered intravenously every six weeks, following two weekly pasritamig step-up doses. Treatment is administered in an outpatient setting.10

About pasritamig and JNJ-9401Pasritamig and JNJ-9401 are investigational bispecific antibodies designed to work together to activate and enhance the immune response against prostate cancer. Pasritamig, a first-in-class KLK2xCD3 bispecific antibody, is designed to direct T cells to prostate cancer cells, while JNJ-9401, a PSMAxCD28 costimulatory bispecific antibody, is designed to provide an additional signal that enhances T-cell activation and function. By targeting two different prostate cancer proteins, KLK2 and PSMA, the combination is designed to deliver complementary signals to T cells.

Pasritamig is being studied as a monotherapy and in combination with other therapies across advanced prostate cancer. Pasritamig with or without JNJ-9401 is being evaluated in the Phase 3 KLK2-comPAS study in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and pasritamig plus docetaxel is being evaluated in the Phase 3 KLK2-PASenger study in first-line mCRPC.

About metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC)Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), also known as metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant prostate cancer (mAPMR), is an advanced form of prostate cancer that continues to progress despite treatments that target the androgen receptor pathway.2 As the disease progresses, it can spread to other parts of the body, including the bones and lymph nodes, and patients may receive additional treatments such as chemotherapy and radioligand therapy targeting prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA).11

Patients with metastatic prostate cancer that has become resistant to androgen pathway modulation face poor outcomes, with survival varying based on factors including the location and extent of disease, prior treatment history and response to therapy. Median overall survival ranges from approximately 13.5 to 31.6 months depending on the site of metastasis.3,4
