Choosing the right TV is a long-term decision that involves several factors — including screen size, picture quality, brightness, viewing environment, and preferred content.

Advances in TV technology have expanded the options available, from OLED, QLED, and Neo QLED to the latest Micro RGB. AI capabilities now go beyond picture and sound optimization to support content discovery, device connectivity, and personalized viewing experiences. As a result, consumers are asking more specific questions about screen size, AI features, and their viewing needs rather than simply “Which TV is the best?”
Samsung Newsroom outlines key criteria and answers common questions about buying a TV.
How To Choose the Right TV Size

When choosing a TV size, viewing distance and available space are key considerations. For comfortable, immersive viewing, the recommended distance is approximately 1.2 times the screen size in centimeters, based on a 40-degree field of view.1
For typical living room seating arrangements, recommended screen sizes vary by viewing distance:
• 3.0 meters or more: 85-inch or larger TVs
These are general guidelines, as comfortable viewing distances may vary depending on viewing habits — such as watching content with subtitles or as a family.
Larger screens enhance immersion but may cause eye strain if too large for the space. Samsung offers TVs ranging from 32 to 114 inches to accommodate different spaces and viewing preferences.

Viewing times and lighting conditions vary from home to home, making the viewing environment an important consideration when choosing a TV. In bright spaces, screen brightness and reflection reduction are key, while contrast ratio matters more in darker settings.
For sunlit living rooms, Neo QLED TVs provide high brightness for clear viewing. OLED TVs, meanwhile, deliver exceptional contrast — making them well suited to darker spaces.

However, advances in display technology are making lighting conditions less of a constraint. OLED TVs with Glare Free technology minimize reflections, maintaining a clear picture even in brightly lit rooms.2

AI Gamma technology analyzes scene brightness in real time and automatically adjusts gamma levels based on ambient lighting. It brightens dark scenes to preserve detail in well-lit rooms and reduces glare while enhancing contrast in darker settings. These adjustments help minimize eye strain without compromising picture clarity.
How Samsung TV Display Technologies Compare
Display technologies produce light and color differently, each offering advantages depending on viewing conditions and intended use:
• OLED: Relies on self-emissive pixels rather than a backlight to deliver near-perfect blacks and fast response times.
• Mini LED: Employs smaller LEDs than conventional backlights to produce strong contrast, particularly for HDR content.
• Neo QLED: Combines Quantum Matrix Technology for precise Quantum Mini LED backlight control with Quantum Dot technology that accurately reproduces 2,140 Pantone colors and 110 skin tones.
• Micro RGB: Features individually controlled, microscopic red, green, and blue (RGB) backlights for a wide color gamut and precise color reproduction.

OLED TVs excel at reproducing deep blacks, making them ideal for movies and TV shows in dark rooms. In brighter spaces, TVs with advanced backlight control have an advantage. Mini LED TVs provide strong contrast at an affordable price, while premium Neo QLED TVs combine rich colors from Samsung’s proprietary quantum dot film with powerful AI upscaling. For vivid, accurate colors and lifelike picture quality faithful to the original content, Micro RGB TVs are another option.
Different types of content call for different TV features:
• Movies: High Dynamic Range (HDR) brings out subtle details and colors in both bright and dark scenes, creating greater depth and realism.

• Live Sports: AI-powered features enhance the viewing experience through real-time picture and sound adjustments. AI Soccer Mode Pro, AI Motion Enhancer, and AI Sound Controller Pro work together to deliver clearer action and more immersive stadium sound.

• Video Games: High refresh rates ensure smooth motion, while low input lag enables faster responses to player commands. AI Gaming Optimizer automatically adjusts picture and sound settings based on the game genre.

• Art: Samsung’s Art TV lineup, including The Frame and The Frame Pro, displays renowned artworks when not in use — transforming living spaces into galleries. Customizable bezels, the One Connect Box, and Wireless One Connect create a picture frame-like appearance, while Samsung Art Store provides access to more than 5,000 artworks through a subscription.
Unlike conventional TVs, Samsung AI TVs automatically optimize picture and sound while supporting content discovery and information searches.
• AI Upscaling Pro: Enhances older or lower-resolution content for sharper visuals on high-resolution screens and more immersive sound.
• AI Soccer Mode Pro: Adjusts picture and sound to recreate the atmosphere of live soccer matches.
• AI Gaming Optimizer: Recognizes game genres and tailors picture and sound settings accordingly.
• Vision AI Companion: Connects with AI services to help viewers search for information and discover related content on-screen.

When choosing a TV, consumers should look for AI features that match their viewing habits — from automatic picture and sound optimization for sports, movies, and games to on-screen information searches.
TV Buying Guide at a Glance
Q. What TV size is ideal for a living room?

For viewing distances of 2.3 meters or more, a 75-inch or larger TV is recommended. With 4K resolution now widespread, larger screens maintain sharp picture quality even at closer distances. However, sufficient installation space and viewing distance remain important.
Q. What TV size is ideal for a bedroom?

Bedrooms typically have shorter viewing distances and limited space, making 42- to 50-inch TVs generally suitable. The ideal size depends on the distance from the bed to the screen, as well as the TV’s overall dimensions including the stand and bezel.
Q. Should consumers choose a 65- or 75-inch TV?
The recommended viewing distance is approximately 2.0 meters for a 65-inch TV and 2.3 meters for a 75-inch model. If possible, compare both sizes from the intended viewing distances before deciding.
Q. Can lower-resolution content still look sharp on a 4K TV?
Yes. AI Upscaling enhances lower-resolution content to match 4K displays for sharper viewing. Results may vary by model and source material.
Q. Do OLED TVs reduce glare?

OLED TVs combine exceptional contrast with Glare Free technology to minimize reflections. The 2025 Samsung S95F OLED TV features a low-reflection layer that diffuses external light while preserving contrast and color, even in bright rooms.
Q. Should consumers choose QLED or Neo QLED TVs?

Neo QLED TVs provide high brightness and precise contrast, while QLED TVs deliver vivid colors at a more affordable price. Both use Quantum Dot technology, but Neo QLED TVs feature smaller Mini LED backlights for more precise backlight control.
Q. What is the difference between HDR and non-HDR TVs?
HDR TVs reproduce a wider range of brightness and preserve details in highlights and shadows, creating greater depth and realism.
Q. Can I use a Samsung Smart TV without a subscription?
Yes. Samsung Smart TVs offer features and free content without a paid subscription. Models supporting Samsung TV Plus provide free channels featuring news, entertainment, dramas, and movies.3
Samsung Art Store allows users to select artworks and the monthly curated Art Store Streams collection for free. A subscription unlocks access to the full collection of more than 5,000 artworks.4
Q. Which is better for gaming, OLED or Neo QLED TVs?

OLED TVs deliver fast response times and near-perfect blacks, while Neo QLED TVs provide high brightness and strong HDR performance. Both offer high refresh rates, low input lag, and Game Modes, making room lighting and preferred game genres important considerations.
Q. How can theater-quality sound be achieved with a Samsung TV?
Q-Symphony enables compatible Samsung TVs and sound devices to play audio together, delivering optimized surround sound based on room layout and device placement.

Seoul, August 7, 2026 – SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com) announced today that it has decided to build new fabs in Yongin and Cheongju to respond to the continuously growing demand for memory in the AI era.
The company approved a total investment of approximately 54 trillion, 35.2 trillion won in Yongin “Y2” fab and 19.1 trillion won in the Cheongju “M17” fab, in a board meeting.

This decision represents execution of the mid-to-long-term investment strategy announced by the company last June. Under its master plan to invest 600 trillion won in the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster and 100 trillion won to expand its Cheongju production base, SK hynix is currently constructing its first fab in Yongin (Y1). With this latest decision, the company is embarking on the construction of subsequent fabs in both Yongin and Cheongju.

According to market research firm Omdia, both DRAM and NAND demand are projected to maintain a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 19% from last year through 2030. The company views this growth not as a temporary supercycle, but as a structural transformation in which memory transcends its role as a mere component to become core infrastructure determining AI performance itself.

SK hynix stated that in the AI era, technological competitiveness alone is not enough and the ability to supply the required volume at the exact moment customers need it is the ultimate competitive advantage. We reached this investment decision after a thorough review of market demand.

Yongin Y2 is the second of four fabs planned sequentially for the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster. It will serve as a DRAM production base spanning a total floor area of 341,000 pyeong (approximately 1,130,000m²). Construction is scheduled to break ground in July next year, targeting the opening of its first cleanroom in June 2029 to produce high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and other next-generation DRAM products. Meanwhile, construction on Y1 is progressing smoothly toward its initial cleanroom opening target of February next year.

SK hynix previously set a goal to advance the completion date of the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster by 12 years—from the originally planned 2045 to 2033—to finish constructing all four fabs. The Y2 construction serves as the second phase supporting this accelerated timeline and the investment spans to October 2031 sequentially.

The investment amount includes construction costs for “Business Support Building” with administrative and welfare facilities for Y2 personnel, an “Integrated R&D Center” to consolidate product development testing, analysis, and experiments, as well as auxiliary infrastructure*.

For the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster—sprawling over approximately 1.26 million pyeong(approximately 4,160,000m²) in Wonsam-myeon, Cheoin-gu, Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do—Phase 1 power and water infrastructure required up through Y2 operation is nearing completion, currently at a 99% progress rate. As fab construction and infrastructure setup have been carried out concurrently, the company plans to proceed with the Y2 construction according to schedule.

In the NAND market, demand is surging rapidly centered on enterprise SSDs driven by the full-scale expansion of AI services. This is further boosted by demand for key-value (KV) cache* storage in AI inference, with application fields expected to broaden further as Agentic and Physical AI are introduced.

SK hynix selected Cheongju as its new NAND fab base because it offers the fastest fab construction timeline. The Cheongju Campus already houses the M11, M12, and M15 fabs, enabling efficient production linked to existing operations on sites equipped with substantial pre-established power and water infrastructure. Cheongju M17 will be built across a total area of 206,000 pyeong(approximately 680,000m²), breaking ground in February next year with plans to open its first cleanroom in December 2028. The investment period runs through April 2031 according to the master plan.

SK hynix plans to proactively secure production infrastructure based on mid-to-long-term demand discussed with customers, while expanding actual production capacity in alignment with the timing of customer needs. Fabs will be constructed according to the master schedule, whereas cleanroom expansions and equipment installation will take place sequentially in line with demand trends to maximize capital efficiency.

The company expects this investment to secure future growth foundations while strengthening the competitiveness of the domestic semiconductor ecosystem and boosting local economies. The large-scale simultaneous investments in Yongin and Cheongju are anticipated to expand joint growth opportunities for supply chain partners, generate employment, and revitalize local commercial districts, thereby contributing to the sustainable growth of the national economy.

An SK hynix official stated that “This investment is a decision made to seize opportunities in line with the market’s growth speed. By proactively securing production capabilities, we aim to establish ourselves as a key partner in AI infrastructure, contributing to the stability of the global AI semiconductor supply chain.”

Seoul, August 4, 2026 – SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com) announced today in collaboration with Sandisk that it has unveiled the first standard specifications for High Bandwidth Flash (HBF), a next-generation storage technology.

The announcement coincides with the opening of ‘FMS (Future of Memory and Storage) 2026,’ held at the Santa Clara Convention Center in California from August 4 to 6 (local time). The company is set to present HBF as a key technology to overcome memory bottlenecks in the AI era through keynote speeches and panel discussions during the event.

HBF technology is a new memory layer between HBM and SSDs. It enables high-speed data transfer similar to HBM while significantly expanding capacity by leveraging NAND technology. With the expansion of AI inference driving a surge in data volumes to process, HBF is gaining attention as a technology that simultaneously resolves bandwidth and capacity scalability challenges.

This milestone comes about six months after launching the consortium in February this year, following the initial standardization partnership with Sandisk in August 2025. Capacity specifications cover up to 512GB based on two stack configurations (8-high and 16-high NAND dies). Bandwidth is categorized into three grades (Grade1~3), delivering scalable performance from approximately 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s.

A key highlight is the interconnect linking HBF technology and processors. HBF technology adopts UCIe*, an industry standard connection interface, laying the groundwork to flexibly integrate HBF technology across different processor types, including GPUs and CPUs.
The standard also outlines ▲connection interfaces and electrical characteristics, ▲reliability and packaging guidelines for HBF die stack process, ▲software I/O guidelines.

The specification was disclosed through the Open Compute Project (OCP), world’s largest open data center technology initiative, positioning it as an open standard for the entire industry rather than a proprietary technology.

SK hynix plans to leverage this release to expand the adoption of HBF technology in the AI storage market and foster the surrounding ecosystem. With Google and Tenstorrent currently participating in the HBF consortium, the consortium aims to expand its reach while enhancing technical maturity and market acceptance based on open collaboration.

On the opening day of FMS 2026 (August 4, local time), SK hynix Executive Vice President Kim Chun-sung (Head of Solution Development) and Vice President Kang Uk-song (Head of Next Generation Product Planning) will deliver a joint keynote address, titled ‘Orchestrating Efficient AI Infrastructure through Tiered Memory in the Era of Agentic AI.’

As Agentic AI* rapidly commercializes, the volume of data to process is surging alongside growing demands for higher speed and efficiency. Recognizing that a single memory type cannot address these complex challenges, both speakers will present the necessity and future direction of a next-generation architecture based on ‘Tiered Memory’ a framework that connects and optimizes diverse memory types into a unified system.

On August 6, SK hynix Vice President Lim Eui-cheol (Head of Solution AT), Sandisk Vice President Rajeev Nagabhirava and Google DeepMind Senior Staff Engineer Xiaoyu Ma will join a panel discussion titled ‘Breaking the Memory Wall with High Bandwidth Flash.’ Bringing together key leaders across memory, storage and AI, the session will examine fundamental shifts in memory architecture across AI infrastructure and highlight the potential and role of HBF as a transformative solution.
Furthermore, SK hynix will host an exhibition booth throughout FMS 2026, featuring a Partnership Zone, a Next-Generation Tech Zone and Tech Sessions.

Notably, the company will publicly reveal for the first time its tenth-generation (V10) 375-layer 4D NAND wafer and products, which are currently under development. The 375-layer 4D NAND improves performance per watt by 2.5 times compared to the previous generation, making it optimized for AI infrastructure environments like data centers that demand high power efficiency and performance. The company plans to initiate mass production of high-performance, high capacity eSSDs based on the 375-layer 4D NAND early next year to reinforce its leadership in the AI NAND market.

SK hynix will also display a versatile product lineup spanning mobile, PC, automotive and robotics, showcasing the company’s competitive edge in memory technology and its collaborative achievements with customers in the AI era.

“With the rapid spread of AI applications, we are at a point where overall data processing structures must be redesigned,” said SK hynix Executive Vice President and Head of Solution Development Kim Chun-sung, adding, “Through HBF, SK hynix will expand the boundaries between memory and storage and contribute to building new architectures that enhance overall system efficiency.”
